The Grey Banks.name: The Grey Banks
The Grey Banks.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Cloud fills the upper part of the frame in flat grey banks, and beneath it the water runs pale, turquoise where the light gets into it and laced with foam where the swell tips over. The horizon is soft rather than sharp, the two greys running together. Swell comes through in short crowded ranks that tip and slide rather than crash, and the foam they leave hangs a moment before the next rank rolls it under. Fliers crossing keep below the cloud base to hold a visible surface underneath them, and take the wet buffeting air that comes with it. Light travels only a little way into water this pale before it scatters and comes back as milk.
The Grey Banks.hiddenInfo: Open water with no landing under The Grey Banks: a flier who loses a heading here has only the sun to correct it. Wildlife under the surface is possible and rarely seen; bandits do not work water this open.

The Green Shallows.name: The Green Shallows
The Green Shallows.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Pale green-blue water with white threading through it, the swell short and irregular rather than running in ordered ranks. Light passes into the pale water far enough to come back green rather than blue, and the returned colour is strongest in the flanks of the swell where the crests thin. A thin overcast sits high enough to leave the surface bright. Wind is slight and comes from a single quarter without varying, which the overcast above carries no sign of. There is nothing on the water to steer by, so a crossing here is flown on heading and elapsed time, and the colour of the sea is the only thing that changes from one span to the next.
The Green Shallows.hiddenInfo: Nothing marks The Green Shallows but swell; the crossing is made on held height and remembered bearing. Ships bound for the Orbital Gate Station pass far above; nothing else uses this sky.

The Deepening Blue.name: The Deepening Blue
The Deepening Blue.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Blue deepens abruptly across this water, the pale inshore colour giving way to a flat strong ocean tone that holds the same shade to every edge of the frame. Swells run long and low and break only at their tops. The water takes light in rather than scattering it, so what returns is colour alone with almost nothing of the sky in it. Above, the air is dry and the horizon stands as a hard ruled edge with no haze softening it. Sun comes off the surface hard with no cloud to cut it, and a flier gains height less for the view than to get above the glare lifting off the water.
The Deepening Blue.hiddenInfo: The Deepening Blue offers no rock, no bar and no rest, and the light off it is the main hazard by midday. A downed traveller is a rescue only if someone saw them go down.

The Driven Ranks.name: The Driven Ranks
The Driven Ranks.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Swells move in a single direction across the whole of this sea, long ridges of dark blue with shallow troughs between them, and the wind that drives them is steady enough to be read off the surface alone. Foam appears only where two lines cross. Between the ridges the troughs hold a colder shade where the sky cannot reach them, and light dies out of the water within the first lift of a wave face. Crews flying it hold a constant altitude, because there is nothing below to judge height against but the swell itself. Cloud is absent and the horizon runs clean all the way round, offering no feature to hold a bearing on.
The Driven Ranks.hiddenInfo: The colour of The Driven Ranks says nothing about what lies beneath, and nothing here will catch a tired flier. Weather arrives from the open quarter with little warning and no shelter.

The Light Track.name: The Light Track
The Light Track.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Light lies on the water in a long broken track that shifts as the flier moves, and either side of it the blue is clean and unvaried. The track widens and narrows as the surface tilts, and where it passes the blue shows a paler core before closing again. The swell is gentle, the surface almost unruffled between crests. Air over it is warm and rising in patches, giving small lifts and drops that are felt rather than seen, and the crossing is steady work rather than difficult work. Sky above is almost bare, a faint high veil that softens nothing and shades nothing.
The Light Track.hiddenInfo: Over The Light Track the wind is the only fixed thing, and it changes. Nothing here needs story evidence except the weather.

The Saturated Blue.name: The Saturated Blue
The Saturated Blue.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Water fills the frame corner to corner with no edge of land anywhere in it, a bright saturated blue that goes slightly greener where the swell faces the sun. The surface is working but not rough. Colour holds to the edges without a rim of paler water anywhere, which is the surest sign that no ground lies under any part of it. The swell runs from one quarter while a weaker cross-set works against it, so crests rise unevenly and collapse without carrying. This is the middle of a span rather than either end of one, and the only measure of progress is time in the air and whatever heading was set at the coast.
The Saturated Blue.hiddenInfo: The Saturated Blue is transit air over deep water, crossed rather than visited. Distance is the danger; the sea itself is indifferent.

Cloud-Streak Water.name: Cloud-Streak Water
Cloud-Streak Water.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Thin streaks of high cloud cross an otherwise clear sky, throwing faint moving shadows onto blue water that is uniform beneath them. The shadows slide across the water faster than the swell moves beneath them, and where they pass the blue drops a shade and recovers. The swell is long and slow and slides under itself without breaking. Wind is light. High cloud is drawn out into parallel fibres all running the same way, which is the only indication of wind at that level. Fliers here have no reason to descend and several to stay up, since height buys time to react if the weather ahead thickens.
Cloud-Streak Water.hiddenInfo: Open water with no landing under Cloud-Streak Water: a flier who loses a heading here has only the sun to correct it. Ships bound for the Orbital Gate Station pass far above; nothing else uses this sky.

The Empty Blue.name: The Empty Blue
The Empty Blue.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Nothing interrupts the surface in any direction: no rock, no bar, no change of colour that would mark shallower ground. The blue is even and strong, the swell regular, the light flat and high. Light goes into the water cleanly and comes back from well below the surface, giving the blue a depth of tone that has nothing to do with texture. Crossings are made without reference to anything below, and a flier who loses a heading has no means of recovering it from what is in sight. The sky is clear to every quarter and the horizon holds a sharp circle with no thickening anywhere on it.
The Empty Blue.hiddenInfo: Nothing marks The Empty Blue but swell; the crossing is made on held height and remembered bearing. A downed traveller is a rescue only if someone saw them go down.

Violet Troughs.name: Violet Troughs
Violet Troughs.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Long ranks of swell run beneath, blue-black in their troughs and bright along their faces, close enough in spacing that the pattern reads as a moving grain rather than as separate waves. Between the ranks the water shows almost violet where the shadow of the wave ahead falls on the face behind it. Air is clear and the visibility good. Cloud is absent and the horizon keeps its line, though it gives no more information than the water does. Wind sits off to one side of the flying line, so a crossing here holds a small constant correction the whole way across.
Violet Troughs.hiddenInfo: Violet Troughs offers no rock, no bar and no rest, and the light off it is the main hazard by midday. Weather arrives from the open quarter with little warning and no shelter.

The Painted Blue.name: The Painted Blue
The Painted Blue.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Open sea entirely, without cloud, coast or surface mark, painted the same deep bright blue from one edge of the cell to the other. Swell is low and so evenly spaced it looks worked rather than natural. The surface returns a hard even light along the crests and lets the troughs go dark, so the pattern reads as bands rather than as water. Heat off the surface builds through the middle of the day and makes the air over it unsteady, which is felt as slow lift and sink rather than as turbulence. No cloud stands anywhere over it and the horizon stays clean, thin and unhelpful.
The Painted Blue.hiddenInfo: The colour of The Painted Blue says nothing about what lies beneath, and nothing here will catch a tired flier. Nothing here needs story evidence except the weather.

Glare Water.name: Glare Water
Glare Water.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Glare is the main difficulty here: a cloudless sky over unbroken blue throws light back up hard enough that the horizon washes out toward the sun side. The swell beneath is low and even. Light goes deep into the blue away from the sun side and comes back as a dense even colour, while toward the sun it returns as sheet-white. The air is dry and holds no haze, which sharpens everything except the one quarter that matters. Fliers turn the crossing so the worst of it sits behind a shoulder where they can, and take their heading from instrument rather than from a horizon they cannot trust.
Glare Water.hiddenInfo: Over Glare Water the wind is the only fixed thing, and it changes. Distance is the danger; the sea itself is indifferent.

High Air Above Peaks.name: High Air Above Peaks
High Air Above Peaks.basicInfo: [Transit · High] High air with nothing under it but more air, the blue thinning toward the top of the frame and hazing along its lower edge. The ridges of the Silver Peaks stand off to the south, snow showing on their upper faces. Light arrives without obstruction and carries no warmth with it, so anything facing the sun heats while everything in shadow stays bitter. Cloud is scarce and what there is lies well below. The haze along the lower edge is not weather but distance, piled up until the far ground loses its colour and keeps only its shape. Fliers at this level work in cold moving air and do not stay in it longer than a crossing requires.
High Air Above Peaks.hiddenInfo: Thin cold air over High Air Above Peaks, with bare rock and old snow beneath and no footing that could be called a landing. Exposure is the hazard; nothing here ambushes anyone who is not already lost.

Cold Summit Sky.name: Cold Summit Sky
Cold Summit Sky.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Cold clear sky, empty of cloud, with the light coming in at an angle that picks out every edge of the massif standing below and southward. The blue overhead darkens rather than pales toward the top of the frame, taking on the density that only height gives it. Snow on the Silver Peaks reads as hard white against grey rock. Air at this height is thin enough that flight is steady but effortful, and there is no shelter in any direction from a wind that does not stop. Wind runs level and unbroken with no ground near enough to deflect it, and it brings no cloud with it. Part of Vexorath.
Cold Summit Sky.hiddenInfo: Cold Summit Sky is the built edge of Vexorath: the same fabric as the city, thinner, and no authored location stands on it. Approach lanes are marked in cobalt; off them is rock and air.

Vexorath High Air.name: Vexorath High Air
Vexorath High Air.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Above and west of the Vexorath massif the air stands open and hard blue, with the summit itself breaking into frame on the eastern side as bare rock and permanent snow. Cloud collects against the upper slopes and tears away downwind in ragged streamers. The streamers pull out into thin fibres and vanish where the air dries again, re-forming closer to the rock a moment later. Above them the sky is uniform and hard, darkening toward the top of the frame and giving no cue of movement. Wind accelerates around the mountain rather than over it, so anything holding this line meets it from the flank. Part of Vexorath.
Vexorath High Air.hiddenInfo: Nothing on Vexorath High Air is a destination; travel here arrives at the nearest named site of Vexorath. Approach lanes are marked in cobalt; off them is rock and air.

The Pinnacle.name: The Pinnacle
The Pinnacle.basicInfo: [Lv 11-23 · High] Thin air and open sky take almost the whole of this ground. The massif's bare summit stands at the lower edge of it, and the light of the surface-to-orbit link rises off the peak in a single vertical line bright enough to be the first thing seen from any direction. Lumina Reach holds that summit ground, white frame and charcoal recess worked tight against the rock. Cloud passes below the highest structures. What surface exists runs to bare grey stone and narrow cobalt-marked decking, cold and scoured clean, with wind against the structure the only thing to hear. Part of Vexorath.
The Pinnacle.hiddenInfo: Lumina Reach is neither closed nor public: access follows legitimate purpose and operational responsibility rather than surname or standing, being Contair bypasses nothing, curiosity creates no access, and House Dravon's permanent denial remains controlling. Authorised visits and docking decisions sit with Solanis Contair or with station systems under him and do not routinely climb to Rezulith. The Orbital Defense Ring, the Command Gallery, the Deep-Space Sensor Hall and the Emergency Isolation Sector stay restricted absent a justified purpose. Known Space routes remain deliberately undeveloped, and that is the problem on Solanis's console: he has found a deep-space traffic pattern that does not match known routes, it has repeated, and the station is the one place on Nexara where an arrival is an event with a border behind it. The next pass of the pattern is predicted.

Cloud-Bank Air.name: Cloud-Bank Air
Cloud-Bank Air.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Banks of torn cloud drift through otherwise clear high air, catching on the flank of Vexorath to the west and shredding out behind it. The blue here is sky, not sea. Between the banks the air is glass-clear and the rock beyond them shows every fracture and ledge. Light is strong and arrives without softening at this level. Cold comes with that clarity and does not lift through the day at this level. Anything flying through is either crossing the shoulder of the mountain deliberately or being pushed sideways by the air coming off it. Part of Vexorath.
Cloud-Bank Air.hiddenInfo: Cloud-Bank Air carries Vexorath's ordinary life outward without any place of its own. Approach lanes are marked in cobalt; off them is rock and air.

Broken Cloud Heights.name: Broken Cloud Heights
Broken Cloud Heights.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Broken cloud fills much of the frame, pale and flat-bottomed, with gaps showing blue above and the grey-white of the Silver Peaks below to the south. The flat bottoms mark a single level where the rising air gives out, so everything above that line is bright and everything below it grey. The air is damp inside the cloud and clear between. Fliers pick their way through the gaps rather than committing to the murk, because what lies beneath is rock and snow and gives no warning of itself through vapour. Light comes through the gaps in shafts that travel across the snow beneath.
Broken Cloud Heights.hiddenInfo: Broken Cloud Heights is high ground and higher air; weather crosses it in bands and visibility swings from clean to nothing. A flier who drops into cloud here has rock in every direction.

Clear High Air.name: Clear High Air
Clear High Air.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Almost cloudless high air, the blue deep and even, with only a faint haze where the sky meets the distant white of the Silver Peaks southward. Nothing occupies this level but weather. Height changes nothing about the view, since the only thing to see is the white ridge line and it comes no closer for climbing. Wind is consistent in direction and strong, and a flier crossing with it makes easy time while one crossing against it spends the whole span working for it. A thin band of colder blue lies along the top of the frame where the atmosphere runs out of substance.
Clear High Air.hiddenInfo: Nothing lives at Clear High Air but wind; the rock is too steep and too broken to walk. Vexorath's approach lanes are marked; everything off them is not.

The Pale Shore Water.name: The Pale Shore Water
The Pale Shore Water.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Sky takes the upper part of this frame in soft layered cloud, and below the horizon the water runs pale and green-tinged, breaking into foam wherever the swell steepens. The join between the two is indistinct in this light. The swell comes through in short sets with slack water between them, and the foam left behind slides down the backs of the crests before dispersing. Crossings are flown low enough to keep the sea in sight, since the horizon cannot be trusted as a reference when it blurs like this. Light under this cloud is even and shadowless, and the pale water gives back most of what reaches it without letting any of it down.
The Pale Shore Water.hiddenInfo: The Pale Shore Water is transit air over deep water, crossed rather than visited. Wildlife under the surface is possible and rarely seen; bandits do not work water this open.

Clean Eastern Deeps.name: Clean Eastern Deeps
Clean Eastern Deeps.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Deep clean blue to every edge, the swell arriving from one quarter in long unbroken lines with no cross-sea working against it. Sunlight sits high and the water returns a hard even sheen. Light enters cleanly and is lost somewhere well below without returning, which is what gives the colour its weight. No coast shows in any direction. The sky holds no cloud at any level and the horizon closes as a hard unbroken ring. A flier out here keeps something in hand for the return, because the air looks the same whichever way it is turned and none of it leads anywhere closer.
Clean Eastern Deeps.hiddenInfo: Open water with no landing under Clean Eastern Deeps: a flier who loses a heading here has only the sun to correct it. A downed traveller is a rescue only if someone saw them go down.

Overcast Reach.name: Overcast Reach
Overcast Reach.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Heavy cloud takes most of this frame, a thick pale overcast that drops the light and flattens the sea beneath it to a dull grey-blue. What water is visible is restless, foam showing where the wind catches the tops. The sea takes almost no colour from a sky that has none to give, and what light gets into it dies within the first turn of a wave. Visibility shortens under the cloud base. The cloud base is ragged rather than flat, hanging in low tufts that pass close overhead. Fliers either drop beneath it and accept the buffeting or climb through and lose sight of the surface entirely.
Overcast Reach.hiddenInfo: Nothing marks Overcast Reach but swell; the crossing is made on held height and remembered bearing. Weather arrives from the open quarter with little warning and no shelter.

Turquoise Patches.name: Turquoise Patches
Turquoise Patches.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Turquoise shows through the surface in broad soft patches where the light reaches into it, and between them the water runs a heavier blue. Where the sun falls through a gap the turquoise brightens and its edges sharpen, and where a cloud passes the whole patch closes to the darker tone. Cloud occupies the top of the frame in loose separated masses with clear sky behind. The swell is moderate and comes in from the open side. Light reaches further into this water than into the open sea beyond, far enough that the colour returns warm rather than cold. Crossing here is straightforward in fair weather and a matter of reading the cloud line when it is not.
Turquoise Patches.hiddenInfo: Turquoise Patches offers no rock, no bar and no rest, and the light off it is the main hazard by midday. Nothing here needs story evidence except the weather.

Foam-Laced Shallows.name: Foam-Laced Shallows
Foam-Laced Shallows.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Foam laces the water in long torn lines, the swell steep enough to break at its crests and pale enough underneath to show green where it thins. Crests collapse forward instead of rolling, throwing their water ahead of them and leaving a pale stain that the following crest crosses. Above the horizon the sky carries scattered cloud with clear gaps between. Wind comes across rather than along the swell, which leaves the surface confused. The horizon is visible but broken by the swell itself, rising and dropping as the nearer water lifts. Fliers hold height through it and do not try to read a heading off the wave pattern.
Foam-Laced Shallows.hiddenInfo: The colour of Foam-Laced Shallows says nothing about what lies beneath, and nothing here will catch a tired flier. Distance is the danger; the sea itself is indifferent.

Two-Tone Water.name: Two-Tone Water
Two-Tone Water.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Two colours of water share this frame: a pale worked turquoise where the swell breaks and a darker steadier blue in the troughs between. The pale worked water carries light a short way and returns it green, while the darker troughs swallow it entirely. Cloud lies along the horizon in a low continuous band that thins with height. The air is moving and damp. Under the band the horizon is a soft join with no clean line anywhere along it. A crossing made early is generally calmer than one made later, when the surface roughens and the cloud builds upward.
Two-Tone Water.hiddenInfo: Over Two-Tone Water the wind is the only fixed thing, and it changes. Wildlife under the surface is possible and rarely seen; bandits do not work water this open.

The Brightening Sea.name: The Brightening Sea
The Brightening Sea.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Bright open water with only a light scatter of cloud above it, the swell running long and the crests catching sun along their upper edges. Colour deepens steadily toward the outer side of the frame as the shallower tone falls away behind. The catch of sun runs along the upper edges as a moving thread and goes out as each crest passes its peak. Nothing marks the surface. Light carries well down into the blue here and comes back cold, which is what makes the deepening read as a change of water rather than of weather. Fliers use the set of the swell as a rough check on the wind and their instruments for everything else.
The Brightening Sea.hiddenInfo: The Brightening Sea is transit air over deep water, crossed rather than visited. Ships bound for the Orbital Gate Station pass far above; nothing else uses this sky.

The Wind Ranks.name: The Wind Ranks
The Wind Ranks.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Wind is the dominant fact here, steady and single in direction, pushing the whole surface into ordered ranks that show white only at their tops. The blue beneath is strong and clean. The ranks stand at a slight angle to the line of travel, each presenting a long sloped face and a short steep back. High cloud is sparse enough to leave the light unfiltered. Where the tops go white the foam is torn away at once rather than left to lie. A flier working into this wind loses ground across the span, and one running with it arrives early and overheated.
The Wind Ranks.hiddenInfo: Open water with no landing under The Wind Ranks: a flier who loses a heading here has only the sun to correct it. Weather arrives from the open quarter with little warning and no shelter.

Horizon Band.name: Horizon Band
Horizon Band.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Toward the upper edge of the frame the sea gives way to a soft band of cloud sitting on the horizon, and below it the water is a clean mid-blue moving in unhurried swells. The band sits low enough that the water beneath it darkens while the nearer sea stays lit. Light is diffuse rather than harsh. There is no land in the cell and no surface mark of any kind, so fliers treat it as open ground to be covered and keep whatever height the air allows. Swell faces show a paler blue than the troughs, though the difference is slight and never sharpens.
Horizon Band.hiddenInfo: Nothing marks Horizon Band but swell; the crossing is made on held height and remembered bearing. Nothing here needs story evidence except the weather.

Wind-Ruffled Calm.name: Wind-Ruffled Calm
Wind-Ruffled Calm.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Flat strong blue with a low swell that barely lifts, the surface just ruffled enough by wind to kill any true reflection. The sky above carries almost no cloud. The ruffling is fine and even, a grain laid over the whole frame that does not change from one part of it to another. Heat rises off the water through the day and makes the lower air unsteady. Colour comes from within the water rather than off it, deep and slightly cold in tone. Crossings here are easy in the sense that nothing interferes, and hard in the sense that nothing helps either.
Wind-Ruffled Calm.hiddenInfo: Wind-Ruffled Calm offers no rock, no bar and no rest, and the light off it is the main hazard by midday. Distance is the danger; the sea itself is indifferent.

The Glittering Chop.name: The Glittering Chop
The Glittering Chop.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Ruffled blue water in every part of the frame, worked into small irregular facets by a wind with no single direction to it. Each facet holds a fragment of sky for an instant and loses it, so the whole surface glitters without any part of it staying bright. Larger swell runs underneath the chop but is difficult to pick out from height. Cloud is minimal and the light even. The light that gets into the water returns quickly and from no great way down, which keeps the blue bright and shallow-looking. Fliers crossing hold a set heading and make no corrections off the surface, which reads differently from one moment to the next.
The Glittering Chop.hiddenInfo: The colour of The Glittering Chop says nothing about what lies beneath, and nothing here will catch a tired flier. Wildlife under the surface is possible and rarely seen; bandits do not work water this open.

The Paling Water.name: The Paling Water
The Paling Water.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Southward the water begins to pale toward the bright shallow tone of the Radiant Strait, while in this frame it still holds the deeper open blue of the outer sea. The change of tone along the southern edge is gradual, a lightening through several shades rather than a boundary. Swell is low and regular and the wind light. Cloud amounts to a few scattered pieces. Light reaches well into the deeper water without finding anything to return from, while over the paler ground southward it comes back sooner and brighter. This is the approach rather than the crossing proper, and fliers bound for the strait pick up their line somewhere in it.
The Paling Water.hiddenInfo: Over The Paling Water the wind is the only fixed thing, and it changes. Ships bound for the Orbital Gate Station pass far above; nothing else uses this sky.

Peaks Approach Water.name: Peaks Approach Water
Peaks Approach Water.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Ahead to the south and east the grey of the Silver Peaks stands up at the edge of the water, and everything else in frame is blue sea running in even low swells. Grey rock stands hard against the water with no softening of tone between the two. The light is clean and the cloud slight. Air changes where the sea meets the rising ground, and fliers approaching the peaks gain height out here rather than trying to climb close in. The swells run in without shortening, since nothing shallow lies under this part of the frame.
Peaks Approach Water.hiddenInfo: Peaks Approach Water is transit air over deep water, crossed rather than visited. A downed traveller is a rescue only if someone saw them go down.

Summit Country.name: Summit Country
Summit Country.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Cloud drifts through the upper air in flat torn sheets, lit hard from above so their tops glare while their undersides stay grey. The massif stands below and to the east, where worked stone marks Summit Countrywest against the bare ground. Air in this band runs smooth and very cold, and fliers hold it deliberately, dropping out of it only once the ridge below is in clear sight. The torn sheets pass through the band fast enough that a gap held one moment is closed the next, and a flier committed to one has to be through it before it goes. Below the cloud the rock keeps its snow in the lines the light never reaches.
Summit Country.hiddenInfo: Updraughts along Summit Country are strong enough to matter and nowhere near reliable. The cold arrives with the shadow and leaves with it.

The Outer Shell.name: The Outer Shell
The Outer Shell.basicInfo: [Lv 4-10 · Moderate] Structure thins to almost nothing along this edge. The upper works of the Fabrication Yards and the pale flank of the Chronicle Hall hold the inner side, and past them the rock simply ends in air. The Outer Shell shows its layering there — old breach repairs left standing as ribs of newer material over older, none of it disguised. The decking underfoot is curved plate with drainage channels cut across it, gritty with dust lifted off the bare rock. Landing ledges are cut narrow and marked in cobalt. Walkers keep to the inner side where there is handrail; fliers come in along the face rather than over the rim. Part of Vexorath.
The Outer Shell.hiddenInfo: An old Shell layer has activated for a threat category nobody now remembers creating, and Vexorath is not a constant battlefield, so the alarm is the story: a false classification, hidden damage, a forgotten system or old embedded technology carries the same weight as an invasion would. The repair crawl network is the natural place to find something where nothing should be, and whether it is human-accessible, drone-only or mixed is deliberately unstated. Final authority sits with Rezulith. The Dravon Attack Archive is embedded in the structure that absorbed the assaults and is distinct from Chronicle Hall's Restricted Dravon Archive, and the Chronicle's entry for the city's first recorded assault reads simply as not named. The woken layer is holding its state, and the crawl-network survey Rezulith ordered has a completion date the layer may not wait for.

The Gate Approach.name: The Gate Approach
The Gate Approach.basicInfo: [Lv 4-48 · Low] White frames step up from the approach ground in tight ranks, curved surfaces set close with charcoal recesses cut between them and cobalt guidance lines running underfoot toward the gate. Rezulith's Workshop keeps a working frontage among them, repair channels open and lit from within rather than from the street, and the Vexorath Gate District lays its plating flush so that nothing catches a wheel. Doors along the route part ahead of the people walking them. Sound stays close and muted, absorbed by the ranks of frame before it can cross a lane. Landing is onto marked plate at the gate side rather than into the ranks themselves. Part of Vexorath.
The Gate Approach.hiddenInfo: Every normal non-Contair arrival enters through the Gate District, whose master states no destination list: Relstaris and Helvyra establish the connection from their side, Solvraxis, Ignivex and Dustfall exclude it by their own closed lists, Quilrath is locked out politically, and Korrvane is undetermined. The Dravon Access Denial Marker states the permanent bar in the open, and a Dravon attempt to enter is never routine. Inside Rezulith's Workshop the corridors move and rooms are reassigned between visits; The Private Lunar Gate Wing to Lumina Reach is settled as a station-operations matter before a guest arrives. The Seris Transfer Bay's function is deliberately undefined, and Lumina Minor keeps changing Workshop systems without Rezulith's preferred architecture; Paul Thovex logs each change. The next reassignment of rooms will move the bay, or not.

Cloud Shoulder.name: Cloud Shoulder
Cloud Shoulder.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Thick cloud occupies most of this height and moves fast enough that gaps open and close over the ground in minutes. What shows through them is grey rock and old snow banked on the northern faces. Summit Countryeast lies on the ground off to the west. Flying blind through here is routine and still punishing, because the summits stand up into the cloud and give no warning inside it. Ice forms on anything held in this air for long and the wind strips it off again unevenly. What rock shows is grey and stripped, standing in ridges too narrow to be useful even where they can be reached.
Cloud Shoulder.hiddenInfo: Cloud Shoulder sits above cloud more often than below it, with the Silver Peaks the only fixed reference. The snowline decides where anything can stop.

Layered Cloud Heights.name: Layered Cloud Heights
Layered Cloud Heights.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Layered cloud fills much of this high air, pale and slow-moving, with breaks that open onto blue above and grey rock below. The Silver Peaks stand through it to the south and west, snow on their shoulders showing where the vapour thins. The layers move at different speeds and slide over one another, opening a gap in one and closing it in the next. This is air rather than water, and unreliable air at that, thickening and clearing again within the space of a single crossing. Light in the breaks is white and hard, and inside them it is grey and without direction.
Layered Cloud Heights.hiddenInfo: Thin cold air over Layered Cloud Heights, with bare rock and old snow beneath and no footing that could be called a landing. A flier who drops into cloud here has rock in every direction.

Grey Bank Chop.name: Grey Bank Chop
Grey Bank Chop.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Grey-white cloud lies in a broad bank across the upper frame and the sea beneath it is pale, moving in short crowded swells with foam along their tops. Crests rise close on one another and give the surface no rest between them. The light is soft and comes from no particular direction. Colour in the water is thin, more green than blue. Light entering water this pale is returned almost at once, so the colour has no depth in it anywhere. Fliers under this cloud stay low enough to see the surface and accept that the horizon gives them nothing.
Grey Bank Chop.hiddenInfo: Open water with no landing under Grey Bank Chop: a flier who loses a heading here has only the sun to correct it. Nothing here needs story evidence except the weather.

Turquoise Patches East.name: Turquoise Patches East
Turquoise Patches East.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Under a sky half filled with flat cloud the water runs pale and slightly choppy, its turquoise cast strongest where the sun breaks through in moving patches. The lit patches travel across the water at the pace of the cloud above and take the colour with them. The swell is short. Between them the sea goes flat grey-green and the swell loses its edges. Wind arrives in gusts rather than steadily. Anything crossing works through changing air the whole way, and holds altitude in the gaps between cloud shadows where the lift is better.
Turquoise Patches East.hiddenInfo: Nothing marks Turquoise Patches East but swell; the crossing is made on held height and remembered bearing. Distance is the danger; the sea itself is indifferent.

Cloud Lane Water.name: Cloud Lane Water
Cloud Lane Water.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Washed-out blue water under a sky carrying long thin cloud, the two meeting at a horizon that is visible but never sharp. The cloud runs in long parallel bars with clear lanes between them, and the water beneath each lane brightens without changing colour. Foam shows in short lines where the swell steepens. The colour is shallow-looking rather than deep. Light penetrates only a little way before scattering back, which is what keeps the blue thin. Fliers cross with the sea kept in view below and take their bearings from heading alone, since the sky offers no fixed feature to hold against.
Cloud Lane Water.hiddenInfo: Cloud Lane Water offers no rock, no bar and no rest, and the light off it is the main hazard by midday. Wildlife under the surface is possible and rarely seen; bandits do not work water this open.

Torn Cloud Water.name: Torn Cloud Water
Torn Cloud Water.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Half of this frame is sky: a broad pale cloud sheet with ragged lower edges and blue showing through the tears in it. The sea beneath runs light and green-tinged, foam threading the crests. Through the tears the sunlight falls in hard-edged patches that slide over the water and vanish. No rain appears to be falling but the air is damp. The sea holds light briefly and gives it back green, so the colour is surface colour with nothing beneath it. Crossings are flown under the sheet where the surface stays visible, with height traded for the certainty of seeing water.
Torn Cloud Water.hiddenInfo: The colour of Torn Cloud Water says nothing about what lies beneath, and nothing here will catch a tired flier. Ships bound for the Orbital Gate Station pass far above; nothing else uses this sky.

Shadow-Cast Shallows.name: Shadow-Cast Shallows
Shadow-Cast Shallows.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Green-blue shallows tone dominates the water, pale enough that the swell throws its own shadow onto the back of each wave. Those shadows travel with the swell and give the water a worked, folded look that the open sea further out never has. Above the horizon the cloud is broken into separate flat-bottomed pieces. The wind is moderate and the surface only lightly foamed. The flat bottoms all sit at the same level, and the sky between them is a clean untroubled blue. There is nothing in the cell to navigate by and nothing to avoid, so fliers pass through without changing anything.
Shadow-Cast Shallows.hiddenInfo: Over Shadow-Cast Shallows the wind is the only fixed thing, and it changes. A downed traveller is a rescue only if someone saw them go down.

Low Swell Passage.name: Low Swell Passage
Low Swell Passage.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Steady low swell under a mostly open sky, the water pale at the crests and darkening in the troughs where the light does not reach. Scattered cloud drifts high enough to cast only faint shadow. The crests carry no foam at all, only a change of tone where the water thins near the top. Nothing breaks the surface. Light comes down at an angle and lays a broad soft sheen across the frame without concentrating anywhere. Air is even and the flying easy, which mainly means that a crossing here is a matter of endurance rather than of skill.
Low Swell Passage.hiddenInfo: Low Swell Passage is transit air over deep water, crossed rather than visited. Weather arrives from the open quarter with little warning and no shelter.

Mid-Blue Passage.name: Mid-Blue Passage
Mid-Blue Passage.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Clean mid-blue water running out to every edge of the frame, the swell long and low and the crests seldom breaking. A few pieces of high cloud stand well above it. The track shifts and lengthens as the sun moves, and the water either side of it keeps a colour the glare does not touch. Light falls hard on the surface and gives back a broad bright track. Below the lit layer the blue closes quickly, so the water looks solid rather than clear from any height. Fliers hold whatever height keeps them out of the worst of the reflected glare and do not descend without cause.
Mid-Blue Passage.hiddenInfo: Open water with no landing under Mid-Blue Passage: a flier who loses a heading here has only the sun to correct it. Distance is the danger; the sea itself is indifferent.

Sun-High Water.name: Sun-High Water
Sun-High Water.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Sun stands high over open blue water with only a little cloud to soften it. The swell is well ordered, arriving in long parallel lines whose pattern shows most clearly from height. Seen from lower down the same ranks lose their order and read as unrelated humps of water. Wind is moderate and steady. The light stands almost overhead and falls straight in, so shadow on the swell faces is short and the colour is even. Air rising off the warmed surface gives intermittent lift, and crews flying here ride it rather than fight the small changes in altitude it causes.
Sun-High Water.hiddenInfo: Nothing marks Sun-High Water but swell; the crossing is made on held height and remembered bearing. Wildlife under the surface is possible and rarely seen; bandits do not work water this open.

Lightening Shallows.name: Lightening Shallows
Lightening Shallows.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Colour lightens across this water toward the pale foam-laced tone of the shallower sea, though nothing actually shows through the surface. Swells run moderate and break in short white lines at their tops. The white lines last only a moment before the next face rolls them under. Cloud is minor and high. Where the tone lightens the water returns more of the sky and less of its own colour, though the change is even and has no edge to it. The crossing is unremarkable in fair weather, and fliers use it as the easy part of a longer span rather than as a stage in itself.
Lightening Shallows.hiddenInfo: Lightening Shallows offers no rock, no bar and no rest, and the light off it is the main hazard by midday. Ships bound for the Orbital Gate Station pass far above; nothing else uses this sky.

The Foam Scatter.name: The Foam Scatter
The Foam Scatter.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Everything in the frame is water: a light clear blue worked into small crests with foam scattered thinly across them. No coast, no cloud of consequence, no change in the surface from one side to the other. The crests are short and rise without order, and the foam sits in isolated flecks rather than in lines. The light is high and flat. Light goes into the clear blue and comes back from well down, giving the colour a lit quality even under a flat sky. Fliers get no help and no hindrance, and the real hazard is losing track of how much of the span is already behind.
The Foam Scatter.hiddenInfo: The colour of The Foam Scatter says nothing about what lies beneath, and nothing here will catch a tired flier. A downed traveller is a rescue only if someone saw them go down.

Turquoise Approach.name: Turquoise Approach
Turquoise Approach.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Eastward and to the south the water pales further into the bright shallow colour of the Radiant Strait, and here it is already lightening, turquoise where the light seems to reach further into it. Foam shows in broken lines. The turquoise deepens in tone away from the strait side and holds a green core in the swell faces. Glare off the surface is strong. Sky is nearly bare and the horizon toward the strait is lost in reflected white. Fliers converging on the strait take their approach through this water and begin losing height from it.
Turquoise Approach.hiddenInfo: Over Turquoise Approach the wind is the only fixed thing, and it changes. Weather arrives from the open quarter with little warning and no shelter.

The Sea Margin.name: The Sea Margin
The Sea Margin.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Water covers most of what can be seen from this margin of the range, bright and open, running up to the point where the first grey rock lifts out of it along the eastern edge. The line between the two is abrupt. Cold air slides off the high ground and out over the surface, so flying this edge is rougher work than the open water further west suggests. The bright water to the west belongs to Radiant Strait, and northward it runs on into Open Ocean without a mark between them. Where the first stone lifts it does so in a single grey step with no shelving in front of it.
The Sea Margin.hiddenInfo: Where The Sea Margin meets the water there is stone to stand on and little else; landings are possible and rarely worth it. Starian bandits are not unknown on lonely coast, and cover here shelters them as readily as a traveller.

Snow Saddle.name: Snow Saddle
Snow Saddle.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Ridgetops break through the cloud base and stand clear, pale and stripped, snow packed into every hollow the sun does not reach. Between them is open air and a long drop. The rock that shows is too steep and too broken to walk, so movement through this cell is flying movement, and the only usable rests are the flat shoulders where a ridge widens before climbing again. Old snow packed into the hollows carries a crust that holds a step and then gives without warning. Wind runs over the ridge tops in one direction and breaks into sink on the far side of each of them. Part of Vexorath.
Snow Saddle.hiddenInfo: Snow Saddle is Vexorath ground by every rule that matters and by no landmark anyone would name. Approach lanes are marked in cobalt; off them is rock and air.

The Residential Tier.name: The Residential Tier
The Residential Tier.basicInfo: [Lv 2-38 · Low] Housing terraces take most of this ground, low and curved, each with a small planted court kept quiet behind screening. The Learning and Development Annex stands among them on a broader platform, frame white, recesses charcoal, repair channels visible along every joint. Public seating shifts to fit whoever settles on it. Walkways through the Residential District are surfaced in a fine pale composite that takes no marks, and the internal illumination stays restrained enough that the courts hold their own shade through the day. Conversation carries no further than the screening allows. Level ground is common here and easy to come down onto. Part of Vexorath.
The Residential Tier.hiddenInfo: Seris Contair lives here rather than inside her mother's Workshop, and the choice is a statement of independence and a practical boundary, not estrangement and not political conflict. She is an independent inventor, the creator of Lumina Minor, and the strongest internal source of change in Vexorath; her childhood friendships with Nina Castro and Zephyra Genesis stay personal rather than alliances between Houses. The district's running tension is the city's worst habit: Vexorath must never become a place where every resident is an engineer, and the Non-Engineer Community Hall is where the educators, cooks, artists, historians, carers and mediators organise against exactly that, with a proposal for the Assembly Floor now being drafted. The proposal goes to the Assembly at the next sitting.

Civic Systems Level.name: Civic Systems Level
Civic Systems Level.basicInfo: [Lv 4-23 · Low] Density is the whole character of this ground: frames set shoulder to shoulder, walkways threaded between them at three or four working levels, cobalt guidance lines everywhere underfoot. The Vexorath Exchange opens onto the widest of the decks, and the Civic Systems Quarter around it runs maintenance in the open, panels swung back and components resetting themselves. Lighting stays low and even. The decks are curved composite with repair channels visible along their edges, and delivery drones crossing overhead break their lines around anyone standing to talk. Landing space is allotted rather than found, and every approach lane is marked. Part of Vexorath.
Civic Systems Level.hiddenInfo: Two live problems sit in the Civic Systems Quarter. Maelis Contair has found that residents have been quietly working around a system rather than reporting it, a complaint pattern that never arrived because people solved it themselves. Sharper: Vexorath records systems rather than private lives, but connected systems reveal behaviour indirectly, and a resident who found that infrastructure monitoring recorded more than intended has brought it to the Privacy Challenge Chamber, where it stays an ongoing tension. Technical authority must explain restrictions once an emergency ends, but no venue for that duty has ever been assigned. The Privacy Challenge hearing is scheduled; the venue for the explanation is not.

The Eastward Face.name: The Eastward Face
The Eastward Face.basicInfo: [Lv 9-15 · Low] Curved white blocks step down the eastern shoulder of the massif in even ranks, their charcoal recesses deep enough to read as shadow from well out. This is Vexorath City ground — dense, quiet, finished — with repair channels running visible along the frontages and small gardens set into the gaps between them. Flight lanes come in low over the rim. Stairs between ranks are shallow and continuous, cut from the same pale material as the frontages, so a descent reads as one surface rather than a series of steps. The gardens hold the only loose ground on this side. Part of Vexorath.
The Eastward Face.hiddenInfo: Vexorath City behaves like an active participant without anyone treating it as a conscious person, and that gap is where its trouble lives. A civic system can reach a technically correct decision that lands badly on real people, an environmental route has begun favouring the wrong users on these terraces, and a maintenance alert may be the visible edge of something deeper. Residents debate automation changes on the Civic Assembly Floor, which does not overrule a genuine systems emergency, though technical authority must explain its restrictions afterwards and the venue has never been fixed. The Lumina Core Indicator Court remains the standing puzzle: nobody states what the indicator displays, what its states mean, or who may stand in the court and read it. The route fault has a review date on the Assembly agenda, and the indicator changed state the morning it was set.

The Grey Cleft.name: The Grey Cleft
The Grey Cleft.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Stone lies underfoot everywhere, grey shading to white where the light strikes it, cut through by narrow clefts that keep old snow long after the exposed rock is clear. The air is thin and dry, and wind changes direction against the faces without warning. The Grey Cleft occupies the ground to the west; southward the slope closes into forest, which is where the bare country ends. That forest southward is Highland Forest, dark and closing over the last of the open stone. The clefts run one way across the face, narrow enough to step over and deep enough to turn an ankle in. Part of Vexorath.
The Grey Cleft.hiddenInfo: Cross The Grey Cleft to reach Vexorath's real districts; it holds only what the city overflows. Approach lanes are marked in cobalt; off them is rock and air.

Outerridge Air.name: Outerridge Air
Outerridge Air.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Air and cloud fill most of this cell, with the outer ridges of the massif showing as pale teeth along its lower edge. Weather crosses in bands and visibility swings from clean to nothing and back. Updraughts run hard along those ridges and can be worked by a flier who reads them, but they turn to rotor and sink on the lee side without looking any different. Ice glazes the exposed faces on the windward side and leaves the lee dry, so what a footing is worth changes within a stride of crossing a crest. Nothing grows anywhere in the cell. Part of Vexorath.
Outerridge Air.hiddenInfo: Outerridge Air is service ground for Vexorath, crossed daily and rarely mentioned. Approach lanes are marked in cobalt; off them is rock and air.

Peak Shadow Water.name: Peak Shadow Water
Peak Shadow Water.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Westward the grey slopes of the Silver Peaks close the frame, and the water in front of them runs pale and moving, foam in short lines across a moderate swell. Cloud sits above the ridge line and spills seaward in a thinning sheet. The sheet stops short of the open water and leaves the outer part of the frame in clear light. The air near the mountains is unsettled. Colour in the sea runs grey-green where the mountain shadow falls on it and pale blue where it does not. Fliers making for the peaks from the water stand off and gain height before committing to the slope.
Peak Shadow Water.hiddenInfo: Open water with no landing under Peak Shadow Water: a flier who loses a heading here has only the sun to correct it. Wildlife under the surface is possible and rarely seen; bandits do not work water this open.

Weather Shelf Water.name: Weather Shelf Water
Weather Shelf Water.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Weather sits in the upper frame as a grey shelf of cloud with brighter sky behind it, and beneath it the sea runs pale and worked, foam scattered across crests that follow no single direction. The shelf has a hard lower edge and a bright rim where the light gets round it. The colour is more green than blue. Wind shifts. Light beneath it is grey and thin, and the water returns almost none of it. A crossing is flown with the expectation that the air will not be the same at the far side as at the near.
Weather Shelf Water.hiddenInfo: Nothing marks Weather Shelf Water but swell; the crossing is made on held height and remembered bearing. Ships bound for the Orbital Gate Station pass far above; nothing else uses this sky.

The Slow Swells.name: The Slow Swells
The Slow Swells.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Broad pale water under a sky half taken by flat cloud, the surface lifting in slow rounded swells that break only occasionally. The horizon shows as a faint change of tone rather than as a line. Where a swell does break it does so quietly, the crest sliding rather than falling. Colour runs green through the shallower shades and grey where the cloud shadow lies. The cloud lies in a single flat layer with no structure to it and no gaps of consequence. Fliers hold below the cloud and take the small buffeting that comes with the lower air.
The Slow Swells.hiddenInfo: The Slow Swells offers no rock, no bar and no rest, and the light off it is the main hazard by midday. A downed traveller is a rescue only if someone saw them go down.

The Choppy Banks.name: The Choppy Banks
The Choppy Banks.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Small crowded waves cover the surface, pale-topped and close together, with a longer swell moving underneath them that shows only from height. The two motions work against each other, and the small waves steepen whenever a long crest lifts beneath them. The sky is mostly clear. Light comes off the water scattered rather than focused. Sky is open enough that the horizon holds a firm line all the way round. Nothing in the cell marks position, and a flier crossing it depends entirely on the heading set before the coast dropped away behind.
The Choppy Banks.hiddenInfo: The colour of The Choppy Banks says nothing about what lies beneath, and nothing here will catch a tired flier. Weather arrives from the open quarter with little warning and no shelter.

Distant Shore Water.name: Distant Shore Water
Distant Shore Water.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Landward to the south the green edge of the Verdant Coast shows at the limit of sight, and between it and this frame there is nothing but pale moving water with foam across the crests. The green reads as a low band with no detail in it, darker than the water and softened by the air between. Cloud takes a good part of the sky and the light is intermittent. Fliers inbound take their first reliable fix off that shoreline and adjust their heading here rather than earlier. Swell runs toward that shore and steepens slightly as it goes, though it breaks nowhere in the frame.
Distant Shore Water.hiddenInfo: Over Distant Shore Water the wind is the only fixed thing, and it changes. Nothing here needs story evidence except the weather.

Crosspoint Water.name: Crosspoint Water
Crosspoint Water.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Strong blue water with the swell running in long low ranks, breaking white only where two lines meet. The meeting points travel along the ranks rather than staying put, so the white appears and dies in a different place each time. Sky is almost clear and the light hard. The green line of the Verdant Coast lies south at the edge of what can be seen. Light comes off the water in a steady sheet on the sun side and leaves the rest of the frame a deep flat colour. Fliers inbound begin losing height here, because the air near the coast is rougher and the descent is better made out over water.
Crosspoint Water.hiddenInfo: Crosspoint Water is transit air over deep water, crossed rather than visited. Distance is the danger; the sea itself is indifferent.

Korrvane Approach.name: Korrvane Approach
Korrvane Approach.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Beyond the southern edge of the frame the ground rises toward Korrvane, and the water in front of it runs deep clean blue in unhurried swells. Cloud is negligible and the surface carries little foam. The swell arrives from the open side and passes under without changing shape. Fliers approaching from seaward pick up this line and hold it, since there is nothing in the water below that would make them alter course before the land comes up. Light goes far into water this clean and returns a dense saturated blue with nothing thin about it. Part of Korrvane.
Korrvane Approach.hiddenInfo: Korrvane Approach is the built edge of Korrvane: the same fabric as the city, thinner, and no authored location stands on it. The bracket sets the week even out here.

The Approach Deeps.name: The Approach Deeps
The Approach Deeps.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Saturated dark blue, with long swells arriving from the open side and passing beneath without breaking. The sky holds only thin high cloud. The high cloud is drawn into fine streaks that shade nothing below them. Away to the south the ground around Korrvane stands as a low broken line above the water. Between swells the surface is almost still, and the colour there goes nearly black before the next face lifts it. Air here is steady and the flying straightforward, which makes this water a piece of a longer approach rather than anywhere anyone stops. Part of Korrvane.
The Approach Deeps.hiddenInfo: Nothing on The Approach Deeps is a destination; travel here arrives at the nearest named site of Korrvane. The bracket sets the week even out here.

The Open Field.name: The Open Field
The Open Field.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Unbroken open water, bright blue and lightly worked, with no coast in frame although the cliffs of the Verdant Coast lie somewhere south of it. The swell is long and even. The working of the surface is fine enough that it breaks the glare into countless separate points rather than one sheet. There is no cloud to speak of and the glare off the surface is considerable through the middle of the day. Light carries a long way down into the blue and the colour holds strong to the limit of what returns. Fliers use the set of the swell as a wind check and otherwise have nothing to read.
The Open Field.hiddenInfo: Open water with no landing under The Open Field: a flier who loses a heading here has only the sun to correct it. Ships bound for the Orbital Gate Station pass far above; nothing else uses this sky.

Strait Approach North.name: Strait Approach North
Strait Approach North.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Approaching the pale water of the Radiant Strait from the northwest, the sea still runs the deeper open blue, swell low and regular under a nearly clear sky. Light strengthens eastward where the shallower colour begins. The paler colour shows first as a brightening along the eastern edge rather than as a line. The Verdant Coast lies south beyond the frame. Swell carries through from the open side without shortening and the surface stays smooth between crests. This water carries more crossing traffic than the open sea further out, and the air over it is seldom empty.
Strait Approach North.hiddenInfo: Nothing marks Strait Approach North but swell; the crossing is made on held height and remembered bearing. A downed traveller is a rescue only if someone saw them go down.

Bright Mid-Channel.name: Bright Mid-Channel
Bright Mid-Channel.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Deep even blue fills the cell, with no cloud overhead and no foam below to interrupt it. The channel is at its most featureless here: water in every direction, the shoulders of land too far off to read as more than a change of colour at the rim of sight. A crossing is made in one committed run, and the wind that builds along the length of the water is the only condition worth watching. Grey ground stands off to the east where Silver Peaks meets the water, low in the view and the only feature of any kind within reach of the eye.
Bright Mid-Channel.hiddenInfo: The colour of Bright Mid-Channel says nothing about what lies beneath, and nothing here will catch a tired flier. Nothing here needs story evidence except the weather.

The Grey Shoulder.name: The Grey Shoulder
The Grey Shoulder.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Lit water reaches across almost the whole cell, broken only by a low grey shoulder of the range on its eastern side. Southward the shoreline turns black where the Ashen Coast begins. Little here offers a landing, and fliers working along the seaward flank of the range stay high enough to clear the stone and low enough to keep the water in view for a heading. Westward the water is Radiant Strait, brighter again and running the length of the channel. The grey shoulder on the eastern side drops to the water without a margin, so there is no strip of stone to work along at its foot.
The Grey Shoulder.hiddenInfo: The shore at The Grey Shoulder is walkable at the cost of wet footing, and the surf covers the sound of anything approaching. Wildlife works the tideline; a careless camp attracts it.

The Frozen Slides.name: The Frozen Slides
The Frozen Slides.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Grey rock comes down to the sea in long spurs on this flank of the massif, bright channels of water between them and white veining where the swell forces into the gaps. Snow holds only in the highest shaded cuts. The ground is walkable along a spur and impossible across one, and the forested slope eastward is the easier way inland for anyone not flying. That forested slope is Highland Forest, standing dark below the bare stone. South of the spurs the shore turns black where the Ashen Coast begins, and the change in the rock is plain from any height.
The Frozen Slides.hiddenInfo: The Frozen Slides is a margin rather than a place: salt, rock and the swell working at both. A stranded hull or a lost load washes up here before anyone reports it missing.

Mist Under Canopy.name: Mist Under Canopy
Mist Under Canopy.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Slopes fall away from the high stone in long steps, each carrying the same close dark timber, the trees thinning only where rock breaks through. Mist gathers under the canopy and stays there long after the open ground above has cleared. Mist Under Canopy lies up the gradient to the north, and the descent southward is gradual enough to walk under a load. The descent runs down toward The Outer Blockworks, which is where the loaded traffic on this slope is going. Where rock breaks through the trees the ground is loose with fragments shed off it and the footing is worse than under full canopy.
Mist Under Canopy.hiddenInfo: Mist Under Canopy is Luminous Forest country: close cover, small watercourses and quiet that carries sound a long way. A lost traveller here is found by the streams, which all run somewhere.

The Snowpatch Belt.name: The Snowpatch Belt
The Snowpatch Belt.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Timber runs unbroken over a gradient that never eases, green-black in daylight and nearly solid to look down on. Snow lies in patches where the slope faces away from the sun and the trees stand more open. Above the tree line the ground climbs toward The Snowpatch Belt; below, the fall continues south past The Gray Rings, with no level footing anywhere between except what has been cut. The cut ground is narrow, benched into the slope and banked along its outer edge, and it holds where everything either side of it does not. Snow on the shaded patches lies over needle litter that gives beneath it, so the footing there is worse than on the bare gradient.
The Snowpatch Belt.hiddenInfo: The tracks through The Snowpatch Belt are kept open by use and would close within a season without it. Foraging is possible for those who know the growth; most do not.

The Wet Dark Floor.name: The Wet Dark Floor
The Wet Dark Floor.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Steep forested ground, dark and wet underfoot, moss and needle litter deadening every sound that is not wind working in the tops. Small water courses cut across any line of travel and make poor crossings. Low flying earns little here, the canopy being unbroken and the air above it rough, so the better going is on the cut traverses angling down toward The Gray Rings. The traverses are cut into the slope at a shallow angle and banked where the ground falls away hardest, and they are the only footing here that does not tilt. Moss holds water and gives it up slowly, so the ground stays soft well after the weather has gone through.
The Wet Dark Floor.hiddenInfo: The Wet Dark Floor is walkable, crossable on foot in a day and easier from the air, where the canopy reads as one surface. The forest hides a camp well and a fire badly.

The Stepped Descent.name: The Stepped Descent
The Stepped Descent.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Broken cloud hangs at the level of the outer ridges, and the gaps in it show grey stone falling away eastward in steps. Light comes through in hard moving patches that change what the ground looks like minute by minute. Beneath, the slope eases southward until it meets The North Route, which gives a flier a line to follow down out of the high air when the weather closes above. West of the broken cloud the ground falls into the timber of Highland Forest, dark and continuous where the stone runs out.
The Stepped Descent.hiddenInfo: Nothing lives at The Stepped Descent but wind; the rock is too steep and too broken to walk. Rescue at this height is a Contair drone or nothing.

Peak Shadow Reach.name: Peak Shadow Reach
Peak Shadow Reach.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Shadow from the Silver Peaks falls across the western part of this water in the early and late hours, and the sea itself runs pale and foam-flecked under a mostly open sky. Swell is short and irregular where it rebounds off the rock. Inside the shadow the water goes grey and its foam is lost against the darker tone, while outside it the pale blue returns at once. Wind comes down from the high ground in uneven pushes, and fliers working this edge keep clear of the slope and hold their height. Light in the open part of the frame comes in low and skims the surface rather than entering it.
Peak Shadow Reach.hiddenInfo: Over Peak Shadow Reach the wind is the only fixed thing, and it changes. Distance is the danger; the sea itself is indifferent.

The Grey Curtain.name: The Grey Curtain
The Grey Curtain.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Overcast covers most of the sky and takes the colour out of the water, which runs pale and grey-green with foam showing in ragged lines. The overcast has no break in it anywhere and no variation of tone to suggest where the sun stands. Visibility under the cloud base is adequate but the horizon has gone. The swell is moderate and disorganised. What light reaches the water is given straight back, and the sea shows no colour at all below its own skin. Crossings are flown low and slow with the surface kept in constant sight, because no other reference is available.
The Grey Curtain.hiddenInfo: The Grey Curtain is transit air over deep water, crossed rather than visited. Wildlife under the surface is possible and rarely seen; bandits do not work water this open.

Inshore Turquoise.name: Inshore Turquoise
Inshore Turquoise.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Close to land on two sides, this water still reads as open sea: pale turquoise where the light gets into it, darker in the troughs, foam-laced at the tops. The green of the Verdant Coast shows south and east. The turquoise is strongest in the middle of the frame and gives way to a heavier tone where the water runs out toward the open side. Cloud is light. Light reaches through the pale water far enough to come back with a faint yellow in it. Fliers making the coast have the shoreline in sight for the rest of the run and usually lose height over water before crossing it.
Inshore Turquoise.hiddenInfo: Open water with no landing under Inshore Turquoise: a flier who loses a heading here has only the sun to correct it. A downed traveller is a rescue only if someone saw them go down.

Dune Grass Shore.name: Dune Grass Shore
Dune Grass Shore.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Blue water takes up nearly the whole of this reach, bright and moving in long swells that break white and then reassemble. The shore shows only as a thin dark seam along one edge, too narrow to walk without wading. A flier crossing holds height for want of anywhere to set down, and the line of green beyond the water is the only thing worth steering by. Open Ocean lies north and west, and the join between it and this water is a matter of tone rather than anything on the surface. Wind crosses the swell rather than running with it, so the crests carry torn spray that lifts, hangs and drops back.
Dune Grass Shore.hiddenInfo: Fliers use Dune Grass Shore as a coast mark; walkers find the going slow and the shelter poor. The nearest help is the nearest city, and it is not close.

The Stacked City.name: The Stacked City
The Stacked City.basicInfo: [Lv 9-17 · Low] Platform over platform, this is the heaviest building fabric in Korrvane City: stone slabs and storm-metal decking laid up the cliff until the vertical streets give up and become stairs and ladders. The Lower Grounds hold the base of the stack in permanent shade, and the Recovery Yards open beside them as flat working ground where loads can be set down. Impact-marked walls are unremarkable here. Daylight arrives late on the lower levels and leaves early, so lamps under the platform soffits stay lit through the day. A walker crosses by going up or down as much as along, and fliers keep to the open shafts, with little clear air standing over the decks. Part of Korrvane.
The Stacked City.hiddenInfo: Everything the upper city breaks is repaired in the Lower Grounds, and Impact Repair Row can usually name which platform is due to fail before any notice says so; Iven Korrash and Kael Drathen have one in mind now and no official reason to stop traffic on it. Class and elevation tension runs through the district without poverty behind it, aired at the Grounded Cup among workers, non-fliers and Sol visitors whose weapons culture unsettles the locals. In the Recovery Yards the Injury Registry Desk tracks suspicious damage patterns, and a fighter turning up repeatedly with injuries that do not match declared matches has become a quiet file; the Rival Waiting Steps put people who just fought each other side by side while the adrenaline is still burning off. The next bracket close will fill the yards, and the platform question cannot wait past it.

Genesis Cliffs.name: Genesis Cliffs
Genesis Cliffs.basicInfo: [Lv 2-93 · Moderate] Cliff and open water meet along the northern side of this ground, the rock dropping in dark storm-metal tiers toward the sea. The Genesis Compound is set into the face itself, galleries and reinforced glass following the stone rather than cutting across it, and Genesis Ridge rises bare and wind-raked behind. Banners stand stiff off the landing shelves. The tiers underfoot are heavy stone slab bedded onto the cliff and edged in bronze-black trim, damp with spray at the lip. Wind comes off the water without a break, carrying salt and the slap of banner cloth against rail. Part of Korrvane.
Genesis Cliffs.hiddenInfo: Korrvane is governed from a single desk in the Genesis Compound. Tacitus Genesis handles minor-house disputes, Arena policy, Contair maintenance relationships and citywide emergencies from an office that never clears, while Ark Genesis anchors the challenge culture and keeps breaking a training ground whose replacement is now a routine line item. Up on Genesis Ridge, reached only through restricted airspace, Sorvina carries grief through private matches on the scar path, Orvanus decides case by case which markers to explain, and conversations happen that neither Ark nor Tacitus would have inside. Challenger invitations from the Visitor Hall carry political weight recipients rarely read correctly, and one has just gone to a Marrik in Dustfall whose family is split over answering it before the bracket.

The Bronze Tiers.name: The Bronze Tiers
The Bronze Tiers.basicInfo: [Lv 3-69 · Moderate] Aevon, Orvantis and Vorreth quarters stack down the cliff in bronze-black tiers, each platform hung under the shadow of the one above and joined by suspended bridges that shift in the wind. Building is looser here than deeper in the city, bare rock showing between terraces, the decking laid in storm-metal panels bolted over stone with the seams left plain. Sea lies off the northern lip, green coast country off the east. Sound arrives in layers: wind across the open gaps, bridge cable humming under load, voices carrying down from the tier above rather than along the same level. Part of Korrvane.
The Bronze Tiers.hiddenInfo: Three houses on one cliff are each arguing with their own history. Orvantis has stayed physically steady while its standing shifted and has not decided whether continuity is foundation or burden: Sophira trains against a standard of dignified defeat she rejects, Hannovar watches from the balcony instead of competing, Hasdrovex decides policy over a corner table, and Vaelris keeps a connection with Sophavel Caelthorn that neither family would endorse. Yadira Aevon knows courier cuts that officially do not exist, and every lane-obstruction investigation asks whether Aevon routes are safe for those flying beneath. Vorreth's Bomivex keeps a record wall that contradicts the civic archives, and Magovar's platform stands empty often enough to be a subject. Each house fields a competitor this week, and the seeding language is already under Caelthorn challenge.

Zelvaris Fringe.name: Zelvaris Fringe
Zelvaris Fringe.basicInfo: [Lv 19-68 · Low] Building thins toward the eastern edge of the city, where the Zelvaris Quarter holds a scatter of platforms and cliff-cut housing with green coming back in the gaps between them. Wind arrives unbroken and the banners are fewer. Made ground gives way underfoot to grass-seamed rock and loose scree, storm-metal decking patched in only where a path needs carrying across a break. Forest takes over past the last of the decking, and a strip of coast shows to the north. Fliers use this air as the approach to the denser layers west; walkers find fewer bridges and more bare rock. Part of Korrvane.
Zelvaris Fringe.hiddenInfo: Zelvaris measures everything, and the measuring is both the house's strength and its danger. The Combat Data Archive holds match analysis on competitors from every district, which other houses find useful, unnerving and occasionally worth acquiring by less than honest means; Hamilvar Zelvaris observes and records more than he says, and someone has been asking about the archive's access. Recovery is built into the quarter's geography, the Recovery Grind Benches running through to the annex in the Recovery Yards, and Eshmunar Zelvaris moves between the two to keep Magara Zelvaris's training loads survivable; The ambition is genuine and the evidence is real, but nobody in the quarter has produced a result that proves the method works at the top, and everyone here, Abdesara and Tannivar included, knows exactly how many weeks it has been.

The Twin Shores.name: The Twin Shores
The Twin Shores.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Mid-channel water, brilliant and shallow-reading, throws light upward hard enough that the air above it stays hazy. Eastward, the dark rock of the Ashen Coast draws a hard black line where the water ends; westward there is only more water. Fliers take their bearing off that dark shore, because it is the one edge that stays legible through the glare. Under the glare the swells run low and evenly spaced, too small to break and too regular to give a flier anything to time against, and the surface holds no mark from one side of the cell to the other.
The Twin Shores.hiddenInfo: The colour of The Twin Shores says nothing about what lies beneath, and nothing here will catch a tired flier. Distance is the danger; the sea itself is indifferent.

Offshore Deeps.name: Offshore Deeps
Offshore Deeps.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Bright open water fills this cell almost completely, swells running long and unbroken with nothing standing out of them. What land there is sits at the far edge as a dark line, black rather than green. A flier crossing has held height the whole way and keeps it, because the nearest place to come down is that black line and it does not improve on approach. Grey stone stands off to the north where Silver Peaks comes down to the water, and westward the surface runs on into Radiant Strait. No foam shows on the open part of this reach; white appears only where the swell reaches the black line and breaks.
Offshore Deeps.hiddenInfo: Over Offshore Deeps the wind is the only fixed thing, and it changes. Wildlife under the surface is possible and rarely seen; bandits do not work water this open.

The Outer Blockworks.name: The Outer Blockworks
The Outer Blockworks.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Grey composite blockwork stands in widely spaced runs on bare dark rock, each run squared to the same alignment and lit by red command-lights set low in the wall faces. Service roads link them in straight segments with turning bays at the joins. The rock between runs is left as it lies, scraped flat only where a road crosses it, and the road surfacing is a thin bound grit that shows its aggregate. Block faces are unornamented and return sound flatly across the open gaps. Highland Forest closes the ground to the north and the broken coast of Ashen Coast lies west, and the flight lanes over the built strip are marked out but little used. Part of Quilrath.
The Outer Blockworks.hiddenInfo: The Outer Blockworks carries Quilrath's ordinary life outward without any place of its own. Surveillance is total at the gates and thin between them.

The Bridged Blocks.name: The Bridged Blocks
The Bridged Blocks.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Low blocks of the same grey composite continue across this ground, set closer together than those to the west, with covered walkways bridging between upper floors. Surfaces are clean and unornamented and the red lighting is old enough that it throws very little. Walkway undersides are ribbed sheet, and the ground beneath them is paved to one level throughout so that nothing steps up or down. Loading aprons and marked landing squares sit at the block ends, and the dark line of Highland Forest shows beyond the last of the building. Part of Quilrath.
The Bridged Blocks.hiddenInfo: The Bridged Blocks is Quilrath ground by every rule that matters and by no landmark anyone would name. Surveillance is total at the gates and thin between them.

The Gray Rings.name: The Gray Rings
The Gray Rings.basicInfo: [Lv 3-15 · Moderate] Construction thins to long parallel terraces of grey composite, part of the work named The Gray Rings, their frontages flat and their windows set in identical bays. Ground between the terraces is hard-surfaced and drained to central channels. Status lighting runs in dim red lines along the parapets. The surfacing is a fine dark composite laid without joints, and the channels are grated flush so that nothing stands proud of the level.
