Sound carries badly, absorbed by the panelling, and movement on foot keeps to the marked lanes. Landing squares sit at the terrace ends. Part of Quilrath.
The Gray Rings.hiddenInfo: Standing decides housing, work, movement radius, queue speed and audit frequency, and Nivarek decides Standing; the Kathvar clerks at the counters only process what has already been determined, which does not stop people begging the wrong one. Ferrik Nivarek audits from the Standing Office believing precision is mercy; his files are immaculate and his sleep is not. Torbek Karn moves extras through the tolerated gray market on a Provision Hall counter with perfect paperwork, useful to the same officials who periodically raid it, everyone's quiet friend and nobody's informant so far. Merron Talvek teaches the official history in the Civics Classrooms, believes about half of it, and a pupil has just asked him about a name he remembers and the records do not; he has until the next lesson to decide which half he says aloud. The next audit cycle opens in Ashfall.

Terrace Row.name: Terrace Row
Terrace Row.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Composite terraces continue, broken by strips of low green growth in the service gaps where nothing has been built over. Panels show the pale patching of repeated repair. Overhead lanes are marked with reflective inlay rather than lit, and fliers using them hold the marked height. The green strips are unsurfaced and slightly sunken, and the paving either side of them is swept clean to the panel line. Air between the terrace walls stays still and moves only where a service gap runs through. Part of Quilrath.
Terrace Row.hiddenInfo: Cross Terrace Row to reach Quilrath's real districts; it holds only what the city overflows. Surveillance is total at the gates and thin between them.

Dustward Edge.name: Dustward Edge
Dustward Edge.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Built ground gives out eastward into dust and scattered scrub, the last composite structures set behind a hard-surfaced road that runs parallel to the edge rather than out of it. Red wall-lights are sparse and set at intervals that leave long dark stretches between them. Underfoot the change is quick: kerbed surfacing on one side of the road, loose grit and low woody growth on the other. Wind crosses the open ground unbroken and packs dust into the panel seams. Walkers keep to the road, there being no made way east of it. Part of Quilrath.
Dustward Edge.hiddenInfo: Dustward Edge is service ground for Quilrath, crossed daily and rarely mentioned. Surveillance is total at the gates and thin between them.

The Long Straightaway.name: The Long Straightaway
The Long Straightaway.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Most of this ground is water: the worked line runs along a narrow strip of coast with Open Ocean filling the view east and swell working the rock below. Spray reaches the surface when the weather is up. The usable ground is thin and the drop beside it is real. The strip is bare rock with a made edge only where the fall is worst, and salt has crusted the stone grey-white along the seaward margin. Sound is surf and wind together and does not let up. Traffic keeps to the landward side out of habit rather than instruction, and the habit is a sound one.
The Long Straightaway.hiddenInfo: The Long Straightaway is corridor ground, one stretch of the functional sequence between the Quiet Mile, the Handoff and the North Routehead. Redline sweeps from Quilrath reach this far on no schedule, and Accord runners time the gaps.

Blue Coast Run.name: Blue Coast Run
Blue Coast Run.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Hard deep blue water lying against the eastern edge of the land, with the worked line of the North Route somewhere inland to the west. The swell arrives at an angle to the shore and the surface stays busy. The angle of the swell drives a slow set along the shore that shows in the drift of the foam rather than in the water itself. Cloud is almost absent and the light direct. Colour holds dark right up to the land, with no paler margin along it. Fliers following the coast southward use this water for the clear air away from the rising ground and the traffic on it.
Blue Coast Run.hiddenInfo: Where Blue Coast Run meets the water there is stone to stand on and little else; landings are possible and rarely worth it. Wildlife works the tideline; a careless camp attracts it.

Calm Coast Water.name: Calm Coast Water
Calm Coast Water.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Between the open water westward and the green shore of the Verdant Coast just east, the sea runs a strong even blue with a long low swell and very little foam. The swell runs parallel to the shore and loses nothing as it goes, meeting no ground to turn it. The sky is clear. Light comes off the surface evenly rather than in a track. Light goes deep and returns an unbroken colour that changes only where the shore's shadow reaches out over the water in the later hours. This is water flown along rather than across, and fliers keep it under them as a margin against the rougher land air.
Calm Coast Water.hiddenInfo: Calm Coast Water is transit air over deep water, crossed rather than visited. Ships bound for the Orbital Gate Station pass far above; nothing else uses this sky.

The Unmarked Blue.name: The Unmarked Blue
The Unmarked Blue.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Nothing interrupts the water here: bright blue to the edge of sight, lifting and settling in swells that take the light and shed it again. No rock, no bar, no standing line of surf. A flier crossing picks one heading and holds it, because the green shore lies out of sight and there is nothing nearer to correct against. Open Ocean holds the whole of the northern and western sides, and the water carries through into it with no change a flier could see or feel. In light air the surface takes on long slick bands that lie across the swell and smooth it briefly.
The Unmarked Blue.hiddenInfo: Open water with no landing under The Unmarked Blue: a flier who loses a heading here has only the sun to correct it. Weather arrives from the open quarter with little warning and no shelter.

The Arena Bowl.name: The Arena Bowl
The Arena Bowl.basicInfo: [Lv 3-89 · Moderate] A bowl of worked stone below the cliff line holds the Arena, its rim ringed by the Gate Plazas where walkers funnel in from the tiers above. The Flight Lanes run as marked open sky over it, busy in both directions, with the Commerce Layer strung beneath them on suspended decking that flexes underfoot as crowds move across it. Caelthorn and Luxaryn quarters press in from either side, ordinary housing with balconies turned out of the wind, gust screens and stacked crates crowding the landings. Bronze-black trim, reinforced glass and moving banners everywhere. The bowl gathers sound and hands it back, so the Plazas stay loud whatever is happening below. Part of Korrvane.
The Arena Bowl.hiddenInfo: The Arena runs on a weekly cycle that never fully stops, and under it sit the pressures worth discovering. Betting odds move in ways nobody can account for; Caelthorn objections arrive at the Judges' Dais already drafted from Adherix Caelthorn's archive of superseded rules; Vorreth results keep breaking prediction models; medical clearances are occasionally optimistic and the Medic Gate sees the consequences. Sophavel Caelthorn's quiet connection with Vaelris Orvantis crosses a line his family would not sanction, and the argument in The Ascent over whether Caelthorn should stay tournament-eligible is not idle. In Luxaryn Quarter, Salambor's withheld invitations are messages the whole city can read, and Didobara's serious ambition keeps being taken less seriously than the party around her. Alcandrus Genesis judges the ladder attempt; Everything comes due at the next weekly final.

The Narrows.name: The Narrows
The Narrows.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Two very different shores frame this reach: green broken cliff on the western side, burnt black shelf on the eastern. Between them the water is bright and works in short crossing chop where the winds off each coast meet. Crossings are made constantly, both rims being close enough to hold in sight at once, and a flier caught by a change of weather can turn for either. The western rim is the Verdant Coast and the eastern the Ashen Coast, and the light comes off each of them differently enough to tell them apart in poor visibility. Between the two the water shallows through the middle and reads paler there than at either edge.
The Narrows.hiddenInfo: Fliers use The Narrows as a coast mark; walkers find the going slow and the shelter poor. Nothing crosses here on any schedule.

The Black Shelves.name: The Black Shelves
The Black Shelves.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Black shelves run out under the water, half of this cell sea and half stone, the division between them shifting with the swell rather than sitting still. Pale grit gathers in pockets above the reach of the surf. Nothing green holds anywhere on the rock, and the flat shelf tops are dry enough to land on only where the spray does not carry. Radiant Strait runs bright along the western side, and inland to the east the ground climbs into Ashen Peaks. Joints cross the shelves at close to right angles and split them into rough squares, so walking here is a series of steps over and along rather than any single line.
The Black Shelves.hiddenInfo: The Black Shelves holds standing water in its hollows and no soil worth the name. The route inland is whatever the rock allows.

The Curfew Corridors.name: The Curfew Corridors
The Curfew Corridors.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Blockwork grows denser inward: grey panels four and five storeys tall, joined by enclosed walkways and served by stair towers at the corners. Curfew gates stand across several of the through-routes, their frames set into the building line itself. The through-routes are paved wall to wall and take no daylight at ground level, so what light there is comes from the red fittings. Stair towers are entered from outside, their treads open metal that sounds underfoot. Bare ridges of the Ashen Peaks rise immediately west, and the westernmost structures are built hard against rock with no ground left over. Part of Quilrath.
The Curfew Corridors.hiddenInfo: The Curfew Corridors is the built edge of Quilrath: the same fabric as the city, thinner, and no authored location stands on it. Redline command-lights mark whose ground this is.

The Glass Rise.name: The Glass Rise
The Glass Rise.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Taller frontages appear here, some faced in dark glass that returns the red command-lighting instead of absorbing it. Elevated routes carry between roof levels on fixed spans, and the ground beneath them is paved and kept clear. Drainage channels run the length of each street. The glass is set flush into composite surrounds and the joint lines are the only relief on it. Street level stays shadowed under the spans through most of the day, and the light that reaches it arrives reflected. Quilrath's high building stands close enough east that its lit grids show over the intervening roofs. Part of Quilrath.
The Glass Rise.hiddenInfo: Nothing on The Glass Rise is a destination; travel here arrives at the nearest named site of Quilrath. Redline command-lights mark whose ground this is.

The Black Star Rise.name: The Black Star Rise
The Black Star Rise.basicInfo: [Lv 3-92 · High] Black star-glass rises in close ranks across this ground, the towers gridded with red command-light and inlaid at their upper stages with gold status marking. The Ascendant Keep stands among them, heavier than the rest and set behind its own approaches. Elevated civic routes cross at several levels and checkpoint bridges close the gaps between. Paving underfoot is engineered to swallow footfall, so Quilrath is bright here and very quiet. That paving runs seamless from tower base to tower base, unbroken by kerb or step, and takes the red grid back off the glass. Patrol drones cross overhead without sound. Part of Quilrath.
The Black Star Rise.hiddenInfo: The Inner Circle is beautiful because the suffering has been pushed outward. Movement runs on Access Levels 0 through 9, and access can be lowered after a relative's bad audit, raised to bait someone into a room, or revoked mid-errand so a citizen learns their new standing at a rank gate in front of witnesses. The Red Ledger Intake Office is where the machinery shows a seam: a few citizens in its queue are holding the edge of the disappearing-records scandal that runs to Red Ledger Prime, and none of them are told. Inside the Ascendant Keep, Kaldor Dravon remains fully in command and deliberately permits the succession pressure between Sorin and Vaelen, while the Red War Room holds Ignivex pressure, Dustfall containment and the early shape of off-world routes. Nivarek observes every oath, and the next advancement trial is where someone's loyalty will be quietly lost.

The Glass Threshold.name: The Glass Threshold
The Glass Threshold.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Star-glass frontage holds along part of this ground and gives out along the rest, where grey composite carries the same red lighting at lower intensity. Planted strips run between the two, kept short and squared. Surveillance pylons stand at the street intersections on plain footings. The change of material happens at a straight line across the paving rather than gradually, and the composite side is duller underfoot as well as in the face. Planting sits in flush beds with no raised edge to rest on. Part of Quilrath.
The Glass Threshold.hiddenInfo: The Glass Threshold carries Quilrath's ordinary life outward without any place of its own. Redline command-lights mark whose ground this is.

The Numbered Streets.name: The Numbered Streets
The Numbered Streets.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Frontages here are composite rather than glass, dark-toned and unbroken, the red lines along them dimmer than those showing to the west. Streets meet at right angles and drain to grated channels at the centre. Doors are recessed and numbered. The street surfacing is cambered toward those channels, so the middle of each run is the low ground and stays damp longest after washing. Nothing is fixed to the frontages above door height. Access between blocks passes under fixed spans carrying the upper routes, and the ground beneath those spans is kept clear of anything standing. Part of Quilrath.
The Numbered Streets.hiddenInfo: The Numbered Streets is Quilrath ground by every rule that matters and by no landmark anyone would name. Redline command-lights mark whose ground this is.

The Scrub Margin.name: The Scrub Margin
The Scrub Margin.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Bare ground takes up as much of this cell as building does: grit, low scrub and hard-packed dust between the last composite rows. A patrol road runs the edge, surfaced and kerbed where the structures stop, with marker posts along it at even spacing. Off the road the dust holds tracks and the scrub grows only in the lee of the rows. Light on the open side is plain daylight, and the red fittings on the last frontages read weakly against it. A flier finds level ground on the open side and none at all among the rows. Part of Quilrath.
The Scrub Margin.hiddenInfo: Cross The Scrub Margin to reach Quilrath's real districts; it holds only what the city overflows. Redline command-lights mark whose ground this is.

Way Station Ground.name: Way Station Ground
Way Station Ground.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Headland rock carries the route here, dark and wind-scoured, the surface narrowing where the cliff edge forces it inland and opening again beyond. Sea wind is constant and heavy with salt. Nothing grows on the exposed faces. Underfoot the worked strip is bare stone swept clean by that wind, its patching showing as darker bands across the paler rock. Open Ocean stands off the eastern edge and throws light back up onto the faces. Dustward Edge lies inland to the west, and crews leaving the worked ground that way climb away from the coast almost at once.
Way Station Ground.hiddenInfo: Crews cross Way Station Ground by timing and route variation; nobody holds it and no patrol is dependable. Cover shelters danger as readily as travellers, and an ambush needs story evidence, not assumption.

Curved Vein Water.name: Curved Vein Water
Curved Vein Water.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] White veining runs across a mid-blue surface in long curved lines, the pattern shifting as the swell passes under it. The veins gather and part as the swell passes beneath them and never quite dissolve. The water is darker here than the shallows further north and holds less green. Inland to the west the dry worked ground of the North Route rises. Sky is nearly clear and the light falls hard on a surface that gives little of it back. Wind comes off the land rather than the sea, so the water close in lies flatter than the water out in frame.
Curved Vein Water.hiddenInfo: Curved Vein Water offers no rock, no bar and no rest, and the light off it is the main hazard by midday. Distance is the danger; the sea itself is indifferent.

The Quiet Blue.name: The Quiet Blue
The Quiet Blue.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Quiet blue water with the swell running parallel to the shore and breaking nowhere in the open. The surface holds long shallow undulations with no crests worth the name. The green edge of the Verdant Coast holds the eastern side of the frame. Sky is clear and the light steady. Colour deepens away from the shore in slow stages and never reaches the heavy tone of the outer sea. Air over the water is smoother than the air over the land beside it, so fliers on a long coastal run stay out over the sea and turn in only where they must.
The Quiet Blue.hiddenInfo: The colour of The Quiet Blue says nothing about what lies beneath, and nothing here will catch a tired flier. Wildlife under the surface is possible and rarely seen; bandits do not work water this open.

Deep Swell Water.name: Deep Swell Water
Deep Swell Water.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Deep blue fills the frame, the swell long and unhurried, white only where one crest rolls over another. Nothing stands above the water. A flier here works entirely on held height and remembered heading, because the shore is somewhere east, low and green, and it does not show itself until the crossing is most of the way done. Open Ocean lies west and gives back nothing at all to steer by. The green, when it finally lifts, is the seaward edge of Luminous Forest.
Deep Swell Water.hiddenInfo: Over Deep Swell Water the wind is the only fixed thing, and it changes. Ships bound for the Orbital Gate Station pass far above; nothing else uses this sky.

Saltwind Fringe.name: Saltwind Fringe
Saltwind Fringe.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Salt air reaches well inland across this ground, with dark navy water filling a wide part of the view and the tree cover broken into stands rather than continuous canopy. Surfaced tracks run between them on flat, sandy footing. What glowing growth there is clings to the damper hollows and shows weakly after dusk. Walking the cell means choosing between the shoreward tracks and the rougher ground under the trees. Verdant Coast holds the shore north and west, and the water in view belongs to it. The sandy footing between the stands takes a print and drains fast, so the tracks stay firm while the hollows either side stay damp.
Saltwind Fringe.hiddenInfo: Under the canopy at Saltwind Fringe the going is tracks and roots, and the glow-growth on wet stone does the lighting after dusk. A lost traveller here is found by the streams, which all run somewhere.

Seam-Glow Hollows.name: Seam-Glow Hollows
Seam-Glow Hollows.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Closed canopy returns in patches over ground that rises and falls in short broken steps, with outcrops of bare rock pushing through the leaf litter. Small watercourses cut between them and are easier to follow than to cross. The pale growth threads along the wet ground and the rock faces, giving enough light after dusk to walk by slowly. The Worked Clearing lies south, and the few made tracks in the cell bend that way. The outcrops are rounded and slick where litter has been worn off them, and they carry the tracks over the wet ground better than the ground does.
Seam-Glow Hollows.hiddenInfo: Seam-Glow Hollows is Luminous Forest country: close cover, small watercourses and quiet that carries sound a long way. Foraging is possible for those who know the growth; most do not.

Outcrop Maze.name: Outcrop Maze
Outcrop Maze.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Rock outcrops stand through the forest floor in long low backs, and the trees crowd between them so that the ground ahead is visible only in short stretches. Glowing growth runs in seams along the wet stone and comes up strongly once the light fails. Foot tracks thread the gaps and none of them hold a straight line. Outcrop Maze sits north and The Pale Root Floor south, and the worn routes between the two cross this ground. The rock backs run one way across the cell, so a route taken along them is straightforward and a route taken across them is a series of climbs. Leaf litter lies deep in the troughs between and hides loose stone under it.
Outcrop Maze.hiddenInfo: The tracks through Outcrop Maze are kept open by use and would close within a season without it. The forest hides a camp well and a fire badly.

Tallwood Close.name: Tallwood Close
Tallwood Close.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Tall canopy closes overhead across most of this ground, broken where sandy soil comes to the surface and the trees thin into scrub. Undergrowth is dense at those edges and sparse beneath the full cover. Pale growth spreads over fallen timber and lights the gaps between trunks once the sun is off the canopy. Korrvane — Arena lies north, and the tracks running up to it are wide enough to take loaded traffic and well worn. Where the sandy soil comes up, the trees stand thin enough to see between and the ground is firm and quick; under closed canopy it is soft and slow. Part of Korrvane.
Tallwood Close.hiddenInfo: Tallwood Close is service ground for Korrvane, crossed daily and rarely mentioned. Flight lanes are the roads; walkers take the long way.

The Broken Stands.name: The Broken Stands
The Broken Stands.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Broken forest and worked ground alternate across the cell, the canopy standing in blocks with surfaced tracks and cleared margins running between them. The ground underneath is uneven and stony, and drainage lines cut across it in shallow grooves. Glow appears mainly in those grooves, where the damp holds. The Fringe Water shows north over the low cover, and movement is easier along the cleared lines than under the trees. The drainage grooves run one way down the cell and are shallow enough to cross without slowing, though the stone in them turns underfoot. Cleared margins beside the tracks give a flier a run of level ground at intervals.
The Broken Stands.hiddenInfo: The Broken Stands is walkable, crossable on foot in a day and easier from the air, where the canopy reads as one surface. Cities patrol their own edges and nothing past them.

Saltbreak Edge.name: Saltbreak Edge
Saltbreak Edge.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Gaps in the tree cover open eastward onto water, which holds a narrow but constant part of the view toward Verdant Coast. Most of the ground is cleared or surfaced, with the forest reduced to windbreaks along the tracks. What glows here does so faintly, the growth thinned by exposure and salt. Flight over the cell is straightforward; walking it means keeping to the made tracks, because the open ground between them is churned and soft. The windbreaks stand in single lines and give shelter only directly behind them. Salt reaches the whole of this ground on an onshore wind and shows in the burnt edges of the growth along the eastern margin.
Saltbreak Edge.hiddenInfo: Nothing is built at Saltbreak Edge; the forest here is a thing cities lean on rather than a place they own. The canopy gives no landing; the clearings decide the route.

The Stone Stair.name: The Stone Stair
The Stone Stair.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Swells run in even ranks across open water, bright at the top and dark in the trough, the whole surface in slow continuous motion. There is no rock and no shoal. Forest holds the western side as a flat dark band, and the choice for anyone crossing is whether to make for that band or stay out over water with nothing beneath. The band is Luminous Forest, and behind it the ground carries on out of sight. Radiant Strait lies south and east, its water brighter and its glare stronger, so a crossing made that way trades one kind of tiring for another.
The Stone Stair.hiddenInfo: The Stone Stair is transit air over deep water, crossed rather than visited. A downed traveller is a rescue only if someone saw them go down.

Wide Channel.name: Wide Channel
Wide Channel.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Wind funnels down the channel and holds one direction for most of the day, so traffic runs with it going one way and fights it coming back. The water underneath is bright and lively, its surface scaled with small whitecaps. Neither shore is far, but the middle of the crossing is where a tired flier feels the span, and the air over it gives nothing back. Green ground holds the western rim where the Verdant Coast runs, and black rock the eastern where the Ashen Coast begins, and the two are in sight at once from anywhere over the middle. The whitecaps stand and collapse without travelling, which makes the surface look busier than the swell beneath it is.
Wide Channel.hiddenInfo: Open water with no landing under Wide Channel: a flier who loses a heading here has only the sun to correct it. Nothing here needs story evidence except the weather.

Tiered Surf.name: Tiered Surf
Tiered Surf.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Shelves of dark rock step down into the water in uneven tiers, the surf driving up the gaps between them and falling back white. Sea and stone are closely matched here. The stone is pitted and holds rainwater in the pits long after the sky clears, and walking it means reading which tier is dry and which is only briefly so. Radiant Strait holds the western side, and the ground climbs east into Ashen Peaks. Thin plates of stone lie over the lower tiers and ring flatly under a boot, which gives some warning of where the rock has parted beneath.
Tiered Surf.hiddenInfo: Along Tiered Surf the line between sea and land moves with every set of swell. Starian bandits are not unknown on lonely coast, and cover here shelters them as readily as a traveller.

The Ashring Stacks.name: The Ashring Stacks
The Ashring Stacks.basicInfo: [Lv 2-51 · High] Density increases sharply here, with prefab housing stacked three and four units high and patched across every face in mismatched panel. Part of The Ashrings stands on this ground, its through-routes narrow and gated at the ends. Work-order boards are fixed beside the stair heads. The routes are floored in worn composite with the bedding showing through along the centre lines, and the stacks are tied together by external stair and bolted landing. Rock of the Ashen Peaks stands directly west, and the last row of units backs onto it without a road between. Part of Quilrath.
The Ashring Stacks.hiddenInfo: The Ashrings' defining fact is a gap: surveillance is total at the ring gates and threadbare in the deep rows, because the regime watches movement between rings far more closely than life inside them. Audits weigh family association, so a relative's fall drags a whole household into review; Sedran Vaereth is raising two children under exactly that pressure, furious at Dravon and at the Dustfall cousins whose gang name makes every Vaereth audit worse. When the Accord's Edge wing strikes a Standing Office or a checkpoint, the reprisal audits land here within days, on Archive families as often as anyone. Mirasha Kathvar works the permit desks that process what has already been decided; Rask Venn and Edda Nhalor are on the boards. The Deep Shelves cell is somewhere in Quilrath and nobody has placed it. The next strike brings the next audits.

The Darkened Rows.name: The Darkened Rows
The Darkened Rows.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Prefab rows run in long unbroken lines, their panels of several different ages and none of them matched. Stairs are external and bolted on. Red lighting survives at the street ends and has failed in the middle stretches, leaving the centre of each run unlit. Queue rails stand outside the service points, fixed into the paving, and the ground through the rows is worn to a smooth dark surface. Between rows the gap takes two abreast and no more, and the panel joints are sealed with strip renewed at different times. Landing means the road at a row end, the roofs being strung with fixings. Part of Quilrath.
The Darkened Rows.hiddenInfo: The Darkened Rows is the built edge of Quilrath: the same fabric as the city, thinner, and no authored location stands on it. Rank gates, curfew frames and patrol roads apply here as in the rings.

Gateward Compound.name: Gateward Compound
Gateward Compound.basicInfo: [Lv 3-19 · High] Walled ground takes most of this cell. Nivarek Compound occupies a squared enclosure with its own internal roads and a cleared margin outside the wall, while The Quilrath Gate stands on the through-route as a built structure rather than an opening, with controlled lanes running through it and holding ground either side. Lighting is red and constant. The cleared margin is graded rock kept free of anything that could stand on it, and the holding ground is hard-surfaced and ruled into bays. Wall faces are plain composite above a stone footing. Part of Quilrath.
Gateward Compound.hiddenInfo: Pelna Ostrek's readings on the Quilrath Gate say the next failure may be the last one. Filing that report would end her career; not filing it might end the city's only door to Relstaris. The inspectors enter under escort because the foundations are legacy Contair infrastructure Dravon cannot legally refuse to have examined and cannot afford to lose, and nobody present knows how to build what they maintain. Next door in the Nivarek Compound, Red Ledger Prime holds the files that matter and records are disappearing out of it; the Erased are the same mystery seen from the other end. The Unbroken Accord's Archive believes it has a friend inside this record system and does not know who, and Myrra Nivarek quietly helps people in the intake queues without ever being confirmed as anything more. The gate's next scheduled inspection and the next disappearing file fall in the same tenday.

Bastion Hard.name: Bastion Hard
Bastion Hard.basicInfo: [Lv 4-33 · High] Hard standing dominates: dark composite laid flat over a wide area and ruled with painted lanes and bays. Balrath Bastion Barracks holds the built portion, long low ranges set parallel with vehicle aprons between them. Perimeter lighting is red and fixed at ankle height along the edges of the surfacing. The composite is laid in large squared plates with sealed joints, and the lane paint has been renewed over older marking that still shows through it. Nothing on the open surfacing breaks the wind, which crosses it steadily. Part of Quilrath.
Bastion Hard.hiddenInfo: Everything that makes Quilrath a cage is manufactured in the Balrath Bastion Barracks, which means everything that makes it a cage can be reached here. Gate lockdowns, rank-gate behaviour and surveillance coverage are set from the Inner Wall Control Yards, and one act of sabotage in the Gateworks changes what the Inner Compliance Gate will accept. The Labor Transit Systems Office moves classified conquered-house populations out to the Camp Belt, and the engineers who route those transports know what their work supplies; Lurani Balrath has begun asking about it, which Sennar and Durvan Balrath have noticed. In the Prototype Gate Lab, Namar Balrath's admiration for the Contair technology he is meant to replace shades into illegal study of captured equipment, and it adds no gate. The next transport roster Lurani is asked to sign will show whether her questions have stopped.

The Outer Yards.name: The Outer Yards
The Outer Yards.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Thin building on wide ground: composite ranges set well apart with surfaced yards between them, fenced and gated at the road. Red lights show on the gate posts and nowhere else along the fencing. Ash-grey grit collects along the outward faces of the panels. The yards are bound grit, kerbed and drained to open gullies at their low corners, while outside the fencing the ground is bare rock with dust in its hollows. Sound travels a long way over ground this open and finds little to return it. Part of Quilrath.
The Outer Yards.hiddenInfo: Nothing on The Outer Yards is a destination; travel here arrives at the nearest named site of Quilrath. Rank gates, curfew frames and patrol roads apply here as in the rings.

The Patrol Runs.name: The Patrol Runs
The Patrol Runs.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Patrol roads cross this ground in long surfaced runs, kerbed on both sides and linked by turning loops. Between them stand low composite sheds and chain-linked holding yards on bare rock. Marker posts and barrier frames are set at the junctions. The road surfacing is dark and rolled smooth, and the rock either side sits unlevelled, so leaving the made ground means dropping a step onto broken stone. Shed roofs are flat sheet without parapet, and nothing is lit between the junctions. Part of Quilrath.
The Patrol Runs.hiddenInfo: The Patrol Runs carries Quilrath's ordinary life outward without any place of its own. Rank gates, curfew frames and patrol roads apply here as in the rings.

The Paved Corridor.name: The Paved Corridor
The Paved Corridor.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Cut and fill work shows plainly along this stretch, the route benched into rock too broken to leave alone, with spoil tipped down the seaward side. The surfacing is uneven and patched over older patches. Dust rises off it behind anything moving. The benched face on the inside stands raw and unlined, shedding stone onto the shoulder after any wind. Open Ocean lies east past the spoil, and nothing worked goes down to it. The ground west toward The Outer Yards lifts quickly into harder country and offers no easy parallel line for anyone wanting to avoid the worked one.
The Paved Corridor.hiddenInfo: The Paved Corridor carries freight tracks, dust and the marks of every crew that passed, none of them named. The informal distress custom holds where crews can afford it and not where they cannot.

The Offshore Run.name: The Offshore Run
The Offshore Run.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Offshore of the worked ground where the North Route runs, the water takes a mid-blue tone with white threaded across it in long curving seams. The seams hold a constant angle to the shore and keep their shape for a long way before breaking up. The swell comes down along the coast rather than in from the open sea. Cloud is minimal and the light hard. Light strikes the water and returns mostly from the white, which makes the blue between read darker than it is. Fliers using this water as a line of travel keep the land in sight westward and the smoother air beneath them.
The Offshore Run.hiddenInfo: Nothing marks The Offshore Run but swell; the crossing is made on held height and remembered bearing. Distance is the danger; the sea itself is indifferent.

The Colour Drop.name: The Colour Drop
The Colour Drop.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Seaward of the Verdant Coast the water deepens in colour quickly, going from a lit blue near the shore to something flatter and heavier out in the frame. The change happens over a short span and then holds, so the frame carries two distinct tones with a broad blurred join between them. The swell is long and foam appears only in scattered patches. Light reaches a long way into the outer tone without returning, which is what flattens it. Fliers use that colour change as a rough guide to how far out they have drifted, since it is the only feature the surface reliably shows them.
The Colour Drop.hiddenInfo: The Colour Drop offers no rock, no bar and no rest, and the light off it is the main hazard by midday. Wildlife under the surface is possible and rarely seen; bandits do not work water this open.

Greystone Margin.name: Greystone Margin
Greystone Margin.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Grey rock carries the landward margin, stepped and wet, the swell filling and draining the gaps in it with every set. Most of what lies in view is still water, bright and open. Salt has stripped the stone of everything but the toughest low growth, and the flat tops of the steps are the only reliable place to set down along this stretch. Open Ocean runs west without anything on it, and inland east the ground carries the cover of Luminous Forest. The steps are not of a height with one another, so a walker working up off the water takes them in an uneven scramble and then finds level going above.
Greystone Margin.hiddenInfo: Where Greystone Margin meets the water there is stone to stand on and little else; landings are possible and rarely worth it. A stranded hull or a lost load washes up here before anyone reports it missing.

The Pale Root Floor.name: The Pale Root Floor
The Pale Root Floor.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Heavy canopy runs almost unbroken over this ground, with pale sandy soil showing where roots have lifted the surface or water has stripped it. Undergrowth is thick and low, and the footing beneath it is loose. Streams cut narrow channels that are the only reliable lines through the cell. After dusk the glowing growth stands out along those channels and over the fallen trunks, enough to move by without a lamp. The Pale Root Floor lies west beyond the heavy cover. The channels the streams cut are narrow, steep-sided and firm in the bed, which is why they carry travel where the undergrowth will not.
The Pale Root Floor.hiddenInfo: Cover at The Pale Root Floor is total below the canopy and useless above it. Wildlife is the ordinary hazard; Starian bandits the less ordinary one, and both need story evidence.

Scrub-Thinned Rise.name: Scrub-Thinned Rise
Scrub-Thinned Rise.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Old forest thins through the middle of the cell into scrub and open stony ground, then closes again toward the edges. Streams run shallow over rock and are crossable almost anywhere. Relstaris — Corelight Crown shows south beyond the trees and throws light into the sky long after dusk, which flattens the glow coming off the growth below. Tracks through here run north and south, kept clear by use rather than by work. The open stony ground through the middle carries the tracks cleanly and dries after weather faster than anything under the trees. Streams there run over bare rock with no bank to speak of. Part of Relstaris.
Scrub-Thinned Rise.hiddenInfo: Cross Scrub-Thinned Rise to reach Relstaris's real districts; it holds only what the city overflows. The capital's edge, not its outskirts.

The Open Stands.name: The Open Stands
The Open Stands.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Sandy ground carries the forest in open stands rather than closed canopy, the trees spaced enough for light to reach the floor and the undergrowth to thicken. Radiant Strait lies east and its brightness comes through the gaps all day. Small watercourses run toward it across easy gradients. The glowing growth is low and patchy on this soil, and a flier crossing after dusk picks out the strait well before the ground beneath resolves. The spacing of the trees lets wind through at ground level, which keeps the floor dry and the sandy soil loose. Watercourses run in shallow scrapes rather than cut beds and are crossed without a step out of stride.
The Open Stands.hiddenInfo: Under the canopy at The Open Stands the going is tracks and roots, and the glow-growth on wet stone does the lighting after dusk. Foraging is possible for those who know the growth; most do not.

The Still Water.name: The Still Water
The Still Water.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Full open water, hard lit, reading shallow even where it is not, so its colour tells a flier nothing about what lies beneath. The eastern rim shows as one unbroken dark band of the Ashen Coast. Air over the middle warms and rises by midday, which makes the outbound crossing easier than the return, and there is no resting place between the two shores. Under the hard light the swell shows as a slow change in brightness rather than as shape, and a flier judging height off it is working from very little. The wind holds along the channel and carries a fine salt haze with it that dulls the far rim by the middle of the day.
The Still Water.hiddenInfo: The colour of The Still Water says nothing about what lies beneath, and nothing here will catch a tired flier. Ships bound for the Orbital Gate Station pass far above; nothing else uses this sky.

The Sea Stacks.name: The Sea Stacks
The Sea Stacks.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Stacks stand off the shore in a loose scatter, black and squared off by the sea, with heavy navy water working between them. The land side is bare flow rock, without soil or shelter of any kind. Surf hits hard and rebounds off the stacks so the water between never settles, and the only quiet ground is the flat above the splash line. Radiant Strait lies west beyond the stacks, and the stripped ground of the Ashen Wastes runs inland to the east. Air between the stacks is broken and unreliable, lifting on one side and dropping on the other, so fliers hold above rather than thread the gaps.
The Sea Stacks.hiddenInfo: The Sea Stacks is a margin rather than a place: salt, rock and the swell working at both. Nothing crosses here on any schedule.

The Camp Line.name: The Camp Line
The Camp Line.basicInfo: [Lv 2-10 · High] Camp construction fills this ground: modular units set in ruled blocks on graded rock, with service runs laid on the surface rather than buried. Part of The Camp Belt stands here, its lanes numbered on painted boards at each corner. Lighting is pole-mounted and white rather than red, spaced to leave no dark ground between. The lanes are graded rock rolled hard, and the service runs cross them in covered trays that have to be stepped over. Unit walls are thin enough to pass sound out into the lanes. Graded rock shows through wherever a tray has been lifted and reset. Part of Quilrath.
The Camp Line.hiddenInfo: No single House governs the Camp Belt and none is invented: classification is Nivarek's, the labour transit system is Balrath's, and the work orders, allotments and clinic coordination are Kathvar's, which means a family can be crushed by three offices none of which considers itself responsible. Maru Sorn keeps the old survey route-songs alive as work rhythms, and the Archive knows every verse is a map; lately the verses are reaching them incomplete, because someone in the camps is editing them, and the next crew release will carry another edited verse out. The residents are not uniformly exhausted or rebellious, and the Erased are not a camp population: erasure is removal from the records, and the people here are still on the ladder.

The Faded Blocks.name: The Faded Blocks
The Faded Blocks.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Modular blocks continue across this cell in the same ruled arrangement, the units older, their panels faded and repaired in flat patches of a different grey. Standpipes and service points stand at the block ends with rails around them. Roads between the blocks are graded rather than surfaced and hold deep ruts. Water standing in those ruts dries to a pale crust that breaks underfoot. Pole lighting reaches the road centres and leaves the ground against the units in shadow. Part of Quilrath.
The Faded Blocks.hiddenInfo: The Faded Blocks is service ground for Quilrath, crossed daily and rarely mentioned. Rank gates, curfew frames and patrol roads apply here as in the rings.

Southreach Edge.name: Southreach Edge
Southreach Edge.basicInfo: [Lv 7-55 · Severe] Dense prefab and modular building fills the northern half of this ground, packed until the gaps between blocks take one person at a time, with power and water runs carried overhead on brackets. South of the last row the surfacing stops and open rock begins. Part of The Southreach lies out on that rock, where the lanes leaving the blocks become patrol roads and the ground stops being built at all. The brackets are bolted through panel into frame and sag between fixings. Underfoot the packed ground is polished in the gaps and loose everywhere else. Landing space is a few cleared squares marked on roof decks. Part of Quilrath.
Southreach Edge.hiddenInfo: Beneath the patrols run the escape lines south. The Quiet Mile is a stretch of the Southreach where the patrol schedule has been quietly purchasable for years and the Archive's routes use it, a standing arrangement rather than a guarantee, and a new officer or a trap would look identical until someone walked it. Cadi Selm guides families through carrying Archive copies as memorised fragments and has never seen Dustfall in daylight. Beyond the Quiet Mile lies the Accord's Dustfall-facing outpost, the Handoff, which is neither Dustfall nor a headquarters. Competing Dravon and Ignivex claims on the shared route exceed what either can control, and skirmishes keep regular patrol off it without removing a single checkpoint here. The next purchased schedule is due, and whether it is still honest is the question Cadi must answer with a family behind her.

The Boundary Line.name: The Boundary Line
The Boundary Line.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Patched housing runs to the edge of the built ground and stops at a made road that follows the boundary without crossing it. Panels are of several colours, none of them original, and the fixings show. Gates stand across the lane ends, hinged and frame-mounted. The road is kerbed on the built side only and its surfacing tapers into rock along the outer edge. Lane floors are packed dirt over old plate, banked against the plate wherever it has lifted. Beyond the road the rock of Ashen Wastes is bare and unlevelled, and chain-linked posts follow the edge at regular spacing. Part of Quilrath.
The Boundary Line.hiddenInfo: The Boundary Line is the built edge of Quilrath: the same fabric as the city, thinner, and no authored location stands on it. Surveillance is total at the gates and thin between them.

Freight Staging.name: Freight Staging
Freight Staging.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Drifted sand lies across the worked surface in this stretch and no one has cleared it, so the route reads as a paler band through dark rock rather than a made thing. Shoulders are soft. The wind refills whatever traffic scours out. The sand is shallow enough that the compacted ground beneath it can be felt through a boot but not seen. Open Ocean stands past the eastern rock and the wind arrives off it steadily. Movement is straightforward and slow, and the firm line gets judged by where the last wheels went rather than by any surviving edge.
Freight Staging.hiddenInfo: The worked line through Freight Staging belongs to the North Route toward Dustfall: made, patched, unmaintained. Redline sweeps from Quilrath reach this far on no schedule, and Accord runners time the gaps.

The Dark Swells.name: The Dark Swells
The Dark Swells.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Navy water, dark and slow, lifting in heavy swells that show almost no white on them. The swells run wide apart and pass with a long interval between them. The colour takes light in rather than giving it back. Inland westward the dry ground of the North Route carries its freight. Light falls straight into the surface and nothing comes back from below it, so the sea shows shape only where a crest turns an edge to the sun. Air over this sea is cooler than the air over the land, and the boundary between the two is felt as a distinct change when a flier crosses it.
The Dark Swells.hiddenInfo: Over The Dark Swells the wind is the only fixed thing, and it changes. A downed traveller is a rescue only if someone saw them go down.

Bright Coast Run.name: Bright Coast Run
Bright Coast Run.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Along this stretch the sea holds an even bright blue, worked into low crests by a wind running down the line of the coast. The crests are small and regular and carry white only on the steepest of them. The Verdant Coast edges the frame to the east, green and continuous. Cloud is negligible and the light hard. Wind holds its direction without varying, which keeps the surface uniform from one edge of the frame to the other. Fliers on this line have ground within reach on one side and nothing at all on the other, which settles most route choices.
Bright Coast Run.hiddenInfo: Bright Coast Run is transit air over deep water, crossed rather than visited. Weather arrives from the open quarter with little warning and no shelter.

The Low Shelf.name: The Low Shelf
The Low Shelf.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Stone and water share this ground about evenly, a low shelf of pale rock running out into mid-blue swell that veins white as it turns. Growth is sparse and wind-flattened where it holds at all. Worked country begins a little inland, and the tracks that serve it come down to the shelf in places but do not follow the water for long. That worked country is Solvraxis Outskirts, and Open Ocean holds the whole of the western view beyond the shelf. Parallel channels are cut into the pale rock at intervals, filling on each set and draining slowly enough that they stay part full between, so a crossing on foot is a matter of stepping over rather than around. Part of Solvraxis.
The Low Shelf.hiddenInfo: Nothing on The Low Shelf is a destination; travel here arrives at the nearest named site of Solvraxis. Weapons are unlawful here as everywhere in the city.

Corelight Crown.name: Corelight Crown
Corelight Crown.basicInfo: [Lv 2-98 · Low] The Citadel rises over this ground in stacked star-glass, and the Relstaris Core housed beneath it makes the light: white at the centre, going gold through the layers above, so the structure is lit from inside rather than from overhead. That intensity shifts through the day, and work periods and evening activity are read off the shifts. Public flight corridors converge here at several levels. Paving around the base is laid in wide plates that take the light up and hold it, and the glass faces above return a second, weaker version of it onto the walkways. Landing ground is on the upper terraces, not at street level. Part of Relstaris.
Corelight Crown.hiddenInfo: Nearly everything decided in the Citadel is decided before it is announced. The Advisor Review Office has open work on conflicts of interest inside the administrative floors, which is why some advisors have become conspicuously cooperative, and Kaelis Morven, Brenn Ordan and Maris Othrel are among the staff whose cooperation is being read. Below, routing decisions on the Core Control Platform determine which districts feel a shortage first, and those decisions have repeatedly been leaned on for political reasons that never appear in the log; Talris Contair monitors the interfaces without authority over the machine. Long-serving maintenance crews know passages the current security model does not account for. Darkstar Castro holds the Core, and the next demand cycle will show which district is being made to wait.

The Deep Shade.name: The Deep Shade
The Deep Shade.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Deep shade holds this ground even at midday, the canopy layered and the undergrowth beneath it sparse for want of light. Little has been cleared and less has been surfaced, so the ways through are foot tracks that follow the easiest gradients. The glowing growth is at its most visible where the dark is deepest, in sheets across rock and root. The House Precincts lies south and Relstaris — Corelight Crown west, both close enough that the tracks carry steady foot traffic. The foot tracks are narrow and worn to bare earth, and they follow the lie of the ground rather than any line laid out for them. Part of Relstaris.
The Deep Shade.hiddenInfo: The Deep Shade is Relstaris ground by every rule that matters and by no landmark anyone would name. Corelight reaches it thinly and the city's rules reach it fully.

Salt-Bitten Shore.name: Salt-Bitten Shore
Salt-Bitten Shore.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Low shore, more water than land, with a thin strip of rock and salt-bitten green holding the western edge against a swell that arrives steadily and without much force. Light comes off the surface hard through the middle of the day. A flier can put down on the strip, but it narrows and widens without warning and offers no cover once the wind rises. Behind the strip the ground rises into Luminous Forest, and the brighter water of Radiant Strait lies north and east of the swell running here. Close in, the sea passes over a pale bottom and reads green rather than blue for a short way out from the rock.
Salt-Bitten Shore.hiddenInfo: Fliers use Salt-Bitten Shore as a coast mark; walkers find the going slow and the shelter poor. The route inland is whatever the rock allows.

The Long Crossing.name: The Long Crossing
The Long Crossing.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Sunlight stands almost straight down on this reach near midday, and the water answers with a flat white shine that hides everything under the surface. Colour returns at the ends of the day, turquoise near the rims and stronger blue in the middle. Crossings are timed around that glare as much as around the wind, since a flier working into it loses the far shore entirely. The green rim of the Verdant Coast holds the western side and the black rock of the Ashen Coast the eastern, and through the middle of the day both go to flat silhouette. The surface breaks nowhere across the width of the cell.
The Long Crossing.hiddenInfo: Open water with no landing under The Long Crossing: a flier who loses a heading here has only the sun to correct it. Distance is the danger; the sea itself is indifferent.

Basalt Drop.name: Basalt Drop
Basalt Drop.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Basalt takes most of this cell, a dark broken plain running to an edge where it simply stops and drops into the sea. No vegetation interrupts it. The water below is narrow in view but loud, forcing into cracks in the rock and coming back out under pressure, and the level ground well back from the edge is where anyone arriving by air sets down. Radiant Strait holds the water to the west, and the Ashen Wastes carry the ground inland east. The plain is fractured into rough polygons, each one loose in its seat, and a stride across them is a series of small tilts rather than a level walk.
Basalt Drop.hiddenInfo: Basalt Drop is Ashen Wastes country, where the horizon repeats itself and a heading is hard to keep. Wildlife is scarce and what survives here is not gentle.

Spine Channels.name: Spine Channels
Spine Channels.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Spines of dark rock run in rough parallel here, split by narrow ash-floored channels that wander rather than lead anywhere. The stone is sharp along the edges and dulled on the flats by blown grit. Heat holds in the channels long after the wind has cleared the tops. Channel floors are soft deep ash that takes a print and keeps it out of the wind, while the spines above them are bare and swept. A flier crossing reads the grain at once, the channels showing as darker seams in the rock. Ashen Coast lies west past the last of the rock.
Spine Channels.hiddenInfo: Glare off the bleached stone at Spine Channels is severe; dust rises with the afternoon wind and sits in the hollows. Nothing here is patrolled, maintained or mapped.

Scoured Plateau.name: Scoured Plateau
Scoured Plateau.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Grey-black rock, scoured level by wind and stripped of everything light enough to move, stretches away under a hard sky. Ash sits only where the ground dips. Sound carries a long way across it and there is little to stop the eye. The surface is gritty and sound underfoot, cracked into wide irregular plates with the cracks swept clean of anything loose. Nothing casts a shadow long enough to stand in. Landing is possible anywhere the plates run true, which is most of this ground.
Scoured Plateau.hiddenInfo: The crust at Scoured Plateau rings differently over old voids, and the sound is the only warning. Water is whatever a traveller carried in.

The Dark Sheets.name: The Dark Sheets
The Dark Sheets.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Flat sheet rock covers most of this ground, dark, unbroken and empty, with only shallow steps where one flow ended and another ran over it. Nothing grows and nothing holds water. Wind moves ash across the surface in thin travelling sheets that erase a track before it can set. The steps are low enough to cross without breaking stride and are the only feature on this ground to take a bearing from. A flier loses all sense of speed over a surface this uniform. Underfoot the sheet is hard, faintly gritty and warm through the sole of a boot.
The Dark Sheets.hiddenInfo: The Dark Sheets is old flow and ash: sharp underfoot, hot by afternoon and empty of anything living. Cover here shelters danger as readily as travellers; Starian bandits use it, given story evidence.

The Hollow Crust.name: The Hollow Crust
The Hollow Crust.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Long low swells of ash-pale rock run across this country, so uniform that a heading is hard to keep without something fixed on the horizon. The crust is thin over older voids in places and rings differently underfoot. Light is flat and nearly shadowless near midday. Where the crust has failed the holes are small, sharp-edged and easy to miss until a foot is in one. Air between the swells stays still enough that dust raised at a step hangs where it was raised.
The Hollow Crust.hiddenInfo: Nothing grows at The Hollow Crust; the ground takes heat in and gives it back after dark. Ignivex patrols and Dravon incursions both cross this ground and neither holds it.

The Collapsed Tubes.name: The Collapsed Tubes
The Collapsed Tubes.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Collapsed tubes open along this ground as long trenches with broken roofs, their floors littered with fallen slabs and drifted ash. They offer real shade and a way out of the wind. They also cut across a line of travel without warning and must be worked around or dropped into. Roof remnants span them at intervals, so the light inside comes in bars and the floor alternates glare and dark. Getting down is a scramble over fallen slab and getting out asks the same at the far end.
The Collapsed Tubes.hiddenInfo: The fissures and tubes of The Collapsed Tubes give real shade and real drops, and cut across any line of travel. Wildlife is scarce and what survives here is not gentle.

Clinker Fields.name: Clinker Fields
Clinker Fields.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Rubble fields of clinkered black stone fill the middle of this ground, loose, angular and slow to cross, with smoother flow tops standing above them like islands. Ash powders everything a shade lighter than it is. Nothing breaks the heat. The clinker turns underfoot where it does not grind, and it makes enough noise doing either to carry across open ground. Flow tops are firm, swept and small. Ash lifted off the rubble hangs low and settles again where it came from. Routes across favour the flow tops, linked where they nearly touch, and the rubble between them gets crossed only where there is no alternative.
Clinker Fields.hiddenInfo: Clinker Fields is Ashen Wastes country, where the horizon repeats itself and a heading is hard to keep. Nothing here is patrolled, maintained or mapped.

Worn Freight Ground.name: Worn Freight Ground
Worn Freight Ground.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Worn pale rock takes up most of this ground, close enough to the freight country eastward that crossing traffic has polished lines into it. Ash has been swept out of the shallow seams by use and wind together. The stone holds heat and gives it back well into the evening. Underfoot it is smooth and fine-grained, giving little purchase along the polished stretches. Those polished lines run darker than the rock around them and stay visible when nothing else marks a way across. Ground this open offers no cover worth the name at any hour of the day.
Worn Freight Ground.hiddenInfo: Worn Freight Ground is corridor ground, one stretch of the functional sequence between the Quiet Mile, the Handoff and the North Routehead. Cover shelters danger as readily as travellers, and an ambush needs story evidence, not assumption.

The Ashen Turn.name: The Ashen Turn
The Ashen Turn.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Rock country closes in on both sides here, grey and featureless, with the worked line holding a level grade through it. The surface is sound down the centre and crumbling at the margins. Heat collects between the walls wherever the cut runs deepest. There is no room to come down beside the line and no reason to, the grade being the only level ground. The walls are cut rock left rough, and stone off them lies along the margins where it has come down. Sound between them returns hard and close, so anything on the line is heard well before it is seen.
The Ashen Turn.hiddenInfo: Crews cross The Ashen Turn by timing and route variation; nobody holds it and no patrol is dependable. The informal distress custom holds where crews can afford it and not where they cannot.

The Dense Still.name: The Dense Still
The Dense Still.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Dense dark water with very little surface movement, the swells long and low and the colour close to black in the troughs. Southward the shoreline turns to the broken rock of the Ashen Coast. The rock along that southern edge is darker than the sea, and the two run together where they meet. The North Route lies inland to the west. Air above is still and carries no haze, so the horizon stays sharp even where the water gives nothing. Light does not carry into this sea at all, and from height the surface reads as a single flat plane with no texture in it.
The Dense Still.hiddenInfo: Nothing marks The Dense Still but swell; the crossing is made on held height and remembered bearing. Wildlife under the surface is possible and rarely seen; bandits do not work water this open.

Veined Water.name: Veined Water
Veined Water.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Veins of white lie across mid-blue water in long trailing lines, marking where the swell has broken and not yet dispersed. The lines lie roughly parallel and are slowly drawn out by the movement of the water until they thin to nothing. The colour is neither the pale inshore tone nor the heavy outer one. The Verdant Coast runs along the eastern edge of the frame. Sky is clear and the light falls evenly, picking out the white and leaving the blue as a single flat tone. Wind is moderate and consistent, and a flier can hold a heading here for a long stretch without needing to correct.
Veined Water.hiddenInfo: Veined Water offers no rock, no bar and no rest, and the light off it is the main hazard by midday. Ships bound for the Orbital Gate Station pass far above; nothing else uses this sky.

Pale Inshore.name: Pale Inshore
Pale Inshore.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Pale blue-green water lies over the inshore ground here, brighter than the open sea beyond it, with a low broken margin of rock and a little coarse sand between the two. Wind runs along the shore rather than into it. The green inland is close enough that leaf shape reads from the air, and the ground between it and the water is walkable in both directions. That inland green is the seaward margin of Luminous Forest, and westward past the bright inshore water the darker surface of Open Ocean takes over. The change between them is one hard line where the ground beneath falls away, plain from the air and invisible from the shore.
Pale Inshore.hiddenInfo: Pale Inshore holds standing water in its hollows and no soil worth the name. Starian bandits are not unknown on lonely coast, and cover here shelters them as readily as a traveller.

Glowroot Deep.name: Glowroot Deep
Glowroot Deep.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Unbroken forest covers nearly the whole cell, bright green from above and close to black beneath, with sandy soil showing in the few gaps where the canopy fails. The ground is broken by low outcrops rather than by any real gradient. Few tracks cross it and those that do are narrow and overgrown at the edges. The glowing growth is thick here and lights the forest floor well enough that moving after dusk needs no lamp. Solvraxis Outskirts lies north past the cover and Verdant Coast holds the shore west. The low outcrops are scattered rather than aligned and the tracks bend round them, which is why nothing in the cell runs straight. Part of Solvraxis.
Glowroot Deep.hiddenInfo: Cross Glowroot Deep to reach Solvraxis's real districts; it holds only what the city overflows. Weapons are unlawful here as everywhere in the city.

The Worked Corridor.name: The Worked Corridor
The Worked Corridor.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Standing forest fills most of the view, cut by a worked corridor running up toward The Stream Channels that is the widest made thing in the cell. Water shows in the north of the frame and the ground falls gently that way. Beneath the canopy the undergrowth is dense and the footing root-bound. Glow rises off the growth on the corridor's shaded verges, so the line of the route stays readable long after the light has gone. The corridor is cut wide and kept clear to its edges, and its surface is firm where the ground either side is root-bound and slow.
The Worked Corridor.hiddenInfo: The tracks through The Worked Corridor are kept open by use and would close within a season without it. Cities patrol their own edges and nothing past them.

Sandy Root Floor.name: Sandy Root Floor
Sandy Root Floor.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Pale sandy soil underlies this stretch of forest and shows through wherever traffic or water has worn the surface. The canopy is moderate rather than closed, and enough light reaches the floor to keep the undergrowth thick. Tracks run east toward Academy Quarter and are the easiest going in the cell. The glowing growth spreads flat across the ground here instead of climbing, so after dusk the worn paths read as dark lines through a lit floor. The tracks running east are worn wide and shallow rather than cut, and they carry traffic in both directions at most hours.
Sandy Root Floor.hiddenInfo: Sandy Root Floor is walkable, crossable on foot in a day and easier from the air, where the canopy reads as one surface. The canopy gives no landing; the clearings decide the route.

Academy Quarter.name: Academy Quarter
Academy Quarter.basicInfo: [Lv 3-66 · Low] Campus ground, dense and low-walled. Relstaris Academy Central Campus sits at the middle with the Research and Applied Sciences, Affinity and Combat, and Civic, Cultural and Professional campuses set around it, pale green-white star-glass standing on older star-metal footings. Academy Commons opens between them as continuous paved ground, the Academy Residential City stacking vertically at one side. The Open Circuit is marked overhead and carries steady low flight. The walls run waist-high as boundaries rather than barriers, so a walker crosses from one campus onto the next without a gate. Part of Relstaris.
Academy Quarter.hiddenInfo: Every major house works the Academy and none controls it, which is why the pressure never stops. A celebrated legacy applicant has been outscored by an unknown examinee with no sponsor, and the review has already left the Admissions Court for the Faculty Council; a separate cheating finding ended a prodigy's reputation in an afternoon and the appeal is turning political because the student's house will argue Republic interference. On the combat campus a house instructor is weighing an offer that would cost a rival student a ranking, one student is hiding an injury from the Recovery and Return Wing, and bookmakers keep finding the observation gallery; Aurex and Auria Genesis, Jorrix Corsair and Saren Valcoro teach across those lines. A junior scholar's discovery is being reframed as a sponsor's own. The Faculty Council sits before term's end.

Forum Heights.name: Forum Heights
Forum Heights.basicInfo: [Lv 3-75 · Low] Monumental construction on every side, silver-white star-glass inlaid with deep blue, the Starian Republic Forum and Civic Commons opening as paving broad enough to see across. The Living Archive and the Public Protection District front the same ground. High Relstaris goes up above all of it in suspended tiers linked by bridges that carry walkers where there is no floor. Nothing grows in this part of Relstaris City. Corelight reaches it plainly and flight corridors run at several heights at once. The paving is slab-laid over older star-metal that shows along the seams, and sound crossing the open squares arrives flattened and late. Part of Relstaris.
Forum Heights.hiddenInfo: The Forum is where the Republic's failures surface first. Dravon's delegation runs a sustained legal campaign against Castro legitimacy, arguing civic failures rather than accusations it cannot document, and each genuine service collapse strengthens the next filing; Elyra Varriko watches the Representative Dining Court produce more binding agreements than the Speaking Floor. Minor houses are using the Petition Season Pavilion to force recognition the major seats keep deferring. In the Living Archive, Daelor Ravello's colleagues keep finding that the ancient Sol holder mattered more than public education admits. Up in High Relstaris the Signal Anomaly Room is working transmissions nobody can classify, and residents are pressing to close the overlooks; Yven Aevon has the Republic objection before petition season ends.

The House Precincts.name: The House Precincts
The House Precincts.basicInfo: [Lv 3-69 · Low] Walled grounds rather than streets: the Castro, Contair, Corsair, Dravon and Volen compounds each keep their own block, each built and lit to its own colours, so no two frontages along the Grand House Concourse match. The Genesis Embassy holds a separate plot. Planted open land lies between them and forest stands beyond the eastern edge. The Concourse runs as one continuous paved strip with every wall set back from it, and what lies between the compounds is grass, gravel and planting rather than building. Approach from the air is direct and lands inside the walls; the Concourse itself is walkable from end to end. Part of Relstaris.
The House Precincts.hiddenInfo: The Concourse's neutrality is maintained by effort, and the effort is being tested from six directions at once. Inside the Dravon Compound, Cassor Dravon runs Kaldor's campaign against Castro legitimacy as law and public argument, and the Quiet Defection Room holds a list that loyalists and hostile outsiders would both act on if it escaped. Varis Contair's Systems Audit Hall can order unsafe infrastructure shut down, and the Independent Failure Archive records every warning the Republic postponed for political reasons. Lucan Castro and Mariel Valcoro manage a Secure Citadel Transit whose log is genuinely sensitive. Tyra Volen's Ember Terrace remembrance names causes the Dravon delegation disputes in public, and Decimus Genesis's Emergency Muster Deck moves before the Republic asks. The next delegation arrival is choreographed so that none of them meet.

Windgrass Point.name: Windgrass Point
Windgrass Point.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Green runs almost to the salt on this side, low wind-shaped growth thinning as it nears the rock and giving out in the last stretch before the surf. Water still holds the greater part of the cell, mid-blue and veined. The House Precincts lies inland behind the growth, and the ground between is even enough that fliers use it in preference to the rock. Eastward the water runs into Radiant Strait and brightens as it goes. The even ground is a firm sandy tread that takes a print cleanly and keeps it until the next weather, so past traffic stays legible across the whole of it.
Windgrass Point.hiddenInfo: Along Windgrass Point the line between sea and land moves with every set of swell. Wildlife works the tideline; a careless camp attracts it.

Shallowbank Reach.name: Shallowbank Reach
Shallowbank Reach.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Shallow banks reach out from both rims into the channel and show plainly from the air as pale green-blue patches inside the deeper blue. The water over them is loud in any weather, breaking white with no shore to break on. Fliers use those patches as waypoints down the length of the strait, and anything on the surface gives them a wide margin. Those rims are the Verdant Coast to the west and the Ashen Coast to the east, and the banks reaching out from each are the same pale colour whatever the ground behind them is. Water over them is loud enough to be heard from a height, which gives them away before the colour does under cloud.
Shallowbank Reach.hiddenInfo: The colour of Shallowbank Reach says nothing about what lies beneath, and nothing here will catch a tired flier. A downed traveller is a rescue only if someone saw them go down.

Spurstone Shore.name: Spurstone Shore
Spurstone Shore.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Spurs of dark stone reach out into the water at intervals, each ending in rubble that the swell moves around rather than over. About half of what lies here is sea. Grit and shattered rock fill the bays between the spurs, walkable but slow, and the spur tops carry a route along the coast for anyone willing to climb down and up again. Radiant Strait holds the water off this shore, and the Ashen Wastes stand inland behind the spurs. Each spur falls from its root toward its tip, so the coastal route runs downhill, along and up again at every crossing and never holds a level for long.
Spurstone Shore.hiddenInfo: Where Spurstone Shore meets the water there is stone to stand on and little else; landings are possible and rarely worth it. The nearest help is the nearest city, and it is not close.

Broken Lava Country.name: Broken Lava Country
Broken Lava Country.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Broken lava country, all of it bare: slabs tilted against one another, fissures too wide to step and too narrow to be useful, ash banked in the shade. Fissure walls show the layered edges of successive flows. No plant survives on it. The surface rings hollow in places where a tube has collapsed and left a thin roof, so weight goes where the rock is visibly continuous, and a route across becomes a sequence of small decisions rather than a heading. Slab edges are knife-cut where they have snapped and rounded where the wind has had them longer. Ashen Coast lies west past the broken ground.
Broken Lava Country.hiddenInfo: Glare off the bleached stone at Broken Lava Country is severe; dust rises with the afternoon wind and sits in the hollows. Water is whatever a traveller carried in.

Bleached Stone Waste.name: Bleached Stone Waste
Bleached Stone Waste.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Bleached stone dominates this stretch, old black surfaces weathered to a dull pale grey that throws the light straight back. Heat comes off it through the middle of the day and shimmers the horizon out of shape. Ash drifts sit in the lee of every low spine. The drifts are soft, fine and warm, and they fill a boot print as it is made. The stone is friable at the surface and powders under a boot, leaving a print that the next wind takes away. Nothing stands high enough on this ground to serve as a mark from any distance.
Bleached Stone Waste.hiddenInfo: The crust at Bleached Stone Waste rings differently over old voids, and the sound is the only warning. Smuggling crews working around Ignivex's eastern mountains cut through ground like this by timing and local knowledge.

Deep Interior Waste.name: Deep Interior Waste
Deep Interior Waste.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Deep interior waste: black rock in ridges and spines with ash banked between them, and no mark of anything living on any of it. The horizon repeats itself in every direction. Wind picks up through the afternoon and drives dust along the hollows. The air tastes of dry mineral grit and carries nothing else. The ridges run without pattern, and the ash between them lies deep, soft and level enough to walk quickly on until it shelves away underfoot. Light off the black rock is poor, and a shape at a distance stays a shape.
Deep Interior Waste.hiddenInfo: Deep Interior Waste is old flow and ash: sharp underfoot, hot by afternoon and empty of anything living. Ignivex patrols and Dravon incursions both cross this ground and neither holds it.

Black Heart Waste.name: Black Heart Waste
Black Heart Waste.basicInfo: [Transit · Severe] Black almost without relief, this is the darkest ground in the interior waste: fresh-looking flows, unweathered, taking the light in rather than returning it. Heat builds on the surface until the air above it moves. Ash is sparse, scoured off by wind that meets nothing to slow it. Heat comes up through boot leather from the rock itself rather than off the air above it, and the surface is loud underfoot wherever the glass breaks. The flow surface is glassy in patches and breaks through to rough rock at the edge of every patch. Nothing standing on it throws a shadow worth using.
Black Heart Waste.hiddenInfo: Black Heart Waste is the darkest ground in the interior: fresh unweathered flow that drinks the light and builds heat until the air above it moves. A heading is lost in minutes here, and no crew works it by choice.

The Bleached Plates.name: The Bleached Plates
The Bleached Plates.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Wide bleached plates of stone lie edge to edge here, their joints packed with grey dust, the whole surface throwing back a hard uniform light. Heat shimmer sits over it from mid-morning onward. There is no shade of any kind and no relief in the shape of the ground. The plates are level enough to run a wheel across and dished very slightly, so the dust in the joints stays where it settles. A flier comes down anywhere on them without trouble and gains nothing by it.
The Bleached Plates.hiddenInfo: The fissures and tubes of The Bleached Plates give real shade and real drops, and cut across any line of travel. Nothing here is patrolled, maintained or mapped.

Ashhollow Ribs.name: Ashhollow Ribs
Ashhollow Ribs.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Shallow ash hollows pock this ground between ribs of dark rock, deep enough in places to swallow a standing figure. The dust in them is fine and moves at a touch. The ribs run in no useful direction. Rib stone is banded pale and dark where the weather has cut into it, and the banding runs on unbroken from one rib to the next. Hollow floors give to the ankle and throw up dust that hangs in still air behind anyone crossing. The ribs are hard, sharp-backed and warm, and they carry sound further than the hollows do.
Ashhollow Ribs.hiddenInfo: Ashhollow Ribs is Ashen Wastes country, where the horizon repeats itself and a heading is hard to keep. Water is whatever a traveller carried in.

The Tilted Slabs.name: The Tilted Slabs
The Tilted Slabs.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Tilted slabs and short drops make this ground awkward rather than hard, with a step down or a scramble up asked for constantly. Ash collects at the foot of each face. The drops are shallow enough to take at a stride and frequent enough to make the whole crossing a matter of small commitments. The rock is dark where it is fresh and grey where it is old, often within the same slab.
