The faces are low but continuous, so a line that looks open from one slab top turns out to be broken from the next. Nothing on this ground is level enough to make good landing.
The Tilted Slabs.hiddenInfo: Glare off the bleached stone at The Tilted Slabs is severe; dust rises with the afternoon wind and sits in the hollows. Smuggling crews working around Ignivex's eastern mountains cut through ground like this by timing and local knowledge.

Route's End Station.name: Route's End Station
Route's End Station.basicInfo: [Lv 10-35 · High] Packed ground and worked stone widen out on this part of the corridor, where a mixed support settlement sits off the line with maintained storage, repair space and somewhere to sleep. Its walls carry patches from several eras of building. Traffic slows through and then moves on. The Handoff stands on this ground, its yard hard-surfaced and swept, its buildings low and set with their backs to the prevailing wind. Work lamps on the yard corners carry the light once the day has gone. What the place offers is bounded, and crews arriving plan around that rather than assuming more of it.
Route's End Station.hiddenInfo: The Handoff's central argument is how to remain useful without letting usefulness become ownership, and every delay here becomes somebody else's washing, repair, meal or missed sleep. Both Archive and Edge people receive help and neither wing commands the other; the place is no headquarters, holds no corridor territory and keeps no master registry of protected people or cells. Care is given by clinical need rather than usefulness, which regularly puts a wounded Edge fighter and a frightened escapee in the same room. A dissenting resident is not expelled, recruited or classified. Funding is donations, purchased services, household contributions and paid supply contracts. Right now guests are staying longer than expected, two crews are overdue from the Dustfall side, and a donor has attached terms to the next supply run that the Bench has not yet accepted or refused.

Lava Rock Coast.name: Lava Rock Coast
Lava Rock Coast.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Lava rock forms the whole of the landward part, dark and low, meeting deep navy water along a line of broken stone that takes the swell without giving anything back. There is no sand and no growth. A worked road runs somewhere inland of the rock, and the stone between that road and the water crosses on foot easily enough while offering nothing against the wind. That road is The North Route, and northward the water opens into Open Ocean. Patches of the flow have set glassy and throw the light back in hard flat sheets that make the surface difficult to read from above.
Lava Rock Coast.hiddenInfo: The shore at Lava Rock Coast is walkable at the cost of wet footing, and the surf covers the sound of anything approaching. Nothing crosses here on any schedule.

The Long Shore Shadow.name: The Long Shore Shadow
The Long Shore Shadow.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Even blue water with a low swell and a light scatter of foam, the coastline of the Verdant Coast holding the eastern margin in a continuous green band. The swell comes in long and slack and lifts the surface without shaping it. The sky is clear. Sun lies far enough over to put the shore into shadow while the water stays lit. That shadowed shore reads as a dark band against lit water, which makes it easier to follow than it is in the middle of the day. Fliers moving north or south use the shoreline as reference and stay out over the sea where the air is less broken.
The Long Shore Shadow.hiddenInfo: Over The Long Shore Shadow the wind is the only fixed thing, and it changes. Weather arrives from the open quarter with little warning and no shelter.

Windlean Shore.name: Windlean Shore
Windlean Shore.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Wind is the constant here, coming off the water and bending everything that grows above the shoreline into the same lean. Rock and a little sand make the margin; beyond it the swell runs mid-blue with white working through it. Growth holds in pockets where the stone gives shelter, and those pockets are the only broken ground on an otherwise clean strip. Open Ocean lies west past the swell, and inland to the east the cover thickens into Luminous Forest. Sand gathers in a long tail behind every stone standing above the strip, all the tails pointing the same way, which makes the run of the wind legible from the air without anything moving.
Windlean Shore.hiddenInfo: Windlean Shore is a margin rather than a place: salt, rock and the swell working at both. The route inland is whatever the rock allows.

The Crossroads Clearing.name: The Crossroads Clearing
The Crossroads Clearing.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Tracks cross this cell in more directions than the forest would suggest, cut through standing timber and kept open by use, with cleared ground at the junctions. The canopy either side is full and the undergrowth beneath it heavy. Streams run through in shallow beds and meet the tracks at fords rather than bridges. Pale growth lines the cut edges where light has been let in, marking the routes after dark. Verdant Coast lies west past the last of the timber. The junctions are trampled bare and wide enough to put down on, which makes them the only landing ground in a cell otherwise closed over.
The Crossroads Clearing.hiddenInfo: Nothing is built at The Crossroads Clearing; the forest here is a thing cities lean on rather than a place they own. Wildlife is the ordinary hazard; Starian bandits the less ordinary one, and both need story evidence.

The Darkfall.name: The Darkfall
The Darkfall.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] The densest cover in this part of the forest stands here, canopy closed over broken rock and deep leaf litter, with almost nothing cleared. Water shows at the edge of the frame and small streams run down toward it over stepped ground. Undergrowth is thick enough that the few foot tracks are the only practical lines through. Glowing growth covers the fallen timber in sheets and gives the interior a steady pale light once the canopy has shut out the sky. Streams here run in stepped beds over rock and drop between one level and the next, so the sound of water carries through the interior. The leaf litter is deep enough to take a boot to the ankle in places.
The Darkfall.hiddenInfo: Cover at The Darkfall is total below the canopy and useless above it. A lost traveller here is found by the streams, which all run somewhere.

Hundred Houses.name: Hundred Houses
Hundred Houses.basicInfo: [Lv 2-15 · Low] Working fabric, tight and warm-toned, amber and copper star-glass over ancient star-metal that shows wherever the newer facing has been stripped back. Hundred Houses Quarter and the mixed-house residential wards stack close together, with Maker's Reach and the South Service Terraces stepping down through them in open decks. Open Contract Hall and Myralis Capitol Clinic front the same paving. Old energy conduits run along the deck undersides, reused as cable runs and warm to stand beneath. The decks are narrow, railed and continuous, so a walker crosses this ground by stepping down through them rather than around. Part of Relstaris.
Hundred Houses.hiddenInfo: The Service Union Rooms on the South Service Terraces are weighing labour action over shift conditions on the cargo floors, and Branna Sol knows a walkout would halt the Gate Hub and the Grand Market within a day. In the Open Contract Hall the Fair Contract Review Office is tracking a legal template designed to trap the signer in unpaid obligation, already circulating under three employer names, while Jaro Sol and other Sol contractors keep being offered the dangerous work. In the Hundred Houses Quarter the Empty Housefront stays staffed and funded with no verified family member seen for cycles, and Elyss Auren and Nalia Quorin broker the petitions that follow each sale on Declining Compound Row. The Supply Shortage Kitchen has run longer than usual this season.

The Grand Approach.name: The Grand Approach
The Grand Approach.basicInfo: [Lv 3-64 · Moderate] Light drops away in this part of the city. Low Relstaris runs beneath and between the bright construction, lit violet and dull gold off old conduits still carrying current, and the Deepways go down again under that. The Vein Market and Relstaris Grand Market fill covered ground with noise and colour, while the Grand Lunar Gate Hub and South Arrival Ward take arrivals continuously. The Hollow Ring and Forgotten House Ward sit in the unlit gaps. The floor underfoot changes without warning from paving to open metal grating to bare star-metal worn smooth by traffic. Part of Relstaris.
The Grand Approach.hiddenInfo: Restricted Movement Control at the Grand Lunar Gate Hub is managing a closure it has not publicly explained, the Dustfall platform has degraded again on far-side component shortages, and Academy Arrival Hall lists a student who never reached the housing desk; Mira Contair has an open calibration fault on a platform still scheduled. Beneath it all, someone in the Deepways is running an Illegal Gate Relay Room, attempting to redirect or imitate transit infrastructure, a Contair-grade problem no Contair engineer has been asked to look at, while Talik Nox sells competing incomplete charts that send two groups into the same hall. In the Hollow Ring, Kelvan Orvantis's match-fixing has already distorted an official competition. A landlord consolidation is moving through Low Relstaris, and the relay will either work or be found before the season turns.

Starfall Quarter.name: Starfall Quarter
Starfall Quarter.basicInfo: [Lv 2-51 · Moderate] Open ground carries most of this cell, building gathered into clusters with forest standing along the eastern side. Convergence Festival Grounds are a paved expanse kept deliberately empty; Nightglass Row and the Starfall Entertainment District set dark glass and saturated colour against it, and the Nexaran Table sits among them. The Grand Waypoint and Cargo Exchange takes freight down onto wide landing plates. Between the clusters the surface is packed earth scuffed to dust by crossing traffic, with lighting rigs standing out on it where nothing is built. Walkers cross unmade ground between clusters; fliers go over it. Part of Relstaris.
Starfall Quarter.hiddenInfo: A consignment of emergency medical cargo has gone missing at the Grand Waypoint and Cargo Exchange between manifest and pickup, and the Lost Parcel Department's file is thinner than it should be; Rexan Vossan knows the Quiet Reroute Office is the site's real vulnerability, legitimate emergency authority with minimal oversight, and a route that has become politically impossible to run is being replaced by a workaround that is barely legal. On Nightglass Row the Closed Window is suspected of preserving far more evidence than it destroyed, and at least one major-house member runs business through the private suites; Yara Aevon, Eris Nox and Ressa Halvar each hold a piece of who. The missing cargo's pickup window has already closed.

The Driftwater.name: The Driftwater
The Driftwater.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Broad bright water with a slow set to it, moving along the channel rather than across, so that anything adrift here travels. Light off the surface turns strong and low-angled at the ends of the day. The green edge of the Verdant Coast holds in view to the west, and eastward the same open blue continues with nothing between to land on. The green edge there is cliffed and forested above the water, and it is the only relief anywhere in the frame. The set carries steadily down the length of the channel and holds its direction through the day, so a flier who stops working is moved without noticing it.
The Driftwater.hiddenInfo: The Driftwater is transit air over deep water, crossed rather than visited. Nothing here needs story evidence except the weather.

Ashen Shore Reach.name: Ashen Shore Reach
Ashen Shore Reach.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] The eastern side of the channel runs up against black rock: burnt shelves at the waterline, and behind them the stripped ridges of the Ashen Wastes going inland. Water here is bright but restless, thrown back off the stone into confused chop. Heat comes off that shore through the middle of the day and lifts fliers unevenly, so crossings out of the east are generally begun early. The shore between the water and that inland ground is the Ashen Coast, black and low along the whole eastern side. Chop thrown back off the stone meets the swell coming up the channel and stands the surface into short peaks that do not travel.
Ashen Shore Reach.hiddenInfo: Ashen Shore Reach holds standing water in its hollows and no soil worth the name. Wildlife works the tideline; a careless camp attracts it.

The Strait Margin.name: The Strait Margin
The Strait Margin.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Dark rock shelves out toward the water on this edge, the waste ending in a ragged margin above the bright surface of Radiant Strait. Salt haze softens the light coming inland. Rock at the margin is cut into shallow basins that hold standing spray and dry white. Ash lies thinner here, blown clear by the onshore wind, and the exposed stone is pitted and hard-wearing. The shelves step down toward the water in short broken faces with no way through most of them. Surf sound reaches a long way inland across ground this bare.
The Strait Margin.hiddenInfo: Along The Strait Margin the line between sea and land moves with every set of swell. A stranded hull or a lost load washes up here before anyone reports it missing.

The Rope-Flow Fields.name: The Rope-Flow Fields
The Rope-Flow Fields.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Sheets of rope-textured lava cover this ground, frozen mid-flow in coils and folds that catch a boot at almost every stride. Grit fills the troughs between them. Where a coil has split open the inside is glassy and darker than the weathered crust. Nothing softens the walking and nothing grows. The coils stand a hand high and roll over one another, brittle at their crests and breaking to sharp fragments underfoot. Heat off the sheets is steady and the air over them carries almost no dust.
The Rope-Flow Fields.hiddenInfo: The crust at The Rope-Flow Fields rings differently over old voids, and the sound is the only warning. Cover here shelters danger as readily as travellers; Starian bandits use it, given story evidence.

The Fissured Ground.name: The Fissured Ground
The Fissured Ground.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Fissured ground makes this stretch slow: cracks run through the rock in long parallel sets, some narrow enough to stride and some not. Ash bridges a few of them convincingly. Crack walls are clean-sided and drop out of the light within a hand's depth, so their floors stay unseen. Nothing grows to mark which ones will hold. The rock between sets is flat and sound, so the walking alternates easy ground and a decision. Dust lifts out of the open cracks whenever the wind gets down into them.
The Fissured Ground.hiddenInfo: The Fissured Ground is old flow and ash: sharp underfoot, hot by afternoon and empty of anything living. Wildlife is scarce and what survives here is not gentle.

The Stepped Benches.name: The Stepped Benches
The Stepped Benches.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Stepped benches of old lava climb gently southward here, each ending in a low face and starting again beyond it. Ash sits on the treads and slides off the risers. The rock is grey on top and black where it has broken. Tread surfaces run wide, level and gritty, and the faces between them are low enough to step up without a hand. Wind travels along the benches rather than across them and keeps the ash moving in one direction. Part of Ignivex.
The Stepped Benches.hiddenInfo: The Stepped Benches is service ground for Ignivex, crossed daily and rarely mentioned. Dravon raids have hit ground like this before.

Ash Gully Country.name: Ash Gully Country
Ash Gully Country.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Ash gullies cut down through this ground in shallow branching lines, their floors soft and their sides crumbling where the rock has rotted. They carry a walker below the skyline. Rotted rock in the sides comes away in flakes that build a loose collar along each floor. They also fill with still, hot air and remove any view of what lies ahead. Gully floors take a print deeply and hold it until wind reaches down into them. The sides shed at a touch and will not carry weight anywhere along their length. Part of Ignivex.
Ash Gully Country.hiddenInfo: Ash Gully Country is the built edge of Ignivex: the same fabric as the city, thinner, and no authored location stands on it. Ash settles on everything level by evening.

Glare Flats.name: Glare Flats
Glare Flats.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Light grey stone, bleached and blasted smooth, covers this ground in wide plates with narrow dust-filled joints between them. Glare off it is severe through the middle of the day. The dust in the joints is pale, fine and packed hard enough to walk on without noticing it. The surface is sound and fast to walk, which makes it tempting, and it offers absolutely nothing to get behind. The plates are polished enough to take a print only where dust has gathered, and the joints are the only broken ground for a long way in any direction. Sound crosses the whole of it unobstructed.
Glare Flats.hiddenInfo: Nothing grows at Glare Flats; the ground takes heat in and gives it back after dark. Nothing here is patrolled, maintained or mapped.

The Ribbed Lanes.name: The Ribbed Lanes
The Ribbed Lanes.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Ribs of rock run north and south through this ground with ash-floored lanes between them, so movement along the grain is easy and movement across it is not. The lanes hold still air and heat. Lane floors are level ash, deep down the middles and thinning to bare rock against the ribs. Grit blown off the tops settles into them constantly and deadens every sound. Rib backs are narrow, hard and continuous, and a walker on one sees the lanes either side and little beyond the next rib. Landing ground is the lane floors, level and soft and rarely wide.
The Ribbed Lanes.hiddenInfo: The fissures and tubes of The Ribbed Lanes give real shade and real drops, and cut across any line of travel. Water is whatever a traveller carried in.

The Heavy Surf.name: The Heavy Surf
The Heavy Surf.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Surf drives into the rock along this whole stretch, white where it enters the gaps and dark the moment it draws back, with heavy navy water beyond. Land takes the greater part of the cell and is black stone throughout. Nothing softens the edge, neither sand nor beach nor growth, and the only usable landing ground is the flat back from the splash. The gaps are narrow and run well back into the stone, and the water inside them rises and falls with each set like something driven rather than poured. Between them the rock is level and dry, dark enough to hold the day's heat and rough enough to grip a boot.
The Heavy Surf.hiddenInfo: Where The Heavy Surf meets the water there is stone to stand on and little else; landings are possible and rarely worth it. Nothing crosses here on any schedule.

Twin Coast Water.name: Twin Coast Water
Twin Coast Water.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Land closes this water on two sides, south and east, where the Verdant Coast comes round, and the sea between runs a solid mid-to-deep blue with low crests on it. The two green edges meet out of frame and the water between them narrows without closing. Cloud is absent. The swell shortens as it approaches the shore and stacks up without breaking in the open. Colour holds the same from the middle of the frame to either shore, since nothing shallow lies between. Fliers cutting the corner rather than following the shoreline take this water and gain time by it.
Twin Coast Water.hiddenInfo: Open water with no landing under Twin Coast Water: a flier who loses a heading here has only the sun to correct it. Wildlife under the surface is possible and rarely seen; bandits do not work water this open.

Breakwater Point.name: Breakwater Point
Breakwater Point.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Scrub covers the ground above the shore in low dense mats, cut through with pale sand where the wind has scoured down to it. The water below runs mid-blue, veined white along the rock. Stepped stone lets a walker get down to the surf in some places and refuses it in others, and from the air the difference reads as a change of colour rather than shape. Open Ocean carries on west of the swell, and inland east the mats give way to the taller cover of Luminous Forest. The scoured lanes of sand all run the same way and are firmer underfoot than the mats either side, so they carry anyone crossing above the shore.
Breakwater Point.hiddenInfo: The shore at Breakwater Point is walkable at the cost of wet footing, and the surf covers the sound of anything approaching. The route inland is whatever the rock allows.

Greywater Margin.name: Greywater Margin
Greywater Margin.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Open ground and scattered stands take the place of continuous forest along this stretch, with water visible west and the light off it colouring everything a colder grey-blue. Almost nothing has been built or surfaced. The footing is firm and the going is fast by the standards of this forest. Glowing growth is confined to the surviving stands, so after dusk the cell reads as lit patches separated by dark open ground. Verdant Coast holds the water west, and the cold light off it reaches across the open ground.
Greywater Margin.hiddenInfo: Greywater Margin is Luminous Forest country: close cover, small watercourses and quiet that carries sound a long way. Cities patrol their own edges and nothing past them.

Longreach Farmlands.name: Longreach Farmlands
Longreach Farmlands.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Worked open country runs beside the Longreach here, flat ground under cultivation with bare sandy patches where the surface has been turned. Roads cross it in a made network feeding south toward The Barge Terraceeast, loaded traffic on them at most hours. The river itself is wide and navigable and barges work it steadily. Forest closes the cell east and west, and the glow from under its edge is the only light off the worked ground once the roads have emptied. Luminous Forest holds both those edges, standing back from the worked ground without a cleared margin between. The roads are laid wide and cambered and take traffic in both directions at once.
Longreach Farmlands.hiddenInfo: Longreach Farmlands is cultivated ground beside the Longreach, flat and worked, with made roads feeding the Barge Terrace in season. A failed harvest here shows at the Hauler Yards in grades and volumes days before any household feels it.

The Cloud Margin.name: The Cloud Margin
The Cloud Margin.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Cloud sits low over this cell more often than not, and the canopy beneath it is patchy, alternating with cleared ground and made surfaces. Roads run east and west between The Grand Approach and The Loose Floor, and the forest has been pushed back from them. Small streams drain toward the worked country west. Under the trees the glowing growth is ordinary rather than thick, enough to show the track edges and not much more. The Longreach lies west of this ground. Cloud sitting low keeps the light flat and the cleared surfaces dark, and it lifts off the canopy later than off the open ground.
The Cloud Margin.hiddenInfo: Nothing is built at The Cloud Margin; the forest here is a thing cities lean on rather than a place they own. A lost traveller here is found by the streams, which all run somewhere.

Sandrise Alternation.name: Sandrise Alternation
Sandrise Alternation.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Mixed cover holds this ground, closed canopy in the hollows and thin stands with sandy floor on the rises, the two alternating often enough that the going changes constantly. Tracks run north toward Starfall Quarter and east toward Verdant Coast, neither of them improved. Water collects in the hollows rather than running through. Pale growth is heaviest in those wet places and almost absent on the dry rises. The hollows hold their water and the rises shed it at once, so the going changes between firm and soft within a few strides. Sand on the rises is loose and pale and shows every track across it.
Sandrise Alternation.hiddenInfo: Cover at Sandrise Alternation is total below the canopy and useless above it. Foraging is possible for those who know the growth; most do not.

The Undercut Headland.name: The Undercut Headland
The Undercut Headland.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Headland rock stands out into the water, green-topped and undercut where the swell has been working at its base. Rather more than half of what lies here is sea. The growth on the tops is low and salt-burned, thick enough to walk through with effort, and the flat behind it takes a landing better than anything nearer the edge. Luminous Forest stands inland to the west, and Radiant Strait runs east past the point of the rock. Each set entering the undercut sends a low boom up through the stone that is felt in the soles as much as heard, and it comes at intervals long enough never to be expected.
The Undercut Headland.hiddenInfo: The Undercut Headland is a margin rather than a place: salt, rock and the swell working at both. Starian bandits are not unknown on lonely coast, and cover here shelters them as readily as a traveller.

Clear Channel Deep.name: Clear Channel Deep
Clear Channel Deep.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Clear channel water, pale in its reading, with the deeper middle showing as a distinct darker band running the length of the cell. Nothing stands out of it. A green rim holds in view along the western side, and the water continues east as more of the same, so a flier arriving from inland faces the widest part of the crossing from this point. That green rim is the Verdant Coast, headland rock with growth on its tops, and it is the last ground before the water opens. The darker middle band holds its position through the day and runs straight enough to be used as a line rather than as a mark.
Clear Channel Deep.hiddenInfo: Nothing marks Clear Channel Deep but swell; the crossing is made on held height and remembered bearing. Ships bound for the Orbital Gate Station pass far above; nothing else uses this sky.

The Bright Passage.name: The Bright Passage
The Bright Passage.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Hard light and bright water, the channel at its most open, with the dark inland ground of the Ashen Wastes closing off what can be seen to the east. Swells run long and low across it. The air holds steady through the morning and roughens later as the land warms, which sets the working hours for anyone who flies this part of the crossing. Between the water and that dark ground the shore is low and black and gives nothing back to the light. Swells crossing the cell carry no foam at all, and the surface reads as one unbroken sheet of brightness from any height.
The Bright Passage.hiddenInfo: The Bright Passage offers no rock, no bar and no rest, and the light off it is the main hazard by midday. A downed traveller is a rescue only if someone saw them go down.

Volcanic Benchland.name: Volcanic Benchland
Volcanic Benchland.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Water fills much of the view on one side, Radiant Strait running bright against a shoreline of black rock with no beach in it. Inland the ground stacks up into low volcanic benches. Glare off the strait makes the stone read darker than it is. The benches are broad-topped and littered with broken slab, and the ground between them holds ash that the onshore wind keeps on the move. Surf works the rock below without ever making a landing place of it.
Volcanic Benchland.hiddenInfo: Volcanic Benchland is Ashen Wastes country, where the horizon repeats itself and a heading is hard to keep. Smuggling crews working around Ignivex's eastern mountains cut through ground like this by timing and local knowledge.

The Basalt Curtain.name: The Basalt Curtain
The Basalt Curtain.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Basalt-black wall runs cross this ground in long straight lengths, reinforced at the joints with copper-bronze plating weathered to a dull green-brown. Between them stand squat structures with heavy roofs and few openings. Grilles in the paving carry warm air up from the tunnels beneath, and the stone above them stays dry. The paving is cut block laid tight, and the grille lines are the only break in it. Air standing over the grilles shimmers and lifts grit out of the joints. Walking here means passing from one wall length to the next through gated openings, and the flat roofs are built to take a landing. Part of Ignivex.
The Basalt Curtain.hiddenInfo: Nothing on The Basalt Curtain is a destination; travel here arrives at the nearest named site of Ignivex. Ash settles on everything level by evening.

The Ash Slopes.name: The Ash Slopes
The Ash Slopes.basicInfo: [Transit · Severe] Loose ash slopes take up most of this cell, grey and deep, with thin threads of open lava showing in the seams where the crust has parted. Heat comes off the ground in visible shimmer. What is built is small and hard: bunkered structures on levelled pads, ringed with firebreak gates and marked at the corners in ember-line paint. The pads are cut stone set into the slope and swept constantly, because ash slides back over them. Sound is thin on this ground, most of it taken by the ash. Footing on the slopes is unreliable, and fliers hold height over them.
The Ash Slopes.hiddenInfo: Loose ash lies deep on The Ash Slopes over threads of open lava, and the shimmer off it hides the seams. Ignivex's bunkered structures here are held ground under standing Dravon pressure, and an alert can close the slope in minutes.

The Living Flows.name: The Living Flows
The Living Flows.basicInfo: [Transit · Severe] Open lava lies in this ground, banked in slow red channels between black crusted flows that break and reseal as they cool. The light here comes entirely from below, red and moving. Ash has drifted against the upwind edges of the older flows. The crust is ridged and rope-turned across the whole field, sharp where it has broken and hollow-sounding where it is thin. Air over the channels carries the small collapse and settle of cooling rock. Nothing is built on the active ground; the nearest works are heat intakes set back on stable rock, hooded and ember-marked along their casings.
The Living Flows.hiddenInfo: Open lava lies at The Living Flows in slow red channels between crusts that break and reseal as they cool, and the light comes from below. Nothing crosses it on foot; fliers keep height against the rising air, and nobody patrols it.

The Crusted Vents.name: The Crusted Vents
The Crusted Vents.basicInfo: [Transit · Severe] Crusted flow fields cover this ground, black and ridged, with lava showing in narrow lines where the crust is thinnest. Vents on the higher ground release steam in steady columns. A hardened service route crosses the field on piers, its deck plated and its rail ember-marked, and the glow under the crust is bright enough to follow the route by. The deck plating is ribbed for grip and warm through a boot sole, the piers footed on the thickest crust the field offers. Ground either side of the piers will not carry weight.
The Crusted Vents.hiddenInfo: Steam stands off the vents at The Crusted Vents in steady columns, and lava shows where the crust is thinnest. The piered service route is Ignivex's and is watched from the Wellhead Fields; leaving it is the danger.

The Cooling Terraces.name: The Cooling Terraces
The Cooling Terraces.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Terraced building holds this ground, black stone faced with copper-bronze banding and stepped up level after level. Cooling canals run along the terrace fronts with mist chambers set at the turns, and the air above them is markedly cooler than the air over open stone. Shaded courts sit behind the canal line. Terrace surfacing is dressed stone, damp within a pace of the canals and dry further back, and the stairs between levels are cut into the retaining faces rather than standing clear of them. Water moving in the channels is the constant sound. Part of Ignivex.
The Cooling Terraces.hiddenInfo: The Cooling Terraces carries Ignivex's ordinary life outward without any place of its own. Ash settles on everything level by evening.

Rockwall Passage.name: Rockwall Passage
Rockwall Passage.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Between dark rock walls the route holds a reasonably straight line through this ground, its surface grey with pulverised stone and its drainage cuts choked with the same. Wind comes through from the sea side in gusts. The line runs level and wide enough that two loads can pass on it, with the walls standing close on both hands. Nothing beside the worked strip offers shelter. The pulverised stone lies loose and deep enough to take a print, and it rises in a pale cloud behind anything that moves through it. Wall faces are unlined and shed grit into the cuts continuously.
Rockwall Passage.hiddenInfo: Rockwall Passage is where a checkpoint might stand tomorrow and did not yesterday. Bent Halo crews, Claimant hunters and Last Line escorts all move here; Dravon and Ignivex claim it and neither holds it.

Salt Ledges.name: Salt Ledges
Salt Ledges.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Ledges of dark rock lie in wide steps above the water, this cell being more stone than sea, the whole surface pitted and streaked pale where salt has dried on it. Growth is absent. The steps run roughly parallel to the water, which makes the walking along them easier than the walking across them, and the widest takes a landing cleanly. The North Route runs inland to the west, and the ledges between it and the water are the whole of what lies between. Grit collects in the pits and grinds under a boot at every step, which wears the pale streaking off the walking lines.
Salt Ledges.hiddenInfo: Fliers use Salt Ledges as a coast mark; walkers find the going slow and the shelter poor. Wildlife works the tideline; a careless camp attracts it.

The Tangled Margin.name: The Tangled Margin
The Tangled Margin.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Trees stand close to the edge of the rock, salt-pruned on the seaward side so the whole stand leans inland. Below them the water runs dark navy and heavy, and the surf sounds hollow where it enters the undercut. Ground between the trees and the drop is narrow but continuous, and it carries a walker along the coast without ever going down to the water. The stand is the seaward end of Luminous Forest, which runs on inland to the east without thinning. Roots stand proud along the lip where the soil has gone from under them, and they take weight well enough to serve as steps on the steeper parts.
The Tangled Margin.hiddenInfo: Under the canopy at The Tangled Margin the going is tracks and roots, and the glow-growth on wet stone does the lighting after dusk. Cities patrol their own edges and nothing past them.

The Ledger Terraces.name: The Ledger Terraces
The Ledger Terraces.basicInfo: [Lv 3-85 · Low] Terraces here sit back from the water, broad and quiet, pale composite underfoot with sandstone-toned facing and planted strips along the step edges. Counting-house frontages stand shoulder to shoulder through the Varriko Ledger District, route-boards clacking above their doors, while the walled ground of the Corsair Estate keeps its gardens behind copper-trimmed gates. A skyhook tower works its slow arc at the eastern edge of the view. The terrace steps run broad enough to walk along rather than merely down, and the noise of the working levels arrives thinned to a murmur. Landing ground is on the terrace tops, level and marked. Part of Helvyra.
The Ledger Terraces.hiddenInfo: Oren Varriko's fake perfect bond and the forged Common Scale seal Verel Ondin is chasing are the same shape of crime, and the open question is whether one forger made both. Verification in the Witness Seal Office has been tightened without explanation, factors appear at the Private Liability Chambers in place of the parties, and Mavriel and Sereth Varriko answer questions by pulling up the record. Above the district, the Corsair Estate keeps the Legacy Chamber for Torvex unopened while Xyren carries Commerce he never trained for; the Family Vault holds the Corsair end of agreements whose other ends sit in the Varriko vaults, and Korriven Corsair is the one reading both. Someone will open the Legacy Chamber or the bond question first, and each answer changes the other.

Waypoint Sprawl.name: Waypoint Sprawl
Waypoint Sprawl.basicInfo: [Lv 2-25 · Low] Everything on this ground arranges itself around the bulk of the Grand Waypoint, a trade hall wide enough to swallow a high season's freight, its approaches paved flat and ramped for haulage from four sides. Routefall Market spills off those approaches in rope-tan awnings and stacked crates, and the Bankside Care Hall keeps a quieter frontage a little off the traffic. Route-boards run three deep at the hall doors, and crane arcs cross overhead without pause. The paving is pale composite scored for grip and scuffed black along the haulage lines. Noise is constant and level, wheels and boards and cable together. Part of Helvyra.
Waypoint Sprawl.hiddenInfo: Forged Common Scale certification has begun surfacing in ordinary goods, so the Ledger Court Annex inside the Grand Waypoint is settling more on-site disputes than usual because the claims cannot wait for the ferry, and Dren Varriko's standing desk on Corsair's floor is busier than Tavren Corsair likes. On Routefall Market, Bareth Kollo has noticed someone paying rent on well-placed stalls that are never worked, buying presence rather than trade, while the Certified Goods Aisle's whole value is that its marks cannot be wrong. Raxen Caelrix's courier dispatch remains the fastest way to move something without it appearing on a manifest anyone reads. At Bankside Care Hall, Meya Orlin's refusal to confirm a patient is present is being tested by a house. The first confirmed forgery in the aisle pushes every affected claim across the river.

The Loose Floor.name: The Loose Floor
The Loose Floor.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Sand shows through the forest floor across most of this ground, pale and loose under a canopy that stands close but not tall. Undergrowth is low and scrubby, and the footing gives underneath. Almost nothing here is made: the tracks are worn rather than cut, and they run west toward The Loose Floor. The glowing growth spreads across the sand in low mats that light the ground rather than the trees. Verdant Coast lies east beyond the trees, and the wind off it reaches this ground without much to break it. The sand gives under weight and slides on any slope, which makes even a shallow rise slow work.
The Loose Floor.hiddenInfo: The tracks through The Loose Floor are kept open by use and would close within a season without it. Wildlife is the ordinary hazard; Starian bandits the less ordinary one, and both need story evidence.

The Narrows Turn.name: The Narrows Turn
The Narrows Turn.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Steep green falls toward the water and ends at rock that has been cut back into a face. Dark swell works the base of it, loud and without pause. Land takes the greater share of this cell, and the practical route runs above the trees rather than below them, because the slope below closes out over the sea in several places. The green is the falling edge of Luminous Forest, and eastward past the cut the water brightens into Radiant Strait. Seepage runs down the face in narrow dark lines that never dry, and the stone either side is pale by comparison.
The Narrows Turn.hiddenInfo: Along The Narrows Turn the line between sea and land moves with every set of swell. The nearest help is the nearest city, and it is not close.

Mid-Strait Passage.name: Mid-Strait Passage
Mid-Strait Passage.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Steady blue water, the foam of a light swell running over it in broken lines that form and disperse without changing the colour beneath. Ground rises green along the western rim above a working shore. This is the most ordinary stretch of the channel and the most heavily crossed, and traffic spreads over its whole width rather than following any one line. That rim is the Verdant Coast, its slope falling to rock that has been cut back at the water. The broken lines of foam form on the crests and are gone before the next crest arrives, so nothing on the surface lasts long enough to steer by.
Mid-Strait Passage.hiddenInfo: The colour of Mid-Strait Passage says nothing about what lies beneath, and nothing here will catch a tired flier. Weather arrives from the open quarter with little warning and no shelter.

Blackrock Ledge.name: Blackrock Ledge
Blackrock Ledge.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Black rock stands along the eastern margin of this reach and drops straight to water that stays bright right up against the stone. There is no shelving beach on that side and no easy landing. Fliers coming off the Ashen Wastes choose a crossing point by where the rock allows a launch rather than by where the water happens to be narrowest. The black margin at the water is the Ashen Coast, dropping clean with no shelf to stand on at its foot. Water right against the stone stays bright rather than darkening, since nothing washed off the rock gets into it.
Blackrock Ledge.hiddenInfo: Nothing grows at Blackrock Ledge; the ground takes heat in and gives it back after dark. Water is whatever a traveller carried in.

The Cleft Shore.name: The Cleft Shore
The Cleft Shore.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] A narrow band of volcanic ground holds between the waste and Radiant Strait, cut by shallow clefts that run down to the water and end in drops. The rock is dark and unweathered where the sea works at it. Its surface is rough, sound and blackened, holding grip even where spray has wet it. Wind moves steadily along the margin, carrying salt one way and grit the other. The band is level enough to walk quickly and narrow enough that both its edges stay in view at once. Cleft floors are dark, damp and slick wherever the spray reaches them.
The Cleft Shore.hiddenInfo: Where The Cleft Shore meets the water there is stone to stand on and little else; landings are possible and rarely worth it. The route inland is whatever the rock allows.

The Wall Routes.name: The Wall Routes
The Wall Routes.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Wall routes continue across this cell, basalt-black and wide enough on top to move along, with firebreak gates at the junctions and copper-bronze reinforcement at every corner. Behind them the ground is given to yards and heavy low buildings with shuttered openings. Ember-line markings run along the kerbs below. The wall tops are decked in cut slab behind a low parapet, and the yards are hard stone stacked with cut stock and covered plant. Shutters are heavy sheet in stone rebates and let very little light out. Broken unbuilt rock lies west, and the wall turns rather than crossing into it. Part of Ignivex.
The Wall Routes.hiddenInfo: The Wall Routes is Ignivex ground by every rule that matters and by no landmark anyone would name. Ash settles on everything level by evening.

The Forgelight.name: The Forgelight
The Forgelight.basicInfo: [Lv 3-69 · Moderate] Forge work dominates here. The Red Forges stand in long halls with roof vents open along their ridges, and The Crucible Yard lies alongside as hard standing scored by heat and stacked with cooled stock. Light is muted red and comes as much from the open hall mouths as from the fittings. Sound is continuous. The yard surface is stone plated where stock is set down, scaled dark and swept into ridges at its margins, and the hall floors run out to meet it at the same level. Air over the yard moves upward and carries grit with it. Part of Ignivex.
The Forgelight.hiddenInfo: When a piece fails in the Red Forges nobody can say at once whether the cause was a rival, a Dravon agent or bad work, and all three accusations get made the same day. In the Halessin workshop the same pattern runs in miniature: Maeron, Nessa and Tavren Halessin are quietly remaking a ruined commission after hours, each holding a private theory of whose fault the ruin was, and the family works smoothly only because none has said theirs aloud. The delivery date has not moved. Across the yard, Kaivor Volen's raw surges outrun his control and the Restraint Trials exist for students like him; Maeryn Volen will fail a trainee for winning badly, and Cassian Genesis is watching how Ignivex trains people to keep moving after they are hit. Tessan Caldris trains beside the Volen students and wants to be seen, which is its own hazard on floors held this hot.

The Wellhead Fields.name: The Wellhead Fields
The Wellhead Fields.basicInfo: [Lv 49-55 · High] Machinery is the built form on this ground: Geothermal Core Facilities occupy it as pressure chambers, capped wellheads and turbine halls, with conduit runs carried on trestles between them. Ash slopes climb behind the works and lava shows in the seams above. The paving is warm underfoot and grilled at intervals to vent. Trestle legs are footed in poured blocks set straight onto the rock, and the conduit lagging is banded and patched along its whole length. The turbine halls hold a low note that is felt as much as heard. Part of Ignivex.
The Wellhead Fields.hiddenInfo: The geothermal network is why Ignivex can refuse Contair-managed infrastructure and Dravon in the same breath, and it is the city's largest single exposure. Sabotage here can threaten whole districts, so the Sabotage Watch Points exist and a cracked conduit is investigated as a possible act before it is written off as wear. Tharen Volen's battlefield is underground: heat tunnels, pressure chambers, thermal gates and engines that would kill most outsiders in minutes, and the accessible face of the system at the Core Facilities is deliberately not the system, whose plant count, depth, capacity and extent stay undefined and partly hidden. The current inspection rotation has an unresolved reading on one conduit that Tharen has not yet classified as wear or act, and that classification decides whether the next shift is maintenance or a manhunt through tunnels nobody has fully drawn.

Kiln Slope.name: Kiln Slope
Kiln Slope.basicInfo: [Lv 22-28 · Moderate] Little is built on this ground and what is stands alone: The Festival Kiln rises from the ash slope as a heavy stone structure with a banked stack and cleared ground all round it. Lava threads the rock beyond in thin bright lines. Ash lies deep enough in the hollows to swallow a footstep. The cleared ground is swept stone held to a squared edge that the ash creeps back over, and the kiln face is smoke-darkened above its openings. Fine grit hangs in the air and settles on everything level. Nothing on this ground makes a sound but the stack, which draws steadily. Part of Ignivex.
Kiln Slope.hiddenInfo: The Festival Kiln celebrates and grieves in one place, sometimes within the same week, and the people who manage the transition do it often. Emberwake is a citywide remembrance rather than a Kiln monopoly; the Cinder Run has no fixed course, start or finish, whatever competitors claim about the Endurance Ground. What the slope actually holds is a question the city understands and does not say: under standing Dravon pressure, a full Kiln is both a morale instrument and a very large gathering of civilians in one exposed bowl, approached only from above onto a levelled pad, with slopes that offer no footing for an evacuation on foot. Each event calendar is therefore also a defence calendar, and the Wallworks and the Hearth Rows shelter wardens plan around it without the plan being announced. The next festival date is fixed; whether the alert schedule can be kept clear of it is not.

The Recovery Baths.name: The Recovery Baths
The Recovery Baths.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Cooling terraces step across this cell, cut in black stone and carrying canals along each front, with recovery baths sunk behind them under shade frames. Water moves slowly and steams where it is exposed. Retaining faces are banded in copper-bronze. Bath surrounds are worn smooth and stay wet, and the stone underfoot changes from warm and dry at the terrace backs to cool and slick at the water's edge. Shade frames are fixed sheet on stone posts and throw hard-edged shadow.
The Recovery Baths.hiddenInfo: Cross The Recovery Baths to reach Ignivex's real districts; it holds only what the city overflows. Ash settles on everything level by evening.

The Firebreak Wall.name: The Firebreak Wall
The Firebreak Wall.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Defensive works make up most of the building here, black wall lengths with firebreak gates and raised platforms behind them overlooking open rock. Heat grilles are fewer on this ground and the paving is cooler for it. Marker lights along the parapets are dull red and widely set. The platforms are decked in slab with stepped access from the rear, and the ground in front of the wall is graded bare and kept that way. Wind off the open rock is the loudest thing here. Ash carried on that wind collects in the gate rebates. Part of Ignivex.
The Firebreak Wall.hiddenInfo: The Firebreak Wall is service ground for Ignivex, crossed daily and rarely mentioned. Ash settles on everything level by evening.

The Dust Flat.name: The Dust Flat
The Dust Flat.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Grit and stone dust cover the worked surface through this stretch, so the route shows mainly as a flatness rather than as a made edge. Loose material builds along the shoulders and slides under a foot placed without care. Where the grit has thinned, worked stone shows beneath it in patches of a colder grey than the country around. The light is hard and the rock beside the line is warm to the hand. That flatness runs true enough to follow at speed, and its compacted core is firmer than anything either side of it. Ashen Coast lies east beyond the rock.
The Dust Flat.hiddenInfo: The worked line through The Dust Flat belongs to the North Route toward Dustfall: made, patched, unmaintained. Cover shelters danger as readily as travellers, and an ambush needs story evidence, not assumption.

Fissure Shore.name: Fissure Shore
Fissure Shore.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Broad black rock, level in the main and cut by narrow fissures that run inland from the waterline, with the sea showing only along one margin. Nothing holds in the fissures but grit and standing water. The surf is out of sight from the inland part and audible from all of it, and crossing the fissures is the slow part of any route along here. The North Route runs west of the rock, and the ground between is unbroken except by the fissures themselves. They widen as they run inland, so the crossing that is a step at the waterline becomes a climb down and up further back, and a route along this coast is better taken near the sea.
Fissure Shore.hiddenInfo: The shore at Fissure Shore is walkable at the cost of wet footing, and the surf covers the sound of anything approaching. Starian bandits are not unknown on lonely coast, and cover here shelters them as readily as a traveller.

The Pocket Sea.name: The Pocket Sea
The Pocket Sea.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Streaked with white across a mid-blue surface, this water sits in a pocket with the Verdant Coast along its northern and eastern sides. The swell comes in obliquely and rebounds, leaving the surface confused. Returning water meets the incoming sets at an angle and raises short peaks that stand and drop without going anywhere. Light is clear and direct. The white lies in brief broken streaks rather than long ones, since nothing here lasts long enough to draw out. Air close to the shore is turbulent enough that fliers hold out over the middle of the water rather than hugging the green edge.
The Pocket Sea.hiddenInfo: Over The Pocket Sea the wind is the only fixed thing, and it changes. Nothing here needs story evidence except the weather.

The Sand Strand.name: The Sand Strand
The Sand Strand.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Ridges of stone run out through the vegetation toward the water, each one carrying growth on its back and ending in bare rock. Between them the ground is soft and green. Surf comes in against the ridge ends and drains out of the hollows behind, and fliers use the ridge tops, which stay dry and level where the hollows do neither. Open Ocean holds the view west beyond the ridge ends, and inland east the cover thickens and closes into Luminous Forest. The soft ground in the hollows takes a boot in and lets it out slowly, and it closes behind a walker so that no track holds.
The Sand Strand.hiddenInfo: The Sand Strand is a margin rather than a place: salt, rock and the swell working at both. Wildlife works the tideline; a careless camp attracts it.

Forgeworks Ground.name: Forgeworks Ground
Forgeworks Ground.basicInfo: [Lv 2-66 · Moderate] Workshop ground, loud and open: the Yalven Forgeworks vents heat and hammering across a yard of scorched paving, and smaller shops crowd the terraces around it with their shutters run up. The Common Scale Hall stands on cleaner stone nearby, its weighing floor open to anyone with a load to settle, while the Veltrax Redcourt frontages keep to tighter, older walling with planted courts behind. Cut steps and cargo ramps link the levels. The yard surfacing is warm underfoot and gritted with scale swept into the gutters, and hot metal carries on the air further than the noise does. Fliers use the forge roofs, the only flat ground clear of stacked stock. Part of Helvyra.
Forgeworks Ground.hiddenInfo: Two investigations are running toward each other across the river and neither bank will admit it. Daxor Veltrax is working a forensic question out of the Redcourt's own Recovery Room log that pairs exactly with the injury pattern Meya Orlin is logging at Bankside Care Hall, and comparing notes would mean conceding the wounds came from neither school. The Yalven Quality Review Office is pulling material traces on charm-bearing components, convinced the Circle Isle failures are a materials fault; canon leaves them wrong, and the actual cause goes unexamined. At the Common Scale Hall, Verel Ondin is tracing a forged seal toward Oren Varriko's impossibly perfect bond. The House Veltrax Office is drafting escort commissions, and at least one is a route meant to be walked visibly past people who will read it correctly; once signed it becomes a Corsair scheduling problem within a day.

Hauler's Row.name: Hauler's Row
Hauler's Row.basicInfo: [Lv 2-85 · Low] Open dusty hard-standing runs along the landward side of this ground, where the Hauler Yards keep the long low shapes of continent-crossing vehicles ranked under nothing but sky. Merchant Row presses stalls and frontages up against the yard edge, untidy, amber-lit and busy at most hours, and Rux Corsair's Sword School holds a walled practice floor behind them. Weathered copper route-boards mark outbound loads. The yard surface is rolled dirt over composite plate, rutted deep where the heaviest vehicles turn, and the dust it lifts settles on the awnings in an even coat. Fliers put down in the lanes between ranks, the only ground wide enough. Part of Helvyra.
Hauler's Row.hiddenInfo: A convoy arrived at the Hauler Yards short, and the paperwork at the Route Inspection Post balances in a way the load does not. Cargo that should have come by river has been arriving by road at cost and nobody will say why, which points at something on the Longreach that somebody wants avoided; the Bank Wardens have no authority out here. Pell Odran passes through the Hiring Wall without staying, because the bonded-labour contract he fled can follow a person into the city through a posting board. At Rux Corsair's Sword School a challenge was accepted that should not have been, and the Wayline Archive is being read to decide whether the acceptance was even valid; whoever reads it first shapes the outcome, and the Blade Courts must hear it before the season closes. On Merchant Row, one guest's movements do not match the manifest they arrived on.

Straitlight Clearing.name: Straitlight Clearing
Straitlight Clearing.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Between the standing forest and the water east, the ground opens into stony clearings the canopy has not closed over. Radiant Strait throws a hard brightness into the eastern part of the frame through the day. Foot tracks run south toward Verdant Coast over easy gradients. Pale growth rings the clearings where the shade begins and stops short of the open stone, so the lit edges hold their shape after dark. The clearings are floored with loose stone over firm ground and take a landing cleanly, which is unusual anywhere in this forest. Between them the canopy closes and the light drops at once.
Straitlight Clearing.hiddenInfo: Cover at Straitlight Clearing is total below the canopy and useless above it. The forest hides a camp well and a fire badly.

The Warm Current.name: The Warm Current
The Warm Current.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Open channel water, uniformly lit, holding the thin shallow blue that makes the strait look crossable at a glance. The eastern limit is a dark shelf of the Ashen Coast; to the west there is water to the edge of sight. Nothing out here gives shelter, and a flier caught by a shift in the wind either finishes the crossing or turns back the whole way. The shelf on that side runs straight for the whole length of the cell without a bay or a break in it. Light passes into the water and comes back weakly, so the shallow reading is a matter of colour rather than of anything actually visible beneath.
The Warm Current.hiddenInfo: The Warm Current is transit air over deep water, crossed rather than visited. Distance is the danger; the sea itself is indifferent.

The Thin Thread.name: The Thin Thread
The Thin Thread.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Nearly all water: bright, open and moving in long swells, with the dark coast reduced to a thin black thread along one side. The contrast between the two is stark under strong light. There is no stopping on the thread, which is rock going straight under, so anyone crossing here treats the whole span as one unbroken run. Radiant Strait carries the water on to the west, and behind the thread the ground runs back into the Ashen Wastes. Air over the black stone lifts hard by midday while the air over the water stays level, so a crossing finishing at the thread ends with an unasked-for climb.
The Thin Thread.hiddenInfo: Open water with no landing under The Thin Thread: a flier who loses a heading here has only the sun to correct it. Ships bound for the Orbital Gate Station pass far above; nothing else uses this sky.

Ashpan Flats.name: Ashpan Flats
Ashpan Flats.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Low black ground runs out toward the coast here, flat enough to walk and rough enough to punish careless footing. Surf sound reaches inland when the wind sits right. The pans are floored in pale ash packed flat and cracked into plates by the heat. Ash gathers in shallow pans that hold nothing else, and the stone between them is blistered and sharp. The blisters break under weight into shells of thin rock with hollows beneath them. Ashen Coast lies west past the last of the flat ground.
Ashpan Flats.hiddenInfo: The fissures and tubes of Ashpan Flats give real shade and real drops, and cut across any line of travel. Smuggling crews working around Ignivex's eastern mountains cut through ground like this by timing and local knowledge.

The Close Stacks.name: The Close Stacks
The Close Stacks.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Building covers nearly all of this ground: heavy black masonry in close blocks of four and five levels, ringed around communal heat cores whose stacks rise well above the roofline. Streets between are narrow and warm, lit low in muted red and floored with grilled sections that carry air up from below. Bridges cross at upper levels. The masonry is laid in large dressed blocks with deep-cut joints, and the street floor alternates solid slab and grille so that the warmth comes in bands. Doorways are set back in thick reveals. Landing is on roof decks, because the street plan leaves no open ground. Part of Ignivex.
The Close Stacks.hiddenInfo: The Close Stacks is the built edge of Ignivex: the same fabric as the city, thinner, and no authored location stands on it. Heat grilles, firebreak gates and alert horns reach this far.

The Cooling Terrace.name: The Cooling Terrace
The Cooling Terrace.basicInfo: [Lv 22-28 · Low] Ignivex Lunar Gate stands on this ground as a plated structure with cleared approaches and painted flight markers on the stone around it. The Cooling Steps descend nearby in broad terraces of canal and shaded court, water running in cut channels from step to step. Air over the steps is cool and damp against the dry heat of the surrounding streets. The approach stone is swept flat and painted in worn lines, while the step terraces are dressed and slightly dished so the water keeps to its channels. Sound at the gate is plated and hollow; at the steps it is water. Part of Ignivex.
The Cooling Terrace.hiddenInfo: A gate with two destinations shapes a city's politics. The Ignivex Lunar Gate reaches Relstaris and Dustfall only, which gives both an outsized place in Ignivex logistics, and under standing Dravon pressure the watch rooms treat who arrives, who departs and who meets them as intelligence. Meravil Ash Hall connects here, so the surrender-leaning house has standing business at the one monitored point where people and information leave, and everyone including House Volen knows it. Down the Cooling Steps, Meravil record keepers move through the recovery terraces gathering the numbers that feed the surrender argument, so a conversation on the Quiet Terrace can be kindness or an intelligence visit or both. The gate is not the only way in or out of Ignivex, which is why the watch rooms are never satisfied, and the next casualty count will be argued before it is finished.

The Emberward.name: The Emberward
The Emberward.basicInfo: [Lv 42-83 · Moderate] Public ground opens here, paved wide and heat-lit from below, with thermal fountains at the intersections throwing steam that is visible before the water is. The Emberward lies on this ground, its courts edged in ember-line marking and its fire sculptures mounted on stone plinths. Ash grit collects in the paving joints. The paving is large-format stone with lit seams between the slabs, warm to sit on and warmer where the fountains stand. Voices cross the open space without much echo, the building around it being low and heavy. Part of Ignivex.
The Emberward.hiddenInfo: Both family districts reach the Emberward and that is the pressure in it. Caldris arrives from the walls with repair counts and evacuation needs, Meravil from the record halls with casualty lists and ration forecasts, and the surrender argument is aired on the same stones where Volen banners hang, with Cynar Volen answering it in the open and Oryn Volen beside him. Delegations are received under watch, every visiting party read for Dravon leanings before it reaches the Delegation Rooms. A challenge brought to the Challenge Ground is genuinely public, and refusing it before the plaza costs more than losing. With the displacement count from Meravil Ash Hall due to be read here, the next plaza session is one where somebody must answer for the numbers.

Cinderline Junction.name: Cinderline Junction
Cinderline Junction.basicInfo: [Lv 22-28 · Moderate] Transit works take this ground: Cinderline Transit runs through it as a built line with platforms, covered halls and conduit galleries below the surface, the grilles along it carrying up warm air and a mineral smell. The Smoke Court adjoins, an enclosed paved space under high walls vented at their base. Light at ground level is pale ember. Platform decking is stone over steel with a painted edge line, and the court paving is laid in a plain bond that runs unbroken to the wall feet. Part of Ignivex.
Cinderline Junction.hiddenInfo: Standing Dravon pressure targets systems rather than open walls, and a movement network is the obvious system to target, so a lane fault, a stuck lift or a vent anomaly on the Cinderline is never treated as merely mechanical. Transit crews get questioned in a way that occasionally curdles into suspicion of their own colleagues, and the Line Control Room carries the knowledge that if the reserved response paths are down when a breach happens, people Rava Caldris's teams could have evacuated will not be. The network's real topology is deliberately unwritten and lives in the crews' heads. Next door, Selyra Volen's Smoke Court lets the shouting run until the truth surfaces and then expects accountability at once; every proceeding is recorded into archive vaults held at Meravil Ash Hall, so the house that counts casualties holds what was said, and the next transit fault will be argued there.

Ashglass Row.name: Ashglass Row
Ashglass Row.basicInfo: [Lv 22-28 · Low] Market building fills much of this cell, Ashglass Market laid out in roofed rows of dark stone and glazed panel, the lanes between them narrow and the stalls built in rather than pitched. Heat from beneath vents at the row ends and the lanes stay warm. Red lighting is fixed high on the roof frames. Lane floors are stone worn to a shine down the middle and gritted along the sides, and the glazing overhead is soot-filmed enough to soften what light comes through it. Sound in the lanes is close and unbroken. Part of Ignivex.
Ashglass Row.hiddenInfo: Ashglass Market runs on merchants and trade families, but the established Corsair trade presence is the thing everyone has an opinion about and nobody can pin down: which house or crew holds the post, what it carries, how its goods reach a city under standing Dravon pressure, and what arrangement it keeps with House Volen. That uncertainty makes the Rumor Tables the fastest information exchange in Ignivex. Sabotage suspicion from the Red Forges lands here too, since a failed piece is often blamed on materials bought in these rows, and a dispute the Dispute Bench cannot settle becomes the kind of grievance that reaches Selyra Volen's Smoke Court; merchants use that as leverage before anyone files. With the heat waivers and spice rankings due, the market is about to fill with exactly the people who trade in what they overheard.

The Copper Fringe.name: The Copper Fringe
The Copper Fringe.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Sparse heavy structures stand on this ground, set apart on levelled stone with unbuilt rock between them and walled routes linking them. Copper-bronze plating shows dull on the exposed corners. Grilles are rare here and the surface is cooler than the streets to the west. The levelled stone is cut square and finishes at a clean edge, past which the rock is broken and holds ash in its hollows. Walled routes are floored in slab and roofed only where they meet a structure. Part of Ignivex.
The Copper Fringe.hiddenInfo: Nothing on The Copper Fringe is a destination; travel here arrives at the nearest named site of Ignivex. Heat grilles, firebreak gates and alert horns reach this far.

The Warm Turn.name: The Warm Turn
The Warm Turn.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Warm brown ground takes over from grey along this part of the corridor, the worked surface running through country already halfway to desert. Scrub appears in ones and twos at the margins. Dust behind a load hangs a long time in the still air. Loose stone has been pushed off the line into low ridges that run along both shoulders, and nothing has moved them since. The surface is compacted grit with brown stone showing through it in bars, and the scrub is low and woody and grows only where the ground has been broken. Ashen Coast lies east past the margins.
The Warm Turn.hiddenInfo: The Warm Turn is corridor ground, one stretch of the functional sequence between the Quiet Mile, the Handoff and the North Routehead. The informal distress custom holds where crews can afford it and not where they cannot.

Tilted Slab Coast.name: Tilted Slab Coast
Tilted Slab Coast.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Slabs of dark stone lie tilted against one another above the water, the land taking almost the whole of this ground and the sea reduced to a dark strip. The rock surface is rough enough to hold a boot and sharp enough to punish a fall onto it. A flier looking for level ground has to hunt for it, because the tilt is general and the flat places are few. The North Route lies west and is the only worked thing in sight of the slabs. Gaps open between the tilted blocks and run down past where the light reaches, narrow enough to step over and deep enough that nothing dropped in comes back.
Tilted Slab Coast.hiddenInfo: Tilted Slab Coast holds standing water in its hollows and no soil worth the name. The nearest help is the nearest city, and it is not close.

Scattered Light.name: Scattered Light
Scattered Light.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Sharp clean blue, the surface lightly ruffled and the swell running low and regular beneath it. The ruffle is fine and even and breaks the light into a countless scatter of points. The green of the Verdant Coast holds the eastern side and the water darkens westward away from it. There is no cloud. Westward the darkening runs on to the edge of the frame with no change in the pattern of the swell. Glare builds through the middle of the day. Fliers along this line have the shore always in view and treat the run as ordinary working flight.
Scattered Light.hiddenInfo: Nothing marks Scattered Light but swell; the crossing is made on held height and remembered bearing. A downed traveller is a rescue only if someone saw them go down.

Green Cliff Edge.name: Green Cliff Edge
Green Cliff Edge.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Bare grey rock holds the shore, scoured clean and keeping standing water in its hollows long after the weather has passed. The sea beyond runs mid-blue with white veining through it. Almost nothing grows below the treeline inland, and the stone is level enough in patches to land on, though the patches do not connect and each has to be picked from the air. The treeline is the edge of Luminous Forest, north and east of the bare ground. Scouring has left a grain in the stone running all one way, fine ridges felt through a boot and crossed more easily along than against.
Green Cliff Edge.hiddenInfo: Where Green Cliff Edge meets the water there is stone to stand on and little else; landings are possible and rarely worth it. Starian bandits are not unknown on lonely coast, and cover here shelters them as readily as a traveller.

Windbreak Edge.name: Windbreak Edge
Windbreak Edge.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Cut and surfaced ground takes as much of this cell as the trees do, with roads running up toward Windbreak Edgewest and cleared lots beside them. Water shows south and west past the last of the cover. The remaining forest stands in windbreaks and steep-sided patches where the ground was too broken to work. Glow is scarce over the open ground and concentrated in those patches, which after dusk read as pale islands in worked country. Verdant Coast holds the water south and west past the last of the cover. The roads are surfaced and cambered and hold their line across the cleared ground, while the tracks into the steep-sided patches are worn and narrow.
Windbreak Edge.hiddenInfo: Under the canopy at Windbreak Edge the going is tracks and roots, and the glow-growth on wet stone does the lighting after dusk. The canopy gives no landing; the clearings decide the route.

The Level Floor.name: The Level Floor
The Level Floor.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Level forest floor runs through most of this cell, the canopy moderate and the undergrowth thick where light gets through. Tracks run north toward Windbreak Edge and east onto the worked ground, firm in dry weather and soft after rain. Streams cross them in shallow beds. The glowing growth is even and unremarkable here, lighting the floor to a low steady pale that makes the tracks readable while hiding the roots in them. The worked ground east is The Longreach, and Verdant Coast lies south past the last of the cover. The level floor makes the walking even and the roots in it the only obstacle, and they run shallow and are easy to catch in poor light.
The Level Floor.hiddenInfo: The Level Floor is Luminous Forest country: close cover, small watercourses and quiet that carries sound a long way. Wildlife is the ordinary hazard; Starian bandits the less ordinary one, and both need story evidence.

Barge Country.name: Barge Country
Barge Country.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] River fills a broad part of this frame, wide and working, barge traffic moving on it steadily under the bulk Helvyra sends along the Longreach. The landward ground is open and worked, green with cultivated strips and bare sandy margins where the bank has been cut back. Little has been built beyond the roads running north. Forest edges the cell east and west, and its glow after dusk stands against the dark moving water. The forest edging the cell is Luminous Forest, and Verdant Coast lies south past the last of the worked strips. Sandy margins along the bank are firm at the top and soft where they have been cut back, so the footing worsens toward the water. Part of Helvyra.
Barge Country.hiddenInfo: Barge Country carries Helvyra's ordinary life outward without any place of its own. Barge traffic and route-boards set the rhythm.

Unwild South.name: Unwild South
Unwild South.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Little in this cell has been made: the forest runs down to the worked country west without a cleared boundary, and the only routes through it are worn foot lines. Sandy soil shows under a canopy open enough to keep the undergrowth low. The ground falls gently south toward Verdant Coast. Glowing growth covers the fallen timber and the exposed roots in thick pale sheets, lighting the floor after dusk better than the canopy lets the sun light it by day. The worked country west is The Longreach, and Verdant Coast holds the ground south and east. Sandy soil under the open canopy drains fast, so the worn foot lines stay firm where forest ground elsewhere does not.
Unwild South.hiddenInfo: The tracks through Unwild South are kept open by use and would close within a season without it. A lost traveller here is found by the streams, which all run somewhere.

The Vent Water.name: The Vent Water
The Vent Water.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Nothing interrupts the water through this part of the channel: no bank, no rock, no shoal reading pale inside the blue. Light lifts off it strongly enough that a flier gains height simply to keep it out of the eyes. The Ashen Coast closes the eastern side as a dark band. Crossings here are made on pace and nerve rather than on any feature to aim at. Pale streaking shows along the top of that dark band where grit has gathered on the stone, and it is the only variation in an otherwise unbroken rim. The water beneath the glare runs deep and gives up nothing about itself.
The Vent Water.hiddenInfo: The colour of The Vent Water says nothing about what lies beneath, and nothing here will catch a tired flier. Nothing here needs story evidence except the weather.

Gritstreak Shelf.name: Gritstreak Shelf
Gritstreak Shelf.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Grit lies in pale streaks across the dark rock above the waterline, blown off the country inland and caught wherever the stone steps. Rather more than half of this cell is water. The surf works the rock hard and without pause, and the streaked ground above it is firm, open and the obvious place to put down along this run. The country inland is the Ashen Wastes, and the water west of the rock belongs to Radiant Strait. The streaks lie where the last wind left them and are somewhere else after the next, so the pattern on the stone is never twice the same and is no use as a mark.
Gritstreak Shelf.hiddenInfo: Gritstreak Shelf is a margin rather than a place: salt, rock and the swell working at both. A stranded hull or a lost load washes up here before anyone reports it missing.

The Grit Drift.name: The Grit Drift
The Grit Drift.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Pale grit begins to take over from the black rock through this ground, filling the hollows and drifting across the flow tops until the two read as one surface. Colour warms southward. Grit collects thickest against the upwind side of every flow lip, banked in smooth pale wedges that the wind rebuilds after each blow. The change is not a line but a gradual loss of the stone beneath the sand, and it alters the walking: firm on exposed rock, slower and less certain wherever the drift has built up toward Dust Barrens. Underfoot the grit is coarse and rolls on the rock like grain on a board.
The Grit Drift.hiddenInfo: The Grit Drift is Ashen Wastes country, where the horizon repeats itself and a heading is hard to keep. Cover here shelters danger as readily as travellers; Starian bandits use it, given story evidence.

Caldris Stoneworks.name: Caldris Stoneworks
Caldris Stoneworks.basicInfo: [Lv 9-73 · High] Fortification building is what stands here. Caldris Wallworks runs across the ground in basalt-black lengths with copper-bronze reinforcement, firebreak gates at the openings and yards of cut stock behind. Pale dust and sand lie thick either side of the works and bank against the stonework. Ember-line marking runs along the gate faces. The yards are floored in compacted grit with stone stacked on bearers, and the wall faces still carry the marks of their cutting. Dust lifts easily from this ground and hangs in the gate openings where the air funnels through. Part of Ignivex.
Caldris Stoneworks.hiddenInfo: The Wallworks exists because Ignivex is attacked often enough that defence has become architecture. Davor Caldris personally held a breach gate during a Dravon raid, and the house's position follows from it: loyal to Volen, certain that surrender is infection rather than strategy. Rava Caldris runs emergency response with no patience for pride when civilians are at risk, which puts her at odds with Volen aggression more often than either side says; Orvak Caldris's patrols stage from these gates into the Dravon-contested outer territory, whose position and extent are undefined, and each rotation comes back with a repair count that Lysa Caldris must turn into shelter capacity in the Hearth Rows. Maedra Caldris designs the firebreak gates deliberately without Contair training; Tessan trains at the Crucible Yard and wants to be seen. The next alert will find out whether the last repair held.

The Hearth Rows.name: The Hearth Rows
The Hearth Rows.basicInfo: [Lv 4-49 · Low] Housing runs in close rows here, The Hearth Rows built around communal heat cores whose stacks stand clear of the roofs and vent steadily. Doors open onto shared courts rather than onto streets. Dust and pale grit blow across the ground and collect at the thresholds. Lighting is pale ember and set at door height. Court floors are stone slab on sand bedding, lifting slightly where the ground beneath has moved, and the core housings stand at the court centres in plain masonry. Sound stays inside a court and does not carry to the next. Part of Ignivex.
The Hearth Rows.hiddenInfo: Domestic life here assumes the city will be attacked again.
