Lysa Caldris's neighbourhood shelters, supply caches, heat-safe routes and civilian drills sit in the calendar beside meals and school, and households that treat drills casually are spoken to by neighbours rather than by any official. That produces its own friction: families argue over stored supplies, over which children are trusted with shelter keys, and over whether readiness has tipped into fear, and Iskara Volen hears most of it before it reaches a court. The Rows also sit downstream of every other district: a forge rivalry, a market grudge or a Crucible Yard humiliation comes home at shift's end and is aired on the Row Step, and a dispute that outgrows the Step becomes one that reaches the Smoke Court. The next drill will show which courts have been quietly skipping them.

The Pale Yards.name: The Pale Yards
The Pale Yards.basicInfo: [Lv 3-11 · Low] Ash-grey stone sets this ground apart from the darker building around it: Meravil Ash Hall stands here, broad and low, with cooling channels cut along its flanks and running out into the surrounding yards. Air is cooler and the light paler, closer to white than to ember. Paving is smooth and unvented. The channel stone is cut in single lengths and worn at the lips where water passes over, and the yard surfacing is the same pale material laid in wide plates. Sound off the hall walls comes back flat and unhurried. Ways in are at ground level through plain openings, and the channels are bridged at every approach. Part of Ignivex.
The Pale Yards.hiddenInfo: Meravil Ash Hall does not feel cowardly; it feels exhausted. House Meravil's surrender-leaning politics come from casualty lists, grieving families, damaged homes and ration forecasts rather than treachery, and the house is not a monolith. Vennik Meravil operates politically; Auralis Meravil dissents against surrender from inside, which makes the Controlled Meeting Rooms genuinely contested. Caevan Meravil's marriage to Nyssara Dravon makes the whole district a living pressure point, and suspicion in Ignivex attaches to that tie and to the politics, not to the cool channels outsiders envy. Ilvara Meravil keeps the casualty records, and the families who come searching for a name are handed numbers that become the argument. The displacement count now being compiled will be read in the Emberward, and whichever total Ilvara signs will be used by both sides of the house.

Hearthcore Block.name: Hearthcore Block
Hearthcore Block.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Blocks of dark stone stand close on this ground around shared heat cores, the stacks braced against the walls and the courts between them paved and warm. Canals do not reach here; cooling is by shade frames and by grilles that can be shut. Ember-line paint marks the court edges and the stair mouths. Court paving is laid tight and holds its warmth well past the fall of the light, and the shade frames are pitched low enough to cut the glare coming off the stone. Stairs run up inside the block walls rather than outside them. Roofs are flat and used, railed at the edges, with pads marked out on the larger of them. Dust Barrens lie south.
Hearthcore Block.hiddenInfo: Hearthcore Block is Ignivex ground by every rule that matters and by no landmark anyone would name. Heat grilles, firebreak gates and alert horns reach this far.

The Dustward Works.name: The Dustward Works
The Dustward Works.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Scattered works stand on open stone at this edge of Ignivex: a wall length, a gated yard, a low structure or two behind it, with wide unbuilt ground between. Dust reaches across the stone from the south in pale streaks. Lighting is sparse, dull red on the gate frames and nowhere else. The open stone is unlevelled and ridged, holding dust in every hollow, and the made ground stops at the yard kerbs without transition. A flier has the whole of it in sight at once and can come down almost anywhere, while a walker picks a line between the ridges. Part of Ignivex.
The Dustward Works.hiddenInfo: Cross The Dustward Works to reach Ignivex's real districts; it holds only what the city overflows. Heat grilles, firebreak gates and alert horns reach this far.

The Faded Line.name: The Faded Line
The Faded Line.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Little remains of the worked surface through this ground, where the route thins to a used line over natural rock and the shoulders stop being distinguishable at all. Grey stone and thin grit make up the floor. The stone lies in broad level beds with shallow joints between them, swept clean by a wind that crosses this ground unobstructed, and the grit gathers only in those joints. The going is even and the marking is not. The rock is flat-bedded and sound, taking a wheel without complaint and holding no track worth following. Ashen Coast lies east past the stone.
The Faded Line.hiddenInfo: The Faded Line carries freight tracks, dust and the marks of every crew that passed, none of them named. Approaching Quilrath the danger turns to paperwork; leaving it the danger turns to thirst.

Rubblefield Shore.name: Rubblefield Shore
Rubblefield Shore.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Rubble covers much of this ground, black fragments of old flow lying loose over solid rock, with the sea a narrow dark presence at one edge. The loose stone shifts underfoot and rings when it does. Nothing grows in it, and a flier coming down picks bedrock over rubble, because rubble will not hold a footing under any weight. The North Route runs inland west of the rubble and carries whatever moves along this coast in quantity. The fragments are angular and lock against one another in places, so patches of the field sit solid while everything around them slides, and the difference cannot be judged before it is stood on.
Rubblefield Shore.hiddenInfo: Fliers use Rubblefield Shore as a coast mark; walkers find the going slow and the shelter poor. The nearest help is the nearest city, and it is not close.

The Ordered Ranks.name: The Ordered Ranks
The Ordered Ranks.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Low swell in ordered ranks under an almost empty sky, the water a strong blue that takes a harder edge where the sun strikes it directly. The ranks arrive evenly spaced and pass without gaining or losing height. Foam is minimal. The frame holds nothing but sea and light. Between them the water lies almost flat, and the colour there is deeper than on the faces. Wind is slight, which removes the usual help of reading direction off the surface, so fliers here rely on heading and time in the air alone.
The Ordered Ranks.hiddenInfo: Over The Ordered Ranks the wind is the only fixed thing, and it changes. Distance is the danger; the sea itself is indifferent.

The Threaded Water.name: The Threaded Water
The Threaded Water.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Threads of foam cross a mid-blue surface that darkens toward the open side of the frame. Green land shows north and east where the Verdant Coast wraps around this water. The two green edges lie at an angle to one another and neither runs far before leaving the frame. Swell arrives across the line of the shore and breaks irregularly. Light goes into the darker outer water and stays there, while the inner water returns enough to keep its colour. Cloud is almost absent and the light steady. Fliers stay high enough to keep both edges of land in view at once.
The Threaded Water.hiddenInfo: The Threaded Water is transit air over deep water, crossed rather than visited. Wildlife under the surface is possible and rarely seen; bandits do not work water this open.

Headland Point.name: Headland Point
Headland Point.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Dark water takes rather more than half of this reach, holding its colour even in strong light, and the shore that meets it is low unremarkable stone. No growth of any size holds there. The surf is small but constant, and the sound of it carries inland further than the water itself can be seen from. Open Ocean lies south and west, and the darker water here runs into it without anything on the surface to show where one becomes the other. The shore stone is a single unjointed sheet for much of its length, which makes it plain walking and gives a flier a clean run at a landing anywhere along it.
Headland Point.hiddenInfo: Headland Point holds standing water in its hollows and no soil worth the name. Nothing crosses here on any schedule.

Reef Break.name: Reef Break
Reef Break.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Cliffs take the shoreward side here, dark stone standing over navy water that does not brighten even at midday, with very little green holding on the tops. Half the cell is sea. Surf enters the fissures under the face and comes back out white, and the dry level above the face is the practical approach for anyone arriving from the air. Open Ocean opens south of the face and Radiant Strait runs bright to the east, so the dark water below is bracketed by brighter water on two sides. The cliff is not sheer but stepped back in overhangs, each one shading the rock beneath it, which keeps the lower stone wet and the upper dry through the middle of the day.
Reef Break.hiddenInfo: Fliers use Reef Break as a coast mark; walkers find the going slow and the shelter poor. Nothing crosses here on any schedule.

Thermocline Reach.name: Thermocline Reach
Thermocline Reach.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Even blue water under an almost cloudless sky, the surface barely scaled. There is a great deal of light and very little air movement, which makes height hot work and low flying hotter. The eastern shore reads as a dark rim and the western as a pale one, with nothing in between to fix on, so heading is held off the two edges together. The dark rim is the Ashen Coast, its stone under a pale film of dust blown off the country behind it. In still air the surface goes almost flat and gives back the sky rather than its own colour, so the water and the air above it read as one thing.
Thermocline Reach.hiddenInfo: Open water with no landing under Thermocline Reach: a flier who loses a heading here has only the sun to correct it. A downed traveller is a rescue only if someone saw them go down.

Dustfilm Edge.name: Dustfilm Edge
Dustfilm Edge.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Dust has settled over the black rock here in a pale film, thick enough in places to hide the stone entirely and thin enough elsewhere to show every crack in it. Navy water works the edge. The dry country inland supplies the dust, the wind moves it continually, and under everything soft the ground is solid rock and takes weight without giving. The dry country is the Dust Barrens, standing inland to the east, and westward the water brightens into Radiant Strait. Each step raises a pale plume that lifts clear and drifts before settling, so a walker leaves a trail in the air as well as underfoot.
Dustfilm Edge.hiddenInfo: Along Dustfilm Edge the line between sea and land moves with every set of swell. Starian bandits are not unknown on lonely coast, and cover here shelters them as readily as a traveller.

The Mesa Fields.name: The Mesa Fields
The Mesa Fields.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Tan sand and gravel take over completely here, with dark broken mesas standing out of it in short flat-topped blocks. Scrub is low, grey-green and widely spaced. The light is hard and the heat entirely dry. Scrub roots hold small mounds of sand together where nothing else does. Mesa sides are sheer and crumbling, their tops flat, swept and firm enough to come down on. The sand between them is coarse and drags at a boot on the open flats, packing hard only where wheels have run.
The Mesa Fields.hiddenInfo: The Mesa Fields is Dust Barrens ground: pale sand or gravel, scattered scrub, no shade worth the name and heat that arrives early. Sandstorms are the defining hazard, warned down Dustfall's beacon line when there is time.

The Open Desert Floor.name: The Open Desert Floor
The Open Desert Floor.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Open desert floor stretches between scattered dark mesas, the sand pale and firm where it is packed and loose where it has drifted across itself. Low thorny scrub grows in clumps and gives no shade worth the name. Heat arrives early and stays. Mesa shadow is the only shade going and it moves off any spot within the hour. Packed ground rings under a boot and drifted ground takes one to the ankle, and the difference is not visible until it is underfoot. Dry channels cross the ground in shallow braids, and following one is easier walking than the open flat right up until it turns the wrong way.
The Open Desert Floor.hiddenInfo: The mesas at The Open Desert Floor hold the only shadow, and the washes between them run dry and hard. Starian bandits work the barrens between the routehead and the corridor, given story evidence.

Dark Mesa Country.name: Dark Mesa Country
Dark Mesa Country.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Darker mesas crowd this part of the barrens, their sides sheer and their bases skirted with fallen rubble and blown sand. Between them the ground is stony rather than sandy. Mesa faces are streaked dark where water has run down them at some point. Wind funnels through the gaps and carries grit at face height. The rubble is angular and unstable, banked at the angle it fell at, while the stony ground between mesas is firm walking the whole way across. The gaps hold noise and throw it back off the walls.
Dark Mesa Country.hiddenInfo: Dark Mesa Country keeps vehicle tracks for weeks and footprints until the next wind. Wildlife is sparse, thirsty and occasionally dangerous.

Stone Pavement Flats.name: Stone Pavement Flats
Stone Pavement Flats.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Stone pavement shows through the sand across much of this ground, dark and flat, with drifts collected against every rise. Scrub is thinner here than further west and lower. Glare off the pale patches is sharp enough to matter. The pavement is set tight, its stones pressed level into the ground and polished on their upper faces, and it carries weight anywhere across its width. The Gate Apron stands beyond the northern edge.
Stone Pavement Flats.hiddenInfo: Nothing at Stone Pavement Flats is built, marked or watered; the beacon line is the nearest made thing. Anything lost here is found by the Claimants or by no one.

Gravel Wash Country.name: Gravel Wash Country
Gravel Wash Country.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Gravel flats alternate with low sand shelves through this country, both of them crossed by shallow washes that run dry and hard-floored. Scrub clings along the wash edges where the ground is disturbed. Gravel here is uniform in size and rounded, laid out as though it had been screened. Light comes down almost vertically through the middle of the day and flattens everything out. Wash floors are smooth, pale and firm, banked a little at their turns, and the gravel between them grinds underfoot. Little of this ground offers any relief a walker could get below.
Gravel Wash Country.hiddenInfo: Sand at Gravel Wash Country is firm on the flats, laborious in the drifts, and dust rides every gust. Refugees on foot come this way when the route is watched.

Sand-Buried Segment.name: Sand-Buried Segment
Sand-Buried Segment.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Half-buried under pale sand, the worked ground in this stretch shows as a firm compacted strip that appears and disappears beneath the drift. Dark rock breaks through where the wind has stripped it clean. Those exposed patches are pitted and sound, and they hold a wheel better than anything around them. Scrub grows along the edges where the surface has been disturbed. The drift lies in low tongues across the strip and can be walked through rather than around, though it takes the speed out of anything wheeled. Air over the open sand shimmers through the afternoon.
Sand-Buried Segment.hiddenInfo: The route at Sand-Buried Segment is a line rather than a road, and it is shared by everyone who will not use the gates. Bent Halo crews, Claimant hunters and Last Line escorts all move here; Dravon and Ignivex claim it and neither holds it.

The Salt Flats.name: The Salt Flats
The Salt Flats.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Salt dries white in the low places of the dark rock, laid down by spray and left standing when the water goes. Most of the ground here is stone; the sea runs deep navy along one side and opens out beyond it. Wind comes across from the dry country inland and carries grit with it, which makes the rock rough to work on and easy to land on. The water south opens into Open Ocean, and the dry country the wind crosses is the Dust Barrens lying inland to the west. The white crust breaks under a boot with a brittle crack and leaves a dark print in the rock beneath, and the prints stay until spray fills the low place again.
The Salt Flats.hiddenInfo: Where The Salt Flats meets the water there is stone to stand on and little else; landings are possible and rarely worth it. A stranded hull or a lost load washes up here before anyone reports it missing.

Low Cloud Water.name: Low Cloud Water
Low Cloud Water.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Thick pale cloud occupies most of the frame and the sea under it is reduced to a narrow band of grey-blue with foam showing white against it. The cloud has weight to it and hangs low, its underside torn into slow-moving lobes. Light is diffuse and gives nothing away about direction. The horizon is not visible at all. What sea is in frame runs restless and short, and the foam is the only bright thing anywhere in the picture. Fliers crossing under this cover work low and slow, and those who climb through it lose the surface entirely for the duration.
Low Cloud Water.hiddenInfo: Nothing marks Low Cloud Water but swell; the crossing is made on held height and remembered bearing. Weather arrives from the open quarter with little warning and no shelter.

Drifting Shadow Sea.name: Drifting Shadow Sea
Drifting Shadow Sea.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Ragged cloud drifts across a good part of the sky, its shadows moving over water that is blue where the sun reaches it and slate where it does not. The shadows have soft edges and change shape as they travel, so the boundary between the lit and unlit water is never fixed. The swell is moderate and the foam thin. Air alternates between still and gusting as the cloud passes over. In the lit patches the blue carries light well down, and in the shaded ones the surface closes and shows nothing beneath it. Fliers take the clear patches for height and let the shaded ones push them down a little.
Drifting Shadow Sea.hiddenInfo: Drifting Shadow Sea offers no rock, no bar and no rest, and the light off it is the main hazard by midday. Nothing here needs story evidence except the weather.

The Broken White.name: The Broken White
The Broken White.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Mid-blue water with white working across it in short broken lines, darker than the shallows to the north and lighter than the outer sea. The broken white appears in clusters and clears again, never holding across the whole frame at once. Land holds the northern and eastern edges where the Verdant Coast runs. Swell is moderate and comes in at an angle. Light works partway into this tone and returns a middling colour with neither the brightness of the shallows nor the weight of the open sea. Wind is offshore and steady, so the water nearest the land lies flatter than the water out in the frame.
The Broken White.hiddenInfo: The colour of The Broken White says nothing about what lies beneath, and nothing here will catch a tired flier. Distance is the danger; the sea itself is indifferent.

Low Reef Shore.name: Low Reef Shore
Low Reef Shore.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Hard dark ground makes up most of this stretch, bare and low, running out to a waterline that shows as a narrow band of deep blue along one side. Nothing of any height grows on it. The surf is heard rather than seen from the inland part, and the crossing on foot is straightforward and exposed the whole way over. Open Ocean holds the water both south and west, and the deep blue band is the near edge of it. The surface is not loose stone but fine material pressed hard, and it rings under a heel and takes almost no print, so nothing crossing it leaves a record.
Low Reef Shore.hiddenInfo: The shore at Low Reef Shore is walkable at the cost of wet footing, and the surf covers the sound of anything approaching. The nearest help is the nearest city, and it is not close.

The Dark Bight.name: The Dark Bight
The Dark Bight.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Sea occupies rather more than a third of what lies here and the rest is low bare shore, dark and flat, with no growth to break the line between them. The swell arrives mid-blue and veined white. Ground dries slowly after weather and holds shallow pools in the depressions, and fliers looking for footing pick the higher patches out by their colour. Open Ocean lies south and east and carries the water out of sight both ways. The pools stand shallow enough to walk through rather than around, and clear enough that the dark ground shows unbroken beneath.
The Dark Bight.hiddenInfo: The Dark Bight is a margin rather than a place: salt, rock and the swell working at both. Nothing crosses here on any schedule.

The Wide Bright.name: The Wide Bright
The Wide Bright.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Wide bright blue with a low swell, opening eastward toward the pale water of the Radiant Strait and closed northward by the Verdant Coast. The opening eastward shows as a widening lightness with no definite edge to it. Foam shows only at the crests. The sky is clear and the light strong off the surface. The northern shore runs level along the top of the frame and gives a straight line to hold a heading against. Fliers bound for the strait cross this on a steady line and get their first sight of the paler channel colour from it.
The Wide Bright.hiddenInfo: Open water with no landing under The Wide Bright: a flier who loses a heading here has only the sun to correct it. Weather arrives from the open quarter with little warning and no shelter.

The Opening Run.name: The Opening Run
The Opening Run.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Westward the channel loses its confinement and runs out into the heavier, darker blue of the Open Ocean, the change showing as a line in the colour rather than anything on the surface. Water on this side is still bright and still reads shallow. Fliers take their last bearing off that brightness, because beyond the line there is nothing below to correct against. Swells crossing the line arrive longer and further apart than the channel's own and carry more weight in them, which is felt before the change in colour is seen. Nothing stands out of the water on either side of it.
The Opening Run.hiddenInfo: Nothing marks The Opening Run but swell; the crossing is made on held height and remembered bearing. Nothing here needs story evidence except the weather.

The Brightening Shallows.name: The Brightening Shallows
The Brightening Shallows.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Chop builds through this reach whenever the channel wind sets against the run of the water, and the surface breaks into short white ridges that carry a long way down its length. The colour stays bright regardless. Dark coastal rock lies along the eastern side, close enough to reach in bad air, and southbound fliers keep it in sight for that reason. That rock is the Ashen Coast, ash-pale over black and low to the water for the whole length of the cell. The white ridges of chop run down the channel rather than across it and hold together far past where they formed.
The Brightening Shallows.hiddenInfo: The Brightening Shallows offers no rock, no bar and no rest, and the light off it is the main hazard by midday. Distance is the danger; the sea itself is indifferent.

The Ashpale Shore.name: The Ashpale Shore
The Ashpale Shore.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Ash-pale ground covers a good part of this stretch, fine and loose over the dark rock beneath, so the colour of the coast changes with how recently the wind has blown. The sea takes only a narrow share of the cell. Underfoot the loose layer gives and then meets stone, and fliers reading the surface from above judge it by shade rather than shape. Radiant Strait holds the narrow water to the west, and Caldris Stoneworkswest stands inland to the east. Wind works the loose layer into low ripples that run in ranks across the open ground, as regular as anything on the sea and firm enough to walk along.
The Ashpale Shore.hiddenInfo: Fliers use The Ashpale Shore as a coast mark; walkers find the going slow and the shelter poor. The route inland is whatever the rock allows.

The Routehead Flats.name: The Routehead Flats
The Routehead Flats.basicInfo: [Lv 4-48 · High] Desert runs unbroken across most of this cell, dry and hard-crusted, the sort of surface that holds vehicle tracks for weeks. The North Routehead marks the last built thing before it — a beacon line, a graded apron, a couple of modules for whoever is waiting — and traffic gathers there rather than anywhere further out. Flight markers stand at intervals past the apron and then stop. The apron is graded sand rolled flat and edged with set stone, and the modules beside it throw the only shade standing on this ground. Wind runs across the crust without lifting much of it, so the air stays clear to the horizon. Part of Dustfall.
The Routehead Flats.hiddenInfo: Beyond the North Routehead the route is shared encounter space that neither Dravon nor Ignivex controls, and no patrol schedule can be relied on. The Claimants camp here with outside warrants: Ravik Rusk holds one Sennra Sol has refused, and the client the Last Line Company walked away from has hired his crew, with Cyrra Hale and Dask Ren ready to move. Miren Tal may be selling route records to Dravon intermediaries, which would explain how an interception knew the Corsair shipment's timing. Beneath the routehead the Crooked Landing moves refugees, medicine and restricted cargo behind false manifests; damage to it would end Bent Halo extraction and force Dustfall to decide whether scarce gate components repair an illegal landing. Brannoc Kest and Neyra Vey are already picking their next departure window.

The Bright Sand.name: The Bright Sand
The Bright Sand.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Bright pale sand covers nearly all of this ground, deep enough in the drifts to make walking laborious and firm enough on the flats to carry weight. Dark rock shows only in isolated low outcrops. Those outcrops are pale-weathered, wind-cut and undercut at their bases. The surface moves with the wind and takes tracks away with it. The drifts lie in long crests with a steep face on one side, so crossing them means going up the shallow side or going round. Heat comes back off the sand from below as well as down from above.
The Bright Sand.hiddenInfo: The Bright Sand is Dust Barrens ground: pale sand or gravel, scattered scrub, no shade worth the name and heat that arrives early. Starian bandits work the barrens between the routehead and the corridor, given story evidence.

The Mixed Flats.name: The Mixed Flats
The Mixed Flats.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Mixed ground here: sand sheets, gravel pans and broken dark rock in no settled pattern, with dry washes threading between them. Scrub is sparse, low and woody. Its stems are bleached on the windward side and darker in the lee. The gravel pans are firm and pale, the sand sheets soft, and the rock between them broken into plates that tilt underfoot. Wind crosses the whole of it with little to slow it and keeps grit travelling at knee height. The worked corridor of The North Route runs through the country to the north and shows as a straighter line than anything the desert makes on its own.
The Mixed Flats.hiddenInfo: The mesas at The Mixed Flats hold the only shadow, and the washes between them run dry and hard. Wildlife is sparse, thirsty and occasionally dangerous.

The Eastern Rim.name: The Eastern Rim
The Eastern Rim.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Grey-brown desert pavement runs out to the eastern edge of the barrens, where the land gives out above Open Ocean and light comes back up off the water. Dust is fine and stays airborne in any wind. It settles on everything level as a pale film and lifts again at the first movement. Cover amounts to shallow scrapes and the lee of low rock, nothing more. The pavement is hard, level and unbroken right to the lip, and the drop beyond it is abrupt rather than graded. Sea air reaches this far and takes the edge off the dryness without cooling the ground.
The Eastern Rim.hiddenInfo: The Eastern Rim keeps vehicle tracks for weeks and footprints until the next wind. Anything lost here is found by the Claimants or by no one.

Muted Corner Water.name: Muted Corner Water
Muted Corner Water.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Muted grey-blue water in the eastern corner, hemmed by the broken dark rock of the Ashen Coast northward and the dry pale ground of the Dust Barrens to the west. The sea takes something of the colour of the land around it. Dust carried off the pale ground hangs over the water and mutes everything seen through it. Swell runs short and slaps rather than rolls. Light comes down strong and is given back weakly, so the sea looks dull under a bright sky. Fliers coming off the barrens meet the sea air abruptly and drop through rough layers at the change.
Muted Corner Water.hiddenInfo: The colour of Muted Corner Water says nothing about what lies beneath, and nothing here will catch a tired flier. Wildlife under the surface is possible and rarely seen; bandits do not work water this open.

The Working Grey.name: The Working Grey
The Working Grey.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Solid cloud covers nearly half the frame, pale and low, with the sea beneath it reduced to a dull working grey-blue band. The cloud base runs level, and the sea beneath it holds one tone from one side of the frame to the other. What foam there is shows brightly against the darker water. Light is weak and even. Swell comes through short and steep, and the crests turn over more often than the light on them suggests. The crossing is made by instrument, because the horizon has gone and the surface under the cloud base offers nothing to hold a heading against.
The Working Grey.hiddenInfo: Over The Working Grey the wind is the only fixed thing, and it changes. Ships bound for the Orbital Gate Station pass far above; nothing else uses this sky.

Sunpatch Water.name: Sunpatch Water
Sunpatch Water.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Patches of sun move across pale water as the cloud above breaks and re-forms, lighting the turquoise in the swell faces and leaving the rest grey. The turquoise appears only while the light is on it and goes out the moment the patch moves on. Foam lies along the crests in thin lines. Wind is variable in both strength and direction. Where the sun does reach, it carries into the water far enough to show the swell as a body rather than a surface. Fliers hold a heading rather than a track through this, and expect to be somewhere other than intended when the far side comes up.
Sunpatch Water.hiddenInfo: Sunpatch Water is transit air over deep water, crossed rather than visited. A downed traveller is a rescue only if someone saw them go down.

Greyed Channel Water.name: Greyed Channel Water
Greyed Channel Water.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Cooler-toned water, blue but greyed, moving in moderate swells that carry little foam. The swell runs long and rounded, lifting without steepening and passing on unbroken. The light is direct with almost no cloud to interrupt it, and yet the surface gives back less than the brighter seas northward do. Wind holds a steady moderate push across the whole reach. Light goes into the greyed water and is lost early, which is why the colour reads cold under an open sky. There is nothing in the frame to mark a position, and a flier has only heading, time and the set of the swell.
Greyed Channel Water.hiddenInfo: Open water with no landing under Greyed Channel Water: a flier who loses a heading here has only the sun to correct it. Nothing here needs story evidence except the weather.

Slate Water.name: Slate Water
Slate Water.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Slate-blue water, weightier than the sea further north, worked with white where the swell breaks and going almost grey in the shadowed troughs. The white does not travel far before it is taken back into the slate, leaving the ranks cleanly marked at their tops alone. The Verdant Coast closes the frame to the north. Cloud is negligible. The green edge along the northern frame is narrow and sits low, dropping out of sight with any loss of height. The swell runs in long ranks spaced widely enough to be counted from height, and fliers read the wind off its direction before committing to a longer leg.
Slate Water.hiddenInfo: Nothing marks Slate Water but swell; the crossing is made on held height and remembered bearing. Distance is the danger; the sea itself is indifferent.

Ink Water.name: Ink Water
Ink Water.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Ink-dark water fills this frame, so deep in colour that the swell shows as a change in sheen rather than as shape. The sheen moves across the frame in slow wide bands that give the only indication of which way the swell runs. The Verdant Coast lies north beyond the edge of it. Nothing breaks the surface and little light returns from it. Sky is clear and the light falls straight in, and none of it comes back out. Fliers get no sense of speed from what is below them here, and hold their altitude by instrument rather than by eye.
Ink Water.hiddenInfo: Ink Water offers no rock, no bar and no rest, and the light off it is the main hazard by midday. Wildlife under the surface is possible and rarely seen; bandits do not work water this open.

Slow Black Swells.name: Slow Black Swells
Slow Black Swells.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Slow black-blue swells pass beneath without breaking, wide apart and barely marked with white. The intervals between crests are long enough that the surface appears to stand still between them. The sky is clear and the sun high, and still the water gives almost nothing back. What white there is sits in small isolated flecks that never join into lines. Air above it is stable and quiet. This is the kind of sea that offers no reference at all, so crossings are flown on a set heading with the far coast as the only intended fix.
Slow Black Swells.hiddenInfo: The colour of Slow Black Swells says nothing about what lies beneath, and nothing here will catch a tired flier. Ships bound for the Orbital Gate Station pass far above; nothing else uses this sky.

Heavy Ridge Water.name: Heavy Ridge Water
Heavy Ridge Water.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Larger swell runs through here than through the water either side, mid-blue ridges with white tearing off their tops and settling into veined trails behind them. The ridges arrive in long ranks and the trails behind them run downwind in straight lengths. The sky is clear. Wind is strong and single in direction. Colour along the faces is brighter than in the troughs, where the water closes and takes the light in. Fliers feel the air working in sympathy with the sea below, and hold more height than the conditions strictly require because of it.
Heavy Ridge Water.hiddenInfo: Over Heavy Ridge Water the wind is the only fixed thing, and it changes. A downed traveller is a rescue only if someone saw them go down.

The Easing Swell.name: The Easing Swell
The Easing Swell.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Lighter blue returns in this water, the swell easing and the surface picking up more of the sky. With the swell down, the surface holds enough stillness to carry a broken image of the sky across most of the frame. Eastward the colour runs on into the pale channel of the Radiant Strait. Foam is sparse. The lightening eastward comes on gradually and is easiest to see from height, where the whole gradient lies in view at once. The light is clean and unbroken by cloud. Fliers approaching the strait from the west cross this on a falling line and take the paler water ahead as their marker.
The Easing Swell.hiddenInfo: The Easing Swell is transit air over deep water, crossed rather than visited. Weather arrives from the open quarter with little warning and no shelter.

The Deepening Channel.name: The Deepening Channel
The Deepening Channel.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Colour deepens through this part of the channel, the bright shallow read giving way to a heavier blue that takes light in rather than throwing it back. Swells arrive longer and further apart. The western side opens toward ocean, and a flier drifting that way loses the shelter of the strait without much warning, since under cloud the two waters look alike. The water opening west is Open Ocean, heavier again and slower to answer the wind. Light falls into the surface here instead of skipping off it, so the reach reads dull even under a clear sky.
The Deepening Channel.hiddenInfo: Open water with no landing under The Deepening Channel: a flier who loses a heading here has only the sun to correct it. Distance is the danger; the sea itself is indifferent.

Darkwater Strait.name: Darkwater Strait
Darkwater Strait.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] South along the channel the water brightens again between two darker reaches, running clear blue under a light swell. Black shelf rock edges the eastern side, and there are gaps in it where a flier can get down onto stone above the surf. Most movement through here runs the length of the strait rather than across it, so the traffic keeps to the middle. That shelf is the Ashen Coast, with pale grit banked against it above the reach of the water. The gaps are narrow and easily overshot, and they show from the air as breaks in the line of surf rather than as anything on the stone.
Darkwater Strait.hiddenInfo: Darkwater Strait holds standing water in its hollows and no soil worth the name. Starian bandits are not unknown on lonely coast, and cover here shelters them as readily as a traveller.

Grit Banks.name: Grit Banks
Grit Banks.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Drifts of pale grit bank against the black rock and thin out toward the water, leaving the last stretch before the surf bare and dark. Land holds most of this ground. The drifts are soft enough to slow a walker and firm enough to take a landing at their edges, while the bare rock nearer the sea stays wet and holds nothing at all. Radiant Strait runs west of the bare rock, and Grit Banks lies inland to the east behind the drifts. Each drift stands steep on its landward face and runs out shallow toward the sea, so a crossing made one way is a climb and the return a walk down.
Grit Banks.hiddenInfo: Along Grit Banks the line between sea and land moves with every set of swell. Wildlife works the tideline; a careless camp attracts it.

Black Dust Quarter.name: Black Dust Quarter
Black Dust Quarter.basicInfo: [Lv 4-60 · Moderate] Tight building and dark surfacing leave little open sand on this ground: modules and old stone set close, lanes narrow enough to hold shade for part of the day. Black Dust keeps a frontage among them, low-lit behind heavy plating, the sort of doorway found without signage. Environmental towers stand over the block with their ducting patched in visible layers. Roofs carry collectors and walkways both, and the landing shelves here are cut small. Underfoot the lanes are dark plate and old stone worn smooth, and sound stays inside them, held between walls that never open out. Part of Dustfall.
Black Dust Quarter.hiddenInfo: Three accounts of one woman cannot all be true. Nyra Sorel's claimed history does not match Ovar Kethrin's missing-person records in the Residential Rows or the identity files Miren Tal keeps at the North Routehead, and at least one of the three is a deliberate construction. Selka Vaereth negotiates for the Black Pennant at Tessik Luxaryn's tables and distrusts Nyra on an instinct she has not justified. With the Corsair shipment still missing, both Tessik and Nyra are offering a route toward the cargo network, and every offer attaches conditions that surface only after a crew has left. False safe-passage papers sell here at the same price as real ones, and the Dravon contact keeps his seat because everyone prefers knowing where he sits. Whoever buys a route first decides which story the settlement ends up believing.

The Guyed Stacks.name: The Guyed Stacks
The Guyed Stacks.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Almost all desert, wind-scored and pale, with built ground reduced to a few isolated stacks toward the western side. What stands is cargo modules weighted and guyed against the wind, collectors bolted flat to their roofs, work lamps burning on their corners for anyone coming in after dark. Nothing marks the limit of the settlement but beacon lines running out into the sand. Between the stacks the crust is bare and firm, drifted only where a wall breaks the wind. The air carries grit steadily enough that everything standing on this ground wears the same pale coat.
The Guyed Stacks.hiddenInfo: Cross The Guyed Stacks to reach Dustfall's real districts; it holds only what the city overflows. No one governs it, and the crews who live here defend it.

Dune Country.name: Dune Country
Dune Country.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Sand dominates this stretch, pale and dune-shaped wherever the wind has had room to work, with the occasional dark shelf of rock breaking the surface. Nothing tall grows on any of it. Dune faces slip in small sheets when they are climbed, taking a stride's worth of gain back at every step. Blown grit travels constantly at ankle height and stings higher when the wind gets up. The shelves stand barely above the sand, swept bare on their tops and drifted hard against on one side. Sound carries poorly across ground this soft, and the wind covers most of what there is.
Dune Country.hiddenInfo: Nothing at Dune Country is built, marked or watered; the beacon line is the nearest made thing. Refugees on foot come this way when the route is watched.

Broad Sand Flats.name: Broad Sand Flats
Broad Sand Flats.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Broad sand flats run through this part of the barrens, broken by weathered rock stubs and shallow dry channels that carry nothing at all. Scrub grows thinly along the channel margins. The light is unrelenting and the ground gives its heat back long after the glare has gone. Channel floors are smooth pale grit, firm and set a little below the flats, and the rock stubs are rounded, pitted and too low to shelter anything. A flier has level ground the whole way across and no reason to use it.
Broad Sand Flats.hiddenInfo: Sand at Broad Sand Flats is firm on the flats, laborious in the drifts, and dust rides every gust. Water stations do not exist out here; the Routehead has the last one.

Chalk Ground.name: Chalk Ground
Chalk Ground.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Chalky pale ground with almost no sand on it fills this stretch, hard under a boot and cut by shallow drainage lines running toward the coast. Scrub is reduced to scattered woody stubs. The drainage lines are shallow, straight-sided and floored with the same pale chip as the ground above them. Glare is severe wherever the surface is lightest. The ground breaks into flat pale chips that grind to dust under weight and coat everything crossing it. Open Ocean shows past the eastern edge, and the light off the water adds to the glare.
Chalk Ground.hiddenInfo: Chalk Ground is crossed by crews who know it and avoided by everyone else. Sandstorms are the defining hazard, warned down Dustfall's beacon line when there is time.

Dustlight Shallows.name: Dustlight Shallows
Dustlight Shallows.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Against the dry western edge where the Dust Barrens meet the water, the sea runs mid-blue and veined with broken white, its colour dulled by the pale ground beside it. The pale ground throws its own light onto the nearer water and takes the depth out of the colour there. Swell comes in short and steep. The sky is clear and the air off the land dry and hot. Short steep crests break early and often, and the white lies in small crossing pieces rather than in runs. Fliers working down this side stay out from the shore, where the air is steadier and cooler.
Dustlight Shallows.hiddenInfo: Nothing marks Dustlight Shallows but swell; the crossing is made on held height and remembered bearing. Wildlife under the surface is possible and rarely seen; bandits do not work water this open.

Cloud Shadow Sea.name: Cloud Shadow Sea
Cloud Shadow Sea.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Scattered cloud throws moving shadow across pale working water, the surface broken into short crests with foam between them. The cloud pieces are small and numerous, and their shadows cross the water faster than the swell beneath them. Colour shifts constantly between grey and a washed blue as the light comes and goes. The swell follows no single direction. Light reaching a sea this pale is returned at once and adds no depth to the colour. Fliers hold height for the lift in the sunlit gaps and accept the sink where the cloud shadow lies over the sea.
Cloud Shadow Sea.hiddenInfo: Cloud Shadow Sea offers no rock, no bar and no rest, and the light off it is the main hazard by midday. Ships bound for the Orbital Gate Station pass far above; nothing else uses this sky.

The Soft Blue.name: The Soft Blue
The Soft Blue.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Softer blue than the heavy water to the east, ruffled rather than swelling, with foam thin and scattered across it. The ruffling runs fine and even, with no long crests standing out of it anywhere. A little high cloud stands well clear of the surface. The light is diffuse enough that the horizon keeps its line. Colour comes back from just below the surface, which keeps the blue soft and slightly pale for open water. Nothing in the cell requires a change of course, and fliers cross it in whatever way the wind of the day makes easiest.
The Soft Blue.hiddenInfo: The colour of The Soft Blue says nothing about what lies beneath, and nothing here will catch a tired flier. A downed traveller is a rescue only if someone saw them go down.

The Rough Crossing.name: The Rough Crossing
The Rough Crossing.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Rough mid-blue water with white running across it in irregular seams, the swell steepening and breaking more often than in the calmer seas either side. Crests are pushed over before they are fully formed and collapse sideways, which is what leaves the seams crooked. The sky is clear. Wind has strength in it and comes across the run of the swell. Light falls on a surface too broken to return it evenly, and the water reads as a mass of small separate brightnesses. Fliers take the buffeting at height rather than descending, since the air lower down is worse where the surface works like this.
The Rough Crossing.hiddenInfo: Over The Rough Crossing the wind is the only fixed thing, and it changes. Weather arrives from the open quarter with little warning and no shelter.

Navy Deeps West.name: Navy Deeps West
Navy Deeps West.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Darkest of the open water in this quarter, a navy so heavy it reads nearly black under a clear sky, with the swell showing only where a crest catches an edge of light. Foam is rare. The swell passes slowly and with a long reach, lifting the whole frame at once rather than travelling across it. The air over it is still and stable. The colour is uniform to every edge and gives no hint of where the light is coming from. Fliers lose all sense of the surface as a moving thing here and treat it as a floor that simply happens to be there.
Navy Deeps West.hiddenInfo: Navy Deeps West is transit air over deep water, crossed rather than visited. Nothing here needs story evidence except the weather.

The Greyed Swells.name: The Greyed Swells
The Greyed Swells.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Greyed blue water lifting in moderate swells, veined with foam where the crests turn over and duller in colour than the brighter seas further out. The lit faces stand out pale against troughs that keep no light at all. High cloud is slight. Light falls at an angle and picks out the swell faces on one side only. Foam breaks into short veins that follow the run of the swell and fade within a few crests. Wind is steady and moderate, and the crossing is unremarkable except for the absence of anything to fix on.
The Greyed Swells.hiddenInfo: Open water with no landing under The Greyed Swells: a flier who loses a heading here has only the sun to correct it. Wildlife under the surface is possible and rarely seen; bandits do not work water this open.

The Still Dark.name: The Still Dark
The Still Dark.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Still, dark and slow, the water here barely lifts, and what swell there is passes under without breaking or catching light. The sky above is clear and empty. The water holds one tone from edge to edge with no gradient and no mark on it. The surface returns so little that from height it is hard to tell whether it moves at all. Air over it is as still as the surface, offering no lift, no sink and nothing to correct for. Fliers rely entirely on instrument, since a flat black plane gives no cue about altitude.
The Still Dark.hiddenInfo: Nothing marks The Still Dark but swell; the crossing is made on held height and remembered bearing. Ships bound for the Orbital Gate Station pass far above; nothing else uses this sky.

Featureless Navy.name: Featureless Navy
Featureless Navy.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Featureless navy water under an open sky, the swell long and heavy and marked with white only where two lines cross each other. The crossing points are few and far apart, and the white they raise is gone before the next pair meets. Colour is uniform from one edge of the frame to the other. Wind is moderate and does not shift. The two lines of swell run at a narrow angle to one another and neither of them takes the surface. Crews working this far out fly it as a single committed leg, because there is nothing below that would make stopping possible.
Featureless Navy.hiddenInfo: Featureless Navy offers no rock, no bar and no rest, and the light off it is the main hazard by midday. A downed traveller is a rescue only if someone saw them go down.

The Colour Boundary.name: The Colour Boundary
The Colour Boundary.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Half of what can be seen is bright strait water and half the darker water beyond its western edge, and the boundary between them wanders as the light changes. White veining crosses the surface of both. Air over this stretch is cooler and freer-moving than in the enclosed middle of the channel, and what cloud there is comes in from the western side. The darker water is Open Ocean, and the wandering boundary between the two is the only feature anywhere in the cell. Neither side carries anything on its surface, so a flier crossing has the colour and nothing else to work from.
The Colour Boundary.hiddenInfo: Over The Colour Boundary the wind is the only fixed thing, and it changes. Nothing here needs story evidence except the weather.

The Deep Channel.name: The Deep Channel
The Deep Channel.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Heavy blue water, less lit than the reaches to the north and slower to give up what lies under it. The eastern side carries the broken dark line of the Ashen Coast, with surf standing white in its gaps. Wind runs the length of the channel here rather than across it, which makes an eastward crossing short work and a southward run a long grind. The dark line on that side is shelf rock running out flat to a clean edge, and the surf standing in its gaps is the only white anywhere in the cell. Water here holds its colour under any light and gives no reading of what lies beneath it.
The Deep Channel.hiddenInfo: The Deep Channel is transit air over deep water, crossed rather than visited. Distance is the danger; the sea itself is indifferent.

The Flat Shelf.name: The Flat Shelf
The Flat Shelf.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Shelf rock runs out flat and unbroken to a clean edge, black above and blacker where the water covers it, the sea narrow in view but deep in colour. Neither grit nor growth breaks the surface. The whole of the shelf is crossable on foot and none of it offers cover, and the edge gives no warning other than the change in the sound. Open Ocean lies south past the edge, and Radiant Strait runs west along it. The shelf carries a slight fall toward the water across its whole width, shallow enough to go unnoticed on the way out and obvious on the way back.
The Flat Shelf.hiddenInfo: Glare off the bleached stone at The Flat Shelf is severe; dust rises with the afternoon wind and sits in the hollows. Ignivex patrols and Dravon incursions both cross this ground and neither holds it.

The Dark Terraces.name: The Dark Terraces
The Dark Terraces.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Terraces of dark stone step down toward the water, each riser sharp and each tread littered with fragments broken off the one above. Sea shows only at the lowest edge. The Dark Terraceswest lies inland of the terraces, and the treads are wide enough to walk and to land on, though the loose fragments make both slower than the level look suggests. Grit Banks stands to the north above the highest of the treads. The risers are cut clean and square, undercut where the stone below has weathered faster, and a walker coming down takes them one at a time.
The Dark Terraces.hiddenInfo: The crust at The Dark Terraces rings differently over old voids, and the sound is the only warning. Wildlife is scarce and what survives here is not gentle.

The Salt Ribs.name: The Salt Ribs
The Salt Ribs.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Coarse sand and scattered gravel floor this ground, with dark ribs of rock running through it and low scrub holding on in their lee. Salt carries faintly on the wind from the south, where the land falls away toward Ashen Coast. Heat sits heavy in the still air between the ribs. Gravel lies loose over firm ground between them and rolls underfoot at every stride, so the going sounds louder than it is. The ribs stand a stride across and run unbroken for long stretches, their tops swept bare and their flanks banked with sand. The Dark Terraceseast lies west past the open ground.
The Salt Ribs.hiddenInfo: The Salt Ribs is Dust Barrens ground: pale sand or gravel, scattered scrub, no shade worth the name and heat that arrives early. Wildlife is sparse, thirsty and occasionally dangerous.

The Thinning Barrens.name: The Thinning Barrens
The Thinning Barrens.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Toward the southern edge of the barrens the sand thins over dark rock and the mesas drop away to low broken shelves. Scrub survives in the cracks and nowhere else. Rock at the surface is dark, fine-grained and hot to the hand through the middle of the day, and it breaks along flat bedding lines wherever it has been disturbed. Air off the water beyond Ashen Coast carries damp into the dry heat without doing much to cool it. The shelves are stepped and flat-topped, littered with loose plate that shifts when it is trodden on. Light comes back up off the pale sand lying between them.
The Thinning Barrens.hiddenInfo: The mesas at The Thinning Barrens hold the only shadow, and the washes between them run dry and hard. Anything lost here is found by the Claimants or by no one.

The Bleached Ground.name: The Bleached Ground
The Bleached Ground.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Bleached ground runs to the water here, pale grit and salt crust lying over dark rock so that the coast reads grey rather than black. The sea opens out to the south and the east. Dry country stands inland and feeds the grit steadily, and the crust breaks under weight, which makes the firm dark rock better footing wherever it shows through. The dry country is the Dust Barrens, holding the ground north and west, and the water opening south and east is Open Ocean. Under a high sun the grey runs so even that it gives the eye nothing to judge height against, and a flier coming down works off the dark patches of rock instead.
The Bleached Ground.hiddenInfo: Where The Bleached Ground meets the water there is stone to stand on and little else; landings are possible and rarely worth it. The nearest help is the nearest city, and it is not close.

Blackstone Water.name: Blackstone Water
Blackstone Water.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Beside the dark rock of the Ashen Coast to the west, the water runs mid-blue with broken white across it, its colour thrown off by the black stone of the shoreline. The black stone takes all the light that reaches it and returns none, so the shore reads as an absence rather than as a line. Swell arrives obliquely and rebounds into a confused chop close in. Cloud is negligible. Out from the rock the swell recovers its shape and runs on with the white settling into short trails behind it. Fliers keep clear of the shore air here, which comes off the heated rock in rough rising columns.
Blackstone Water.hiddenInfo: Open water with no landing under Blackstone Water: a flier who loses a heading here has only the sun to correct it. Ships bound for the Orbital Gate Station pass far above; nothing else uses this sky.

Corner Water.name: Corner Water
Corner Water.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Corner sea, navy-dark and heavy, its long swells passing beneath without breaking and its colour unvaried to every edge. The swell comes from a single quarter and runs out of the frame without meeting anything to turn it. There is no cloud and no coast anywhere in the frame. Light falls straight in and comes back barely at all. The horizon closes as a hard ring of slightly lighter blue, and the only difference between sky and sea is which of them is darker. Anything crossing this water is doing so to reach somewhere else, and carries the whole leg in reserve, since nothing here supports a stop.
Corner Water.hiddenInfo: Nothing marks Corner Water but swell; the crossing is made on held height and remembered bearing. A downed traveller is a rescue only if someone saw them go down.

Navy Deeps.name: Navy Deeps
Navy Deeps.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Uniform navy from edge to edge, the swell so long that a flier passes over several crests without registering the change. The crests run wide and low and lift the surface without shaping it. No rock or spit interrupts the surface anywhere in frame. The sky is clear and the sun high, and the water absorbs almost all of it. Light goes down into the navy and returns a colour so nearly uniform that nothing anywhere offers an edge to settle on. Air is stable and the flying steady, but the absence of any visual reference makes altitude the thing most easily lost out here.
Navy Deeps.hiddenInfo: Navy Deeps offers no rock, no bar and no rest, and the light off it is the main hazard by midday. Weather arrives from the open quarter with little warning and no shelter.

The Black Water.name: The Black Water
The Black Water.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Black-blue water without a mark on it, the darkest tone anywhere in this sea, showing no foam, no colour change and no sign of the swell except a slow shift in sheen. The sheen travels from one side of the frame to the other at the pace of the swell beneath it. The sky is empty. Light enters and does not return, so the colour of the water is the colour of what lies under the light rather than of the light itself. Nothing at all distinguishes one part of the frame from another. The horizon holds a thin band of paler blue standing at the same height all the way round, with nothing on it to steer toward.
The Black Water.hiddenInfo: The colour of The Black Water says nothing about what lies beneath, and nothing here will catch a tired flier. Nothing here needs story evidence except the weather.

The Impenetrable Dark.name: The Impenetrable Dark
The Impenetrable Dark.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Impenetrable dark water, blue only by name, taking the sun without returning it and holding the same tone from one edge of the frame to the other. The surface carries no white at any point and shows its movement only as a slow tilting of the whole frame. The swell moves slowly and does not break. No cloud stands over it. Sky above is clear and pales toward the horizon, and the contrast between the two makes the water look heavier than it is. Crossings here are the longest sort of empty flying, and crews keep to a set altitude by habit, because nothing below will correct them.
The Impenetrable Dark.hiddenInfo: Over The Impenetrable Dark the wind is the only fixed thing, and it changes. Distance is the danger; the sea itself is indifferent.

The Veined Shallows.name: The Veined Shallows
The Veined Shallows.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Paler than the water either side of it, this sea runs a working mid-blue veined with white where the crests break. The veins break and re-form continually and never lie in the same place for long. Light cloud drifts high above. The swell shortens and steepens toward the northern edge of the frame. Light comes back from within the paler water and gives the colour a lit quality the darker seas beside it lack. Wind is moderate and consistent, and fliers use its steadiness to hold a line they have no other means of checking.
The Veined Shallows.hiddenInfo: The Veined Shallows is transit air over deep water, crossed rather than visited. Wildlife under the surface is possible and rarely seen; bandits do not work water this open.

Sombre Navy.name: Sombre Navy
Sombre Navy.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Sombre navy under a clear sky, the swells long and slow with almost no white on them. The colour deepens further toward the eastern edge. The deepening is gradual and shows only by looking from one edge of the frame across to the other. Air is quiet and the visibility unlimited, which counts for little when there is nothing in any direction to see. Swell faces carry a slightly lighter tone than the troughs, and that is all the shape the water shows. Fliers hold height and heading and expect the leg to look at its end exactly as it looked at its start.
Sombre Navy.hiddenInfo: Open water with no landing under Sombre Navy: a flier who loses a heading here has only the sun to correct it. A downed traveller is a rescue only if someone saw them go down.

The Strait Approach.name: The Strait Approach
The Strait Approach.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Where this heavy navy water runs east it begins to lift toward the paler tone of the Radiant Strait, though in frame it is still dark and slow, its swells wide and its surface almost unmarked. The lightening begins as a faint warming of tone along the eastern edge and strengthens beyond the frame. The sky is clear. Nothing returns from the water but a dull sheen. Swell runs on through the change without altering, so the surface gives no warning of it. Crews cross on instrument and take their first real fix off the change of colour ahead.
The Strait Approach.hiddenInfo: Nothing marks The Strait Approach but swell; the crossing is made on held height and remembered bearing. Weather arrives from the open quarter with little warning and no shelter.

The Southern Turn.name: The Southern Turn
The Southern Turn.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] At the southern corner of the bright channel the water turns dark and the swells lengthen, taking on the character of the Open Ocean lying north and west. Light no longer skips off the surface as it does further up the strait. This is where easy navigation ends, and a crossing from here is something to be planned and provisioned rather than simply begun. Open Ocean holds the whole of the northern and western view from this corner, and the water carries into it without a line on the surface anywhere. Swells arrive long and deep and lift a low flier through a slow rise and fall with nothing sharp in it.
The Southern Turn.hiddenInfo: The Southern Turn offers no rock, no bar and no rest, and the light off it is the main hazard by midday. Nothing here needs story evidence except the weather.

The Dark Turn.name: The Dark Turn
The Dark Turn.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Dark water fills this stretch, so deep in tone that under overcast it reads almost without colour and shows blue only when the sun is directly on it. Nothing floats and nothing breaks the surface. The bright shallow character of the channel has gone by this point, and a flier navigating by the colour of the water alone has little left to work with. Swells run long and low and arrive at intervals wide enough that the surface goes almost still between them. Wind crosses rather than follows the line of the water and raises no whitecaps worth the name.
The Dark Turn.hiddenInfo: The colour of The Dark Turn says nothing about what lies beneath, and nothing here will catch a tired flier. Distance is the danger; the sea itself is indifferent.

The Strait's End.name: The Strait's End
The Strait's End.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Navy water, heavy and slow, marks the southern limit of the channel where it gives out eastward into the Open Ocean. Swells run long and hold very little light. The air is cooler here than anywhere up the strait and carries more moisture with it, and cloud can close the whole reach in without leaving a horizon to fly against. Open Ocean takes the water east of this corner, and the change between the two is felt in the swell before it is seen in the colour. The surface lifts and settles without breaking anywhere across the cell.
The Strait's End.hiddenInfo: Over The Strait's End the wind is the only fixed thing, and it changes. Wildlife under the surface is possible and rarely seen; bandits do not work water this open.

Hemmed Dark Water.name: Hemmed Dark Water
Hemmed Dark Water.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Hemmed by the dark rock of the Ashen Coast on its northern and eastern sides, this water is nearly black, with a slow heavy swell and no foam to speak of. The rock stands in broken ridges along both those edges and drops to the water without a margin. Westward it runs into the paler channel of the Radiant Strait. The contrast between the stone and the sea is slight, both being dark, and at low height in poor light one can be taken for the other. Light in the middle of the frame is taken in completely, and the only brightness anywhere is the paler water toward the west.
Hemmed Dark Water.hiddenInfo: Hemmed Dark Water is transit air over deep water, crossed rather than visited. Ships bound for the Orbital Gate Station pass far above; nothing else uses this sky.

Cracked Slab Ground.name: Cracked Slab Ground
Cracked Slab Ground.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Cracked black rock covers effectively all of this ground, old flow split into slabs with narrow gaps between them and ash pressed into the gaps. The sea is not in sight from anywhere on it. Wind moves across without obstruction, the surface holds no water and grows nothing, and the slabs are level enough that a landing anywhere is much the same. Open Ocean lies west beyond the last of the flow and shows from none of it. The ash packed into the gaps has set hard and pale, drawing the whole crack pattern out in light lines across the black, and it takes no print at all under a boot.
Cracked Slab Ground.hiddenInfo: Cracked Slab Ground is old flow and ash: sharp underfoot, hot by afternoon and empty of anything living. Water is whatever a traveller carried in.

The Ridged Flows.name: The Ridged Flows
The Ridged Flows.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Flows of dark rock lie in long parallel ridges running toward the water, stopped where they stopped and rough along every edge. Only a thin margin of sea shows. The Dark Terraceswest lies inland of the ridges, and the troughs between them make the easier walking, though they close and open without pattern and force frequent climbs over. Each ridge ends in a blunt steep nose above the margin of water, dropping away too quickly to walk off, so a route that has followed a trough to its end has to turn back or go over. The crests are sharp where the rock broke and smooth where the flow ran, alternating within a stride.
The Ridged Flows.hiddenInfo: Nothing grows at The Ridged Flows; the ground takes heat in and gives it back after dark. Smuggling crews working around Ignivex's eastern mountains cut through ground like this by timing and local knowledge.

Windtrail Shore.name: Windtrail Shore
Windtrail Shore.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Blown grit lies in thin trails across black stone, marking out how the wind runs along this coast rather than across it. Most of the cell is rock, with the sea taking a dark strip at the southern side. The surf is heavy against the low edge, and the ground back from it is solid and open, which makes it straightforward both to cross and to land on. The Dark Terraces holds the ground inland to the north. The grit banks on the downwind side of every crack in the stone and leaves the upwind side swept bare, so each crack carries a pale streak on one flank and none on the other.
Windtrail Shore.hiddenInfo: The fissures and tubes of Windtrail Shore give real shade and real drops, and cut across any line of travel. Cover here shelters danger as readily as travellers; Starian bandits use it, given story evidence.

Pale Dust Shelf.name: Pale Dust Shelf
Pale Dust Shelf.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Fine pale material covers the dark rock over most of this ground, deep enough to smooth the surface and to take a print. No waterline lies within sight of it. Dry inland country stands behind and the wind moves the loose layer steadily, and under all of it the rock is unbroken, so the footing is soft but never uncertain. That inland country is The Dark Terraces, standing to the north. A print pressed into the pale layer holds its edges at first and softens as the wind works at it, so the age of a track can be read off how sharp it still is.
Pale Dust Shelf.hiddenInfo: Pale Dust Shelf is Ashen Wastes country, where the horizon repeats itself and a heading is hard to keep. Ignivex patrols and Dravon incursions both cross this ground and neither holds it.

Fractured Edge.name: Fractured Edge
Fractured Edge.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Fractured rock makes up this ground, black slabs broken small and lying at angles, with pale grit filling between them and the sea reduced to a thin dark line. Nothing green appears anywhere on it. The Dark Terraceseast lies inland, and the grit-filled ground between the slabs is the only surface here even enough to bring a flier down on. The slabs lean consistently one way across whole stretches, as though the ground shifted once beneath them, and a walker going with the lean crosses faster than one going against it.
Fractured Edge.hiddenInfo: Glare off the bleached stone at Fractured Edge is severe; dust rises with the afternoon wind and sits in the hollows. Wildlife is scarce and what survives here is not gentle.

The Bare Margin.name: The Bare Margin
The Bare Margin.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Heavy navy water works the southern edge of this rock, rising against it and drawing back without leaving anything behind: no sand, no drift, no soft margin. Stone takes most of the cell. The dark surface is broken but broadly level, and it stays dry back from the edge, which is where anyone arriving by air puts down. The Dust Barrens carry the ground inland to the north, open and dry to the limit of sight. The edge itself is a clean step rather than a slope, low enough to sit down on and high enough that the water never comes over it, which keeps the stone behind it dry while everything below stays wet.
The Bare Margin.hiddenInfo: The shore at The Bare Margin is walkable at the cost of wet footing, and the surf covers the sound of anything approaching. Nothing crosses here on any schedule.

The Salt Wind Shore.name: The Salt Wind Shore
The Salt Wind Shore.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Weathered black stone runs along the water, rounded where the surf reaches it and sharp everywhere above, with open sea beginning on the eastern side. Land holds the larger part of this cell and carries nothing living on it. The wind is constant and salted, and the rock stays wet across a broad band because the spray carries well inland of the surf. The Dust Barrens stand inland to the north, and the sea beginning east is Open Ocean. The line between the rounded stone and the sharp above it runs level along the whole shore, and it marks the reach of the water better than anything else here.
The Salt Wind Shore.hiddenInfo: The Salt Wind Shore is a margin rather than a place: salt, rock and the swell working at both. The route inland is whatever the rock allows.

The Last Water.name: The Last Water
The Last Water.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Last of the open water on this side, dark navy and slow, with the swell arriving from the north and passing on without breaking. The swell arrives evenly spaced and loses nothing in crossing the frame. The colour is heavy and takes in the light rather than returning it. Nothing stands in the frame but sea. Sky is clear and the light falls steeply, and still the surface returns only a dull even sheen. Fliers reaching this corner turn back along the coast rather than continuing, since there is nothing further out to make for.
The Last Water.hiddenInfo: Nothing marks The Last Water but swell; the crossing is made on held height and remembered bearing. Nothing here needs story evidence except the weather.

High Ridge Air.name: High Ridge Air
High Ridge Air.basicInfo: [Transit · High] High air above the massif, empty except for thin cloud that forms and tears apart again within the hour. Rock appears only along the lower edge of what can be seen, pale ridges holding snow in their shaded faces. There is no footing in this cell whatever: a flier crossing it is between summits with nothing underneath, and cold and moving air are the whole of the conditions. Nothing in the frame holds still: the cloud shifts, the light on the rock below changes with it, and the ridgelines come and go from one moment to the next. Sound carries poorly at this height and the wind is the only thing to be heard.
High Ridge Air.hiddenInfo: High Ridge Air is crossed at height and never on foot, and the cold takes the unprepared first. Rescue at this height is a Contair drone or nothing.

Armada Shelf.name: Armada Shelf
Armada Shelf.basicInfo: [Lv 3-48 · Moderate] Cloud stands against this shoulder of the massif, pale across the long shuttered faces of the Armada Holds and the quieter frontage of the Myralis Continuum. Built ground is sparse — a few broad platforms, flight lanes marked in cobalt, and a great deal of open air past the rim. The rock beneath carries the same repaired layering as the rest of the outer edge. The platforms are curved white plate over charcoal understructure, damp where cloud has drifted across them, and the walkways between run short and railed. Little sound reaches out here but air moving over the shutters. A walker finds few routes; a flier finds most of the ground. Part of Vexorath.
Armada Shelf.hiddenInfo: The Inactive Personality Review Bay inside Armada Holds holds the hardest open question in the city, and no case there is resolved: a quirky drone is not automatically a person, and a construct is not denied review because its individuality emerged unintentionally. Tavris Contair administers the doctrine that keeps Ward units out of private homes without emergency cause and Aegis units off routine enforcement, and the Echo-Class work stays restricted: each shell models a consenting living Starian's appearance, voice and technique without memory or identity, on a limited deployment period with a reset plan. Avara Myralis's medical veto is intact. One Echo authorisation and one review-bay case are both approaching their period limits in the same tenday, and the two decisions are being watched as one.

The Strait Gate.name: The Strait Gate
The Strait Gate.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Bright blue water runs edge to edge, lifting in long swells that the light rakes into moving silver. This is the northern opening of the channel, where the enclosed brightness gives way to the heavier tone of the Open Ocean, and a grey shoulder of the Silver Peaks stands off to the east. Fliers keep that rock as their one fixed mark, since the surface below offers nothing at all to steer by. The swell arriving from the open side sets against the run of the channel and leaves the surface confused, crests standing rather than travelling.
The Strait Gate.hiddenInfo: The Strait Gate is transit air over deep water, crossed rather than visited. Nothing here needs story evidence except the weather.

The Snowline.name: The Snowline
The Snowline.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Bare rock makes up nearly all of this ground: grey, fractured, stepping up in ledges too narrow to shelter on. Snow survives only in the seams that never take direct light. The slope drops southward into the dark conifer of the Highland Forest and climbs eastward toward Mist Under Canopy, and the wind across the open faces is strong enough to matter to anything on foot. Frost works the fractured rock apart and leaves fresh edges on it, so the ledges shed fragments onto whatever lies below them. The ground offers nothing to get out of the wind behind, and the walking is a matter of picking between one narrow step and the next.
The Snowline.hiddenInfo: The Snowline is high ground and higher air; weather crosses it in bands and visibility swings from clean to nothing. Vexorath's approach lanes are marked; everything off them is not.

The Glare Crossing.name: The Glare Crossing
The Glare Crossing.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Glare comes off this stretch through the whole middle of the day, the water lit so evenly that it reads flat until a swell passes beneath and the light slides across it. Nothing stands above the surface. Crossing fliers hold a steady line and a steady height, because dropping low buys no shelter and costs the horizon that keeps a heading honest. Open Ocean lies north and west, darker in tone and heavier in its swell, and the boundary between the two waters is a change of colour with nothing on the surface to mark it. The channel's own set runs along its length here rather than across, so anything adrift on it travels steadily.
The Glare Crossing.hiddenInfo: The Glare Crossing offers no rock, no bar and no rest, and the light off it is the main hazard by midday. Weather arrives from the open quarter with little warning and no shelter.

Steepfall Timber.name: Steepfall Timber
Steepfall Timber.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Conifer stands close and dark on ground that pitches too steeply to hold a footing, so the canopy reads from above as one continuous mass with no gap wide enough to drop into. Bare rock shows over it to the north. What routes exist follow the contour and double back where the slope allows nothing else, and the timber runs on southward toward The Outer Blockworks. That bare rock is the Silver Peaks, standing above the last of the trees. Under the canopy the ground is deep in needle litter over roots and holds the wet long after the open ground above has dried.
Steepfall Timber.hiddenInfo: Under the canopy at Steepfall Timber the going is tracks and roots, and the glow-growth on wet stone does the lighting after dusk. Wildlife is the ordinary hazard; Starian bandits the less ordinary one, and both need story evidence.

Eastern Shoulder Forest.name: Eastern Shoulder Forest
