Eastern Shoulder Forest.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Dense conifer covers the eastern shoulder of the massif, broken where the slope steepens into bare stone and where running water has stripped a channel through it. Between the trees the footing is loose and tilted. Grey rock stands above on two sides, and downhill the forest thins toward Dustward Edge, which is the usual way off the slope for anyone on foot. The grey rock above is the Silver Peaks, closing the slope on both of those sides. The stripped channels are floored with loose stone and run straight down the gradient, which makes them quick to descend and difficult to stop in.
Eastern Shoulder Forest.hiddenInfo: Nothing is built at Eastern Shoulder Forest; the forest here is a thing cities lean on rather than a place they own. Cities patrol their own edges and nothing past them.

The Last Shoulder.name: The Last Shoulder
The Last Shoulder.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Sky and cloud take up most of this frame, the last pale shoulders of the range standing along its lower margin with the sea running out flat beyond them. In haze the two blues are hard to tell apart. This is the outer corner of the high country, where the ridges give out and the ground below drops toward The North Route, and the air over it is cold, damp and rarely still. That sea is Open Ocean, running out past the last of the stone with nothing on it. The shoulders here carry less snow than the ridges inland and hold their grey throughout.
The Last Shoulder.hiddenInfo: The Last Shoulder is crossed at height and never on foot, and the cold takes the unprepared first. The cold arrives with the shadow and leaves with it.

Tidemark Bay.name: Tidemark Bay
Tidemark Bay.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Water dominates, mid-blue and veined white where the swell turns over itself, with a broken rock margin holding the eastern side. Salt-killed growth clings in the seams of the stone and gives out well short of the waterline. The worked ground of The Northern Ledges stands beyond that margin, and the only easy landing is the flat rock above the surf. Northward the water opens out into Open Ocean and loses its veining; southward the dark cover of Luminous Forest closes the horizon. The margin rings hollow underfoot where blocks have parted from one another, and the gaps between them are wide enough to catch a boot.
Tidemark Bay.hiddenInfo: Tidemark Bay holds standing water in its hollows and no soil worth the name. Nothing crosses here on any schedule.

Black Rock Bight.name: Black Rock Bight
Black Rock Bight.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Rock stands high along this stretch, pale stone faces dropping straight into dark navy water that carries no light back up. Wind-cut growth holds the tops in low mats, and coarse sand collects where the rock steps down. The Fringe Water lies inland behind the headland tops, and fliers use the level ground above the faces because the base offers none. The Northern Ledgeseast holds the ground to the west, and the water runs north into Open Ocean. Air lifts hard along the faces where the wind meets them, so a flier working in along the top can ride that lift instead of climbing for it.
Black Rock Bight.hiddenInfo: Along Black Rock Bight the line between sea and land moves with every set of swell. The route inland is whatever the rock allows.

Ironstone Point.name: Ironstone Point
Ironstone Point.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Almost the whole of this cell is open water, bright and unshadowed, the swells long enough that a low flier loses sight of everything but the next crest. No rock or islet shows above the water anywhere in frame. Dark forest shows along one horizon as a low unbroken band, and until a crossing reaches it there is no ground underneath at all. That band is Luminous Forest, and it is the only edge in view worth working toward. Eastward the water brightens where Radiant Strait begins; northward it deepens into Open Ocean with no line to mark the change.
Ironstone Point.hiddenInfo: Nothing marks Ironstone Point but swell; the crossing is made on held height and remembered bearing. Weather arrives from the open quarter with little warning and no shelter.

The Shelving Shallows.name: The Shelving Shallows
The Shelving Shallows.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Along the western side of the channel the water stays clear and bright, shelving paler as it approaches the green rim of the Verdant Coast. Surf shows there as a thin white line. The crossing is short-tempered in wind and easy in calm, and solid ground lies within reach to the west for a flier who would rather set down than press on. The paler water runs over ground that comes up gradually rather than in steps, so the change in colour is gradual too and gives a fair reading of what lies beneath. Wind crossing off the land arrives uneven and meets the channel's own set at an angle, which puts a short chop on the surface that does not travel far.
The Shelving Shallows.hiddenInfo: The Shelving Shallows offers no rock, no bar and no rest, and the light off it is the main hazard by midday. Nothing here needs story evidence except the weather.

Broken Flow Coast.name: Broken Flow Coast
Broken Flow Coast.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Volcanic rock makes up nearly all of this ground, dark grey and broken, with grit collected in the lows and the sea confined to one narrow side. Nothing grows on it. The surface is old flow, hard-edged and awkward underfoot, and fliers prefer the grit flats to the rock because a landing on the flow risks putting a foot through the crust. Silver Peaks rises to the north and Ashen Peaks closes the ground southward, with The Outer Blockworks standing off to the east. The old flow keeps its ropy set in patches, ridged in tight curves that trip a stride taken at speed.
Broken Flow Coast.hiddenInfo: Broken Flow Coast is old flow and ash: sharp underfoot, hot by afternoon and empty of anything living. Smuggling crews working around Ignivex's eastern mountains cut through ground like this by timing and local knowledge.

The Long Surf.name: The Long Surf
The Long Surf.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Broken stone edges the water on the landward side, wet and dark where the swell washes over it and grey above that. The rest is open blue. Trees begin close behind the rock and run inland without much of a transition, so a walker leaving the surf is under canopy almost at once and out of the wind with it. Those trees are the outer edge of Luminous Forest, which holds the ground both east and south of the stone. Water left on the rock by each set drains back through one gap and makes a sucking noise well out of time with the surf.
The Long Surf.hiddenInfo: The shore at The Long Surf is walkable at the cost of wet footing, and the surf covers the sound of anything approaching. A stranded hull or a lost load washes up here before anyone reports it missing.

The Fringe Water.name: The Fringe Water
The Fringe Water.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Water takes nearly a third of the frame, deep navy and heavy, and the forest that reaches it is reduced to a fringe on ground already given over to surfacing and structure. Little glow survives where the canopy has been opened. The Fringe Water lies west across the worked ground, and the tracks here run toward it rather than into the trees. A flier has the shoreline as a guide for the whole crossing. Verdant Coast holds the water north and east of the worked ground, so the shoreline carries on in both directions from this frame. Underfoot the surfacing is hard and even where it has been laid and churned into ruts where it has not.
The Fringe Water.hiddenInfo: The Fringe Water is a margin rather than a place: salt, rock and the swell working at both. The nearest help is the nearest city, and it is not close.

The Bright Offing.name: The Bright Offing
The Bright Offing.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Open water, evenly bright, moving in swells that arrive without fixed rhythm and pass on. The surface gives back so much light at midday that the horizon softens and the far shore goes uncertain. Ground lies only to the west, a dark forested line seen edge-on, and a flier wanting to come down commits to reaching it rather than looking for anything nearer. That line is Luminous Forest, and nothing else stands above the water in any other direction. Radiant Strait begins north and east of here, brighter again and shallower in its reading, so the water changes character twice inside a single crossing.
The Bright Offing.hiddenInfo: Nothing marks The Bright Offing but swell; the crossing is made on held height and remembered bearing. Nothing here needs story evidence except the weather.

Forest-Shadow Channel.name: Forest-Shadow Channel
Forest-Shadow Channel.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Close under the western shore the channel shallows and the blue turns clearer and paler, with darker lanes marking where the bottom falls away. Behind the broken shoreline the canopy of the Luminous Forest stands dark and continuous. This is the sheltered edge of the water, and low fliers and boat traffic work along it rather than commit to the open middle. The broken shoreline itself is Verdant Coast, running north and south of this reach in the same low line. Air along the edge is smoother than out in the channel and holds its direction, since the land takes the worst of the wind before it reaches the water.
Forest-Shadow Channel.hiddenInfo: The shore at Forest-Shadow Channel is walkable at the cost of wet footing, and the surf covers the sound of anything approaching. The nearest help is the nearest city, and it is not close.

Brightfall Gravel.name: Brightfall Gravel
Brightfall Gravel.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Light comes through this canopy more than most, the trees carrying a lighter green and standing further apart over ground that drains well. Water lies at the eastern edge of the frame below Hundred Houses. Streams run clear over gravel and are easy to cross on foot. The pale growth here is abundant but washed out by the daylight that reaches it, and only comes into its own well after dusk. The lighter canopy lets wind down to the floor and keeps the undergrowth low and open between the trunks. Gravel in the stream beds is clean and pale and shows through the water from any angle.
Brightfall Gravel.hiddenInfo: Under the canopy at Brightfall Gravel the going is tracks and roots, and the glow-growth on wet stone does the lighting after dusk. The forest hides a camp well and a fire badly.

Dark Water Margin.name: Dark Water Margin
Dark Water Margin.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Forest comes down the slope and stops where the salt starts, the last growth stunted and hard-leaved, standing over dark navy water that gives back little light. Land takes most of this cell. Starfall Quarter lies behind the treeline, and the walkable ground is the bench between the trees and the drop rather than anything at the waterline. Eastward the water runs bright again where Radiant Strait begins, so the dark water below this slope is narrow seen against it. The bench carries stone fallen from the ground above, blocks lying where they stopped, and the walking threads between them rather than over them.
Dark Water Margin.hiddenInfo: Fliers use Dark Water Margin as a coast mark; walkers find the going slow and the shelter poor. Starian bandits are not unknown on lonely coast, and cover here shelters them as readily as a traveller.

Old Flow Road.name: Old Flow Road
Old Flow Road.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Old flow country, almost entirely stone: dark grey to black, lying in long low rolls with ash gathered in the seams. No water shows from anywhere on it. A worked road runs through the middle, and off the road the surface alternates between solid rock and hollow-sounding crust often enough that most traffic stays on the worked line. The road is The North Route, arriving from the north and carrying on south, and the Ashen Wastes hold the ground to the west. Ash lying in the seams takes a print deeply and keeps it, so what has crossed away from the road stays legible between one weather and the next.
Old Flow Road.hiddenInfo: Old Flow Road carries freight tracks, dust and the marks of every crew that passed, none of them named. Skirmishes between the competing claims keep regular patrol off the line.

The Low Dark Shore.name: The Low Dark Shore
The Low Dark Shore.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Half water and half low dark shore, the division running through this ground without much to mark it: no cliff, no stand of trees, only stone that goes under the swell and comes back out of it. Light is flat here. Nothing grows worth the name, and a flier who sets down finds ground that is firm but wet through, useful as a stopping place and little else. Open Ocean lies both north and south of this stretch, so the shore reads as a dark interruption in a long run of water. Under the flat light the wet stone gives back no colour at all and the whole cell reads in greys, which makes the waterline hard to place from any height until a set moves across it.
The Low Dark Shore.hiddenInfo: The Low Dark Shore holds standing water in its hollows and no soil worth the name. A stranded hull or a lost load washes up here before anyone reports it missing.

Trackfall Stand.name: Trackfall Stand
Trackfall Stand.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Long stands of full-height forest run across this cell with little cleared between them, the floor deep in litter and broken by rock at intervals. One worn line of foot tracks runs east toward The Barge Terracewest and carries most of what passes through. Streams cut shallow beds and cross it without difficulty. Glowing growth is heavy on the shaded rock faces and sparse wherever the sun gets in. Verdant Coast holds the shore west past the last of the stands. The litter on the floor is deep and dry and carries sound badly, so movement through the cell is quieter than the closeness of the trees suggests.
Trackfall Stand.hiddenInfo: Trackfall Stand is Luminous Forest country: close cover, small watercourses and quiet that carries sound a long way. The canopy gives no landing; the clearings decide the route.

The Barge Terrace.name: The Barge Terrace
The Barge Terrace.basicInfo: [Lv 9-66 · Low] Water takes a fifth of this ground and most of its noise. Cargo ramps and stairways cut down from the terraces to the Barge Quays, where hulls lie against wet stone and loads swing up on skyhook cable through the working day. Mornings come cold off the river and the paving stays dark long after. The Open Circle holds clear ground above the loading, amber-lit at its margins, and route-boards on every corner run the day's colour-codes for what moves and when. Quay stone underfoot is grooved for grip and worn smooth at the ramp heads where loads are dragged across it. Fliers keep out of the cable arcs and come down on the terrace instead. Part of Helvyra.
The Barge Terrace.hiddenInfo: Imma Dray refused a rich contract to haul unmarked crates and the client did not take it well, so the crates found another hull and the Drays are watching the berth line to see whose. Tolvir Nash of the Bank Wardens has an impossible question: cargo went into the river upstream and never surfaced anywhere on a river the wardens work this closely, and the trackers involved may connect to the non-Dravon signal Dustfall keeps raising. On the Open Circle's island, piecework charms failed on the same day, the Circle and the Yalven Forgeworks are publicly committed to explanations that are both wrong, and Quenna Sil is holding a student's route-charm that worked where route-charms cannot. Maelrix Corsair makes every unexplained result political, and the high season will raise the water before any of it is settled.

Thornbreak Scrub.name: Thornbreak Scrub
Thornbreak Scrub.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Thin forest stands over firm rolling ground, the canopy broken enough that the undergrowth beneath it grows tall and tangles the spaces between trunks. Rock breaks the surface along the higher lines. Tracks run east toward Windbreak Edgewest and south toward Verdant Coast, both worn and neither surfaced. Glow after dusk is moderate and comes mostly off the tangled growth at chest height rather than off the floor. Verdant Coast holds the ground south and west, so two sides of the cell open toward water. The tall undergrowth between the trunks is springy and hard to push through and forces the tracks to hold their lines.
Thornbreak Scrub.hiddenInfo: Thornbreak Scrub is walkable, crossable on foot in a day and easier from the air, where the canopy reads as one surface. A lost traveller here is found by the streams, which all run somewhere.

The Cold Steps.name: The Cold Steps
The Cold Steps.basicInfo: [Lv 3-10 · Low] Stone stairways drop level after level toward the water, the terraces narrow and stacked, Riverrow's frontages built right out to the lip of the fall. Cold-store doors along the Cold Pour District breathe chilled air into the lanes and keep their thresholds wet; below the paving the Underbank runs lit passages beneath the working levels. Lantern amber does most of the lighting once the light goes. The steps are worn hollow in their middles and run with meltwater where the cold stores stand open, so footing changes from dry to slick within a stride. Barge traffic moves below in both directions and the crane towers track it. Part of Helvyra.
The Cold Steps.hiddenInfo: Tam Vessic keeps a ledger of who climbed the terraces and who simply stopped appearing, and three recent Underbank tenants are in the second column: gone within a month, rent paid in advance, rooms untouched. Paid-forward rent means whoever arranged it expected them not to need the rooms, which is not the same as tenants who ran, and the Shared Wash House already knows more than the ledger. In the Long Pour's cellar Essim Corle holds a Quilrath vintage nobody will admit importing, the thread-end of a smuggling line the Dravon Disconnection says cannot exist, and Xyren Corsair drinks regularly in the one district where conversations go unrecorded. The Bank Wardens hold only the water edge; the rooms above are nobody's to investigate until someone insists.

The Green Shore Channel.name: The Green Shore Channel
The Green Shore Channel.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Green forest comes nearly to the waterline on the western side, the dark canopy of the Luminous Forest standing above a short broken shore. Water off it is clear and bright, paling over the near bottom. Air on this flank carries more moisture than the open middle, and low cloud forms over the trees early before drifting out across the channel. North of this reach the shore turns to the rock of the Verdant Coast, so the tree line ends and the margin hardens within sight of it. The low cloud lies in a flat layer that thins as it crosses and is gone before it reaches the middle of the channel.
The Green Shore Channel.hiddenInfo: Fliers use The Green Shore Channel as a coast mark; walkers find the going slow and the shelter poor. A stranded hull or a lost load washes up here before anyone reports it missing.

Clifftop Green.name: Clifftop Green
Clifftop Green.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Little land shows here, a thin bright line of rock along one side and open blue everywhere else, the swells running long and breaking only against that line. Growth is negligible. Anyone working this stretch on foot is on wet stone most of the way, and the flying route stays out over the water because the shore gives so little to follow. Open Ocean holds the water west and south, and the bright line of stone stands between the two reaches. The rock is pale enough to read almost white under strong light and shows from well out, which makes it useful as a mark even where it is useless as ground.
Clifftop Green.hiddenInfo: Along Clifftop Green the line between sea and land moves with every set of swell. Nothing crosses here on any schedule.

The Brightwater Edge.name: The Brightwater Edge
The Brightwater Edge.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Most of this ground is land: green over broken rock, with pale sand collected in the low places and the sea showing only as a bright edge along one side. Wind comes across it steadily and keeps the growth short. The walking is straightforward, the footing changes from turf to grit without warning, and the open sand takes a landing where the turf does not. Luminous Forest closes the ground north and west, and the bright edge east is Radiant Strait. Broken rock shows through the turf as flat plates the size of a stride, level with the surface and easy to cross until one lifts underfoot.
The Brightwater Edge.hiddenInfo: The shore at The Brightwater Edge is walkable at the cost of wet footing, and the surf covers the sound of anything approaching. Wildlife works the tideline; a careless camp attracts it.

Veined Water Crossing.name: Veined Water Crossing
Veined Water Crossing.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Surface veining of white crosses mid-blue water where the swell coming up the channel meets the set running along the western shore. That rim is green and cliffed, with surf working at its foot. Landing on it is possible and rarely convenient, so most traffic stays out over the water, where the air runs smoother and the going is more predictable. The green rim is the Verdant Coast, turf over broken rock with sand in its low places. The veining forms and disperses along one line that keeps its position through the day, which makes it the most reliable mark anywhere on this part of the channel.
Veined Water Crossing.hiddenInfo: Veined Water Crossing offers no rock, no bar and no rest, and the light off it is the main hazard by midday. Weather arrives from the open quarter with little warning and no shelter.

The Surf Ledge.name: The Surf Ledge
The Surf Ledge.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Flat shelving rock runs under the swell at a shallow angle, so the waterline shifts across it and the wet stone reaches well beyond where the surf actually breaks. The colour of the water is a settled mid-blue. Walking is possible along the whole shelf and slippery for all of it, and the dry ground above is where a flier comes down. Luminous Forest stands inland to the north above the dry ground. Between sets a thin film runs back down the whole slope of the shelf and keeps it wet where nothing has broken over it, so the footing is poor well above the reach of the surf.
The Surf Ledge.hiddenInfo: Along The Surf Ledge the line between sea and land moves with every set of swell. The route inland is whatever the rock allows.

Windscour Beach.name: Windscour Beach
Windscour Beach.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Ground holds nearly all of this cell, a mix of low green and grey broken rock, with the sea reduced to a bright strip along one side. Wind arrives salted and does not let the vegetation stand tall. Between the rock outcrops the turf is firm and open, which makes the whole stretch usable for landing and unremarkable to cross on foot. Luminous Forest holds the ground northward beyond the last of the outcrops. The rock stands proud in rounded backs rather than edges, worn smooth on top and easy to walk over.
Windscour Beach.hiddenInfo: Where Windscour Beach meets the water there is stone to stand on and little else; landings are possible and rarely worth it. Wildlife works the tideline; a careless camp attracts it.

Greywater Shelf.name: Greywater Shelf
Greywater Shelf.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Thick green covers this ground right to the point where the salt stops it, running unbroken over low rises with only a little pale sand showing through toward the shore. The water is a narrow bright band along the southern side. Worked river country lies inland, and the level turf here takes flight traffic easily, being open, dry underfoot and clear of standing rock. That worked river country is The Longreach, north beyond the last of the green, and the bright band south opens into Open Ocean. The rises run in long parallel swells of ground, low enough to see over and regular enough to set a walker's rhythm.
Greywater Shelf.hiddenInfo: The shore at Greywater Shelf is walkable at the cost of wet footing, and the surf covers the sound of anything approaching. A stranded hull or a lost load washes up here before anyone reports it missing.

The Surf Wall.name: The Surf Wall
The Surf Wall.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Growth covers most of what lies here, deep and low and shaped by the wind into one continuous slope toward the water. Sand shows in thin streaks near the edge of it. Surf works a short run of rock at the foot of the slope, loud enough to hear from well back, and the ground above is even enough to cross at speed on foot. Luminous Forest stands above the slope north, and the water south runs into Open Ocean. The cover is matted tight enough to carry a stride on its surface rather than through it, and a fall onto it is broken rather than cushioned.
The Surf Wall.hiddenInfo: The Surf Wall is a margin rather than a place: salt, rock and the swell working at both. The nearest help is the nearest city, and it is not close.

Cliffside Calm.name: Cliffside Calm
Cliffside Calm.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Cliffed green ground stands to the west, and the water runs bright up to its foot and breaks there in a white line visible from well out. Out from that edge the channel is evenly blue and calm-reading. Wind is lighter through this stretch than further up the strait, and fliers use the easy air to gain height before committing eastward over open water. That western ground is the Verdant Coast, dark stone standing over water that does not brighten under it. The white line at its foot marks where surf enters the fissures in the face and comes back out, and it holds the same position through any weather.
Cliffside Calm.hiddenInfo: Cliffside Calm holds standing water in its hollows and no soil worth the name. The route inland is whatever the rock allows.

The Gate Apron.name: The Gate Apron
The Gate Apron.basicInfo: [Lv 10-16 · Moderate] Pale sand covers most of this ground, wind-scored into long low ridges that reset after every strong blow. The Lunar Gate Yard holds the built edge of it — dust-scored plating, a cleared apron kept swept, flight markers set out in a line where the surfacing stops. Structures around the yard are cargo modules stacked two and three high with salvaged panel welded over the joints. Daylight comes down hard and flat. The crust breaks to loose sand a stride off the apron, so wheeled traffic keeps to the plating and everything else walks. Wind is the steady sound, working the guy lines and the loose panel edges. Part of Dustfall.
The Gate Apron.hiddenInfo: The Lunar Gate Yard is one failed part away from a decision nobody can make. The missing Corsair shipment carried gate components, and if the failed part is not locally replaceable the gate will degrade in a way nobody here can arrest. Repair is a standing negotiation between Halvora Orvantis's expertise, Tiva Nhalor's smaller work, Sura Venn's tracker knowledge, rare contracted technicians and whatever Veyra Corsair can obtain. Behind it sits the political question: whether Dustfall should deliberately close its gate for a period under Dravon pressure and stay unmonitored, cutting itself off from Relstaris, Ignivex and Helvyra at once. Respected locals, gangs, households and crews would all have to live with that and none of them can decide it. The Unregistered Arrival Bench keeps taking people who cannot be recorded. The next gate cycle that stutters starts the argument for real.

Stony Pavement.name: Stony Pavement
Stony Pavement.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Stony desert with little loose sand covers this ground, the surface a pavement of dark chips set in pale grit. Scrub is almost absent. What little there is grows flat against the pavement rather than up out of it. Wind comes off the sea beyond Ashen Coast and keeps the air moving without making it cool. The chips are sharp, close-set and loud underfoot, and they lie level enough that a flier can come down almost anywhere across the pavement. Nothing standing on this ground breaks a sightline.
Stony Pavement.hiddenInfo: Stony Pavement is crossed by crews who know it and avoided by everyone else. Water stations do not exist out here; the Routehead has the last one.

The Darkening Run.name: The Darkening Run
The Darkening Run.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Darkening blue, with the veining of broken swell spread thinly over it and the colour going heavier southward. The Verdant Coast closes this water on its northern and western sides. Southward the swell lengthens as the colour goes, and the crests break less often for it. Cloud is almost nothing. Where the veining crosses a trough it holds together, and where it crosses a crest it is pulled apart. Light comes down hard and is absorbed rather than returned. Fliers leaving the land here lose their last surface reference within the span of this water.
The Darkening Run.hiddenInfo: Over The Darkening Run the wind is the only fixed thing, and it changes. Wildlife under the surface is possible and rarely seen; bandits do not work water this open.

The Settled Blue.name: The Settled Blue
The Settled Blue.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Cloudless sky over water that runs a settled mid-blue, veined with white where the swell has turned over. The veining lies in loose loops rather than lines and drifts slowly out of shape. The green shoreline of the Verdant Coast closes the northern edge of the frame. The surface is busy but not rough. Light falls hard on the surface and is mostly taken in, leaving the white to carry what brightness there is. Heat coming off it makes the lower air unsteady through the day, and fliers wanting a smooth run take height early and hold it across.
The Settled Blue.hiddenInfo: The Settled Blue is transit air over deep water, crossed rather than visited. Ships bound for the Orbital Gate Station pass far above; nothing else uses this sky.

Frontier Edge.name: Frontier Edge
Frontier Edge.basicInfo: [Lv 10-16 · Low] Half made ground and half open desert: modules and old stone walling hold the eastern side, while bare sand runs west toward Ashen Coast with nothing on it. The Frontier Care House keeps the largest roof here, reinforced glass set into a patched alien-metal frame, rooftop collectors angled across the whole span. A water station stands at the corner of its yard with a queue line painted onto the dirt. Wind moves dust through all of it and nobody sweeps twice. The walling is old stone to knee height and salvaged plate above, and the lanes between are floored in packed dirt that powders underfoot. Part of Dustfall.
Frontier Edge.hiddenInfo: The Frontier Care House is rationing in front of the people it rations. Consumables are the shortage, not skill, and the staff are making explicit decisions about limited medicine while the Corsair shipment stays missing. Eyla Marris works the wards while living inside the Black Pennant's compound, and Maela Drin covers what the Last Line Company can spare; neither arrangement is written down and both would collapse under a hard look. Patients keep arriving with restraint damage they have not explained and pursuers behind them, forcing the house's oldest conflict, gang loyalty against patient protection, into the treatment rooms. Treating someone does not oblige the staff to surrender them, and refusing carries costs the building cannot absorb. Stock will run out before any replacement lands, and the first refusal that becomes a standoff at the door will decide what the house is.

The Walkway Warrens.name: The Walkway Warrens
The Walkway Warrens.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Built ground almost wall to wall, and none of it planned — cargo modules stacked into blocks, alien-metal sheeting lapped over old stone, reinforced glass salvaged in whatever sizes came to hand. Rooftop walkways cross between the stacks, so most movement happens a level above the lanes. Patched environmental towers stand clear of the roofline with ducting strapped on in later layers. The lanes below run narrow and shaded, floored in swept dirt with offcut plate laid where the dirt turns to dust. Sound comes down from overhead rather than along, footfall carrying on the walkway decking. Part of Dustfall.
The Walkway Warrens.hiddenInfo: The Walkway Warrens is service ground for Dustfall, crossed daily and rarely mentioned. Collectors, guy lines and dust; the beacon line is close.

Refit Strip.name: Refit Strip
Refit Strip.basicInfo: [Lv 3-77 · Moderate] Repair work sets the character of this ground. Refit Row runs gantries and open bays along the main lane, hulls and drives stripped down in daylight under salvage frames bolted to whatever would hold them, tool chatter carrying a long way in dry air. The Long Shot keeps a doorway on the same stretch, dark and cool behind a heavy curtain hung against the dust. Bay floors are plate laid over levelled sand, stained through with old fluid and gritted for footing. Landing shelves sit close to the bays so nothing has to be dragged far. Walkers cut between bays rather than along the lane, which is usually occupied. Part of Dustfall.
Refit Strip.hiddenInfo: Sennra Sol has refused to recognise the warrant Ravik Rusk carries, on the ground that Dravon authority alone backs it, and Rusk has not yet tested how far the town would defend that refusal; everyone in the Long Shot can see the confrontation coming and nobody has scheduled it. Down the lane, Refit Row is where a supply theft becomes a political fact. Sura Venn has pulled a tracker that reports to somebody other than Dravon, meaning a second party has learned the same control architecture, and Korrik Caelthorn may have bought a component matching the missing Corsair manifest without knowing it. Halvora Orvantis audits everything Iven Torris brings in; Kaedra Vossan's Jackals may be auctioning stolen parts in good faith. The job board fills with work that is really about the shipment, and who volunteers unpaid is noted as carefully as who demands payment first.

The Sand Scatter.name: The Sand Scatter
The Sand Scatter.basicInfo: [Lv 3-23 · Low] Sand holds nearly two-thirds of this cell, open and wind-combed, with only a scatter of structure standing in it. Grit and Supply is the one that matters: a broad-fronted store of stacked modules and old stone, its awning weighted against the wind, water and parts sold across the same counter. A few worn flight markers lean out of the sand in a rough line eastward. The light is hard and shadowless, and the ground between buildings is walked rather than surfaced. Loose sand drifts against the windward walls and is shovelled back into ridges that last until the next blow. Fliers come down wherever the crust holds, which is most of the open ground. Part of Dustfall.
The Sand Scatter.hiddenInfo: Veyra Corsair reported the Corsair shipment missing and may be carrying a Corsair-side contract complication she has described to nobody in Dustfall. One manifest held ammunition, medical stock, spare parts and Lunar Gate components together, so the Gate Component Cage is the part of Grit and Supply that matters most: if the failed gate part is not locally replaceable, the settlement's argument moves from prices to isolation within days. Hidden humanitarian cargo, counterfeit goods, Corsair route politics and equipment bound for outer Quilrath buyers all move through the same rear bay, and Veyra prefers not to know which is which until a ledger entry forces her. Dravon inspection pressure reaches her through intermediaries, and the next one is due.

The Last Stacks.name: The Last Stacks
The Last Stacks.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Low stacked housing thins westward into open sand, the last modules standing alone with guy lines pegged into the crust. Rooftop collectors are fitted to nearly every roof that has one, all angled the same way, and a pair of environmental towers show patching in three different metals. Past the last of it the ground runs bare toward Ashen Coast. Salt and dust both reach this far, and the glare coming off the sand is hard enough to squint through most of the day. Between the stacks the ground is loose and unmade, with boards laid across the softest stretches. Part of Dustfall.
The Last Stacks.hiddenInfo: The Last Stacks is the built edge of Dustfall: the same fabric as the city, thinner, and no authored location stands on it. No one governs it, and the crews who live here defend it.

The Cluster Gaps.name: The Cluster Gaps
The Cluster Gaps.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] More sand than structure here, the built ground broken into separate clusters with wide dusty gaps between them. Each cluster does the same things: modules stacked around a swept yard, a collector array on the roofs, a shaded strip where the walls come close enough together to hold shade at midday. Rooftop walkways connect what they can and stop where they cannot. Tracks between clusters are worn into the crust rather than made, and fliers use the roofs as landing ground by habit. The gaps carry nothing but wind and blown grit, and voices from one cluster do not reach the next. Part of Dustfall.
The Cluster Gaps.hiddenInfo: Nothing on The Cluster Gaps is a destination; travel here arrives at the nearest named site of Dustfall. No one governs it, and the crews who live here defend it.

Dustfall Core.name: Dustfall Core
Dustfall Core.basicInfo: [Lv 2-15 · Moderate] This is Dustfall's own centre of gravity, and it looks like everything else here: cargo modules and old stone crowded around open ground, advanced machinery running in the middle of hand-built repair, dust over all of it. Water stations sit where the lanes meet, fed down from the collectors crowding the roofs above. Open landing shelves take flight traffic straight into the built ground. The open ground is packed hard by use and swept in patches, plate laid where traffic is heaviest and bare dirt everywhere else. Gate light and strip lighting pick out the lane mouths once the daylight goes. Part of Dustfall.
Dustfall Core.hiddenInfo: The strip is where the supply failure becomes an argument. One Corsair shipment of Contair equipment has not arrived, so ammunition, medical stock, spare parts and Lunar Gate components are short at once, and prices at the water station and the job rail are already moving. Households accuse each other of hoarding and of feeding undeclared arrivals, and shutting the gate for a while is being said aloud in the meal yard before anyone has carried it to the Long Shot's dispute table. Draxen Sol organises a town-wide response without holding any office; Kell Ardan is wherever he should not be; Maressa Oryn keeps her cleaning storefront immaculate and takes contract work elsewhere. If the shortage lasts through the next tenday, households and crews will have to authorise incident delegates, and nobody has agreed what such a mandate may touch.

The Stacked Rows.name: The Stacked Rows
The Stacked Rows.basicInfo: [Lv 4-60 · Moderate] Homes stacked three and four modules deep make up the Dustfall Residential Rows across this ground, each stack patched in a different metal and shaded by whatever came to hand — panel, canvas, salvaged plate. Rooftop walkways run the length of the rows and carry most of the daily traffic, leaving the lanes below to deliveries. Collectors crowd every roof not being walked on. Doorways stay curtained against the dust, and the light between stacks falls sharp and narrow. The walkway decking is salvaged grating and plank laid over the module edges, springy in places and bolted hard in others. Part of Dustfall.
The Stacked Rows.hiddenInfo: The Residential Rows are what the perimeter is defending, and several of the organisations sheltering here are recruiting here. In Old Banner Hall the Black Pennant records commitments that are hard to withdraw from, and a young survivor asking to leave is testing whether Rhex Vaereth sees betrayal faster than Selka Vaereth sees the risk of recreating Dravon control; Torven Vaereth and Kalen Dorr are watching which way it breaks. Messa Taar's informal food and shelter agreement with the Nhalor household keeps the Iron Jackals' protection debts falling due on people who cannot pay. Ovar Kethrin's missing-person records in the Last Names Room contradict identity files held elsewhere in Dustfall. Sev Marrik has a Korrvane tournament invitation that Darven reads as redemption and Mareva reads as danger, and the reply cannot wait past the season.

The Salvage Yards.name: The Salvage Yards
The Salvage Yards.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Workyards and storage take this ground, less lived in than the rows further west: salvage gantries standing over cleared bays, containers ranked in lines, machinery under canvas between uses. Strip lighting runs along the gantry legs and stays lit through the night. The bays are floored in levelled grit with plate set under the gantry feet, and the container lines leave straight shaded lanes between them. The made ground gives out eastward into Dust Barrens with only beacon lines and worn flight markers to say where the settlement stops. Part of Dustfall.
The Salvage Yards.hiddenInfo: The Salvage Yards carries Dustfall's ordinary life outward without any place of its own. No one governs it, and the crews who live here defend it.

The Colour Change.name: The Colour Change
The Colour Change.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Just north and west of where the sea pales into the Radiant Strait, the water holds a mid-blue with white veining across it and a moderate swell running through. The change of colour toward the channel is visible along the eastern and southern edges. The veining lies across the swell rather than along it and breaks up where the water runs paler. Light is strong. The sky is open and the light falls steeply, so the paler channel colour reads brighter from height than from low down. Fliers use that boundary as the last usable mark before the crossing proper begins.
The Colour Change.hiddenInfo: The colour of The Colour Change says nothing about what lies beneath, and nothing here will catch a tired flier. Weather arrives from the open quarter with little warning and no shelter.

The Beacon Line.name: The Beacon Line
The Beacon Line.basicInfo: [Lv 5-56 · High] Edge ground, and the edge is a line rather than a barrier — the Dustfall Perimeter crosses this cell as beacons and worn flight markers driven into the sand, some leaning, all kept up by whoever passes them. Hard daylight, steady wind, dust in every seam. A handful of low modules with clear sightlines serve the volunteer patrols working outward from them, and beyond those the desert runs south toward Ashen Coast with nothing built on it. The ground between beacons is open crust, walkable in any direction and marked only by the tracks already crossing it. Part of Dustfall.
The Beacon Line.hiddenInfo: Draxen Sol has confirmed that the missing Corsair shipment was taken by an organised interception, not lost to route conditions, so the question on the perimeter has changed from recovery to who supplied the timing. Tavra Korrin recently walked the Last Line Company off an escort after learning the client meant to raid refugee housing; the client has since hired the Claimants camped at the North Routehead, and the raid Tavra refused is still being planned. Brask Hollan and Joric Pell keep the barracks on shorter rotations than the contract pays for. Bent Halo crews cross the line on departures under an understanding nobody has written down, and Iven Torris keeps adding Dravon hardware to the Captured Equipment Rack from checkpoint shells he should leave alone. The perimeter works by observation and how fast volunteers can be raised; the night the raid moves, that speed will be measured.

The Outer Scatter.name: The Outer Scatter
The Outer Scatter.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Scattered structure across a great deal of open sand: module blocks standing in twos and threes with wind-scoured gaps between them, and no through lane that crosses the whole cell. Collectors sit on every roof, and one patched environmental tower carries higher than anything near it. Tracks cross the crust in several directions and none of them are surfaced. The blocks sit on levelled pads with their doorways turned out of the prevailing wind, and sand piles against the other walls until somebody clears it. Light falls flat and the horizon stays visible from ground level. Part of Dustfall.
The Outer Scatter.hiddenInfo: The Outer Scatter is Dustfall ground by every rule that matters and by no landmark anyone would name. No one governs it, and the crews who live here defend it.

The Enclosed Dark.name: The Enclosed Dark
The Enclosed Dark.basicInfo: [Transit · Moderate] Enclosed on its northern and western sides by the Ashen Coast, this water runs mid-blue with white broken across it, lighter in tone than the sea it opens into eastward. The rock rises in dark broken steps along both enclosed edges and shows no soft ground anywhere along them. Swell comes in short and confused where it rebounds off the rock. The air above the coast is hotter and rougher than the air over the water, so fliers hold to the seaward side of the frame. Light reaches into this water more easily than into the darker sea eastward and comes back with the white carrying most of it.
The Enclosed Dark.hiddenInfo: Open water with no landing under The Enclosed Dark: a flier who loses a heading here has only the sun to correct it. Weather arrives from the open quarter with little warning and no shelter.

The Open Road.name: The Open Road
The Open Road.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Worked ground begins in rock country below the grey heights of Silver Peaks, the route surface cut into the slope and shored where the ground would not hold it. Cold air comes down off the peaks early in the day. Loose stone gathers along the lower shoulder. The surfacing is bound stone laid thin over cut rock, the shoring showing as squared blockwork wherever the slope has been taken out from under it. Water off the heights crosses the line in shallow scours. Freight moving through is going somewhere else, and the country either side of the cut is steep enough to discourage leaving it.
The Open Road.hiddenInfo: The worked line through The Open Road belongs to the North Route toward Dustfall: made, patched, unmaintained. Bent Halo crews, Claimant hunters and Last Line escorts all move here; Dravon and Ignivex claim it and neither holds it.

Thinned Canopy.name: Thinned Canopy
Thinned Canopy.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Thinned forest gives way here to worked ground and hard surfaces, the canopy standing only in patches between cleared lots and made-up tracks. The pale growth that lights the rest of this forest survives in the shaded margins and nowhere else, so dusk comes down darker than it does further south. Outcrop Maze stands close enough east that its lights carry over the remaining trees, and a flier crossing the cell has open sightlines most of the way. Verdant Coast lies north and west, near enough that salt reaches the cleared lots on a steady wind. The made tracks are surfaced coarse and cambered, so they stay usable where the turned ground between them does not.
Thinned Canopy.hiddenInfo: Cover at Thinned Canopy is total below the canopy and useless above it. The canopy gives no landing; the clearings decide the route.

Gritfall Ridges.name: Gritfall Ridges
Gritfall Ridges.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Unsnowed ridges of dark rock stand in close ranks here, crests bare and flanks streaked with grit that has slid into every gully. Nothing softens the outline. Wind comes through the saddles in steady pushes and drops ash-fine dust into the lee of each spur. The rock is fractured into blocks that ring under a boot and slide where grit has worked beneath them. Sound carries between the ridges and dies in the gullies. Footing on the spines is sound where the stone is unbroken and treacherous where weather has loosened it, so height is gained by reading which shoulder holds.
Gritfall Ridges.hiddenInfo: Nothing grows at Gritfall Ridges; the ground takes heat in and gives it back after dark. Cover here shelters danger as readily as travellers; Starian bandits use it, given story evidence.

The Bare Shoulders.name: The Bare Shoulders
The Bare Shoulders.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Ridge country without snow: grey-dark stone rising in blunt shoulders, seamed with fracture lines and holding almost no soil. Loose scree collects at the foot of every face and shifts underfoot. Light comes off the rock flat and colourless, and heat builds in the sheltered hollows through the middle of the day. The fracture seams take a boot whole and are packed with grit that gives no warning of how deep they run. Ways through follow the low saddles rather than the crests, and the choice of saddle matters more than the effort spent climbing.
The Bare Shoulders.hiddenInfo: Updraughts along The Bare Shoulders are strong enough to matter and nowhere near reliable. The snowline decides where anything can stop.

The Worked Clearing.name: The Worked Clearing
The Worked Clearing.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Cleared ground takes as much of this cell as the trees do, in worked lots and made surfaces laid out where the canopy has been cut back. The forest that remains stands in dense blocks with rock breaking through at their edges. Solvraxis Outskirts lies south and The Worked Clearing east, and traffic through here is going to one or the other. Glowing growth persists in the deeper stands and is thin to absent over the open ground. Verdant Coast lies west past the last of the worked lots, close enough that the wind off it carries through the open ground. Rock at the edges of the stands stands proud in low steps that the tracks go round rather than over. Part of Solvraxis.
The Worked Clearing.hiddenInfo: The Worked Clearing is Solvraxis ground by every rule that matters and by no landmark anyone would name. Transit Rings and forest paths meet on this ground.

Castro Heights.name: Castro Heights
Castro Heights.basicInfo: [Lv 3-91 · Low] White stone dominates, cut in broad faces and paired with dark star-glass that gives back the silver-blue light of the avenues. Castro Citadel stands over this part of Solvraxis on a raised terrace with reflective pools set at its foot, so the structure appears twice. The open space is deliberate: plazas run wide and building never crowds a walkway. The paving is pale and close-jointed, swept clean, its joints running unbroken from one plaza into the next. Sound carries a long way and comes back softened, and there is no signage clutter to read, only lighting laid along the routes. Part of Solvraxis.
Castro Heights.hiddenInfo: The hub's calm is genuine and it is also an export: Solvraxis sells education, verification and trust to cities that cannot generate their own, and every polished walk is part of the argument. The most consequential room here is the smallest. The Veyth Notary belongs to a faded minor House with no district and no civic seat, and its family archive is said to hold a contract a wealthy family would pay heavily to bury; which family, what it proves, how old it is and who else knows are all unanswered, and Caevin Veyth and his relatives are notaries rather than schemers. Somebody has begun asking the Veyths for an appraisal, and the request must be refused or answered before the season's end.

The Archive Quarter.name: The Archive Quarter
The Archive Quarter.basicInfo: [Lv 3-17 · Low] Quieter ground, half of it public garden and open lawn, with pale terraces standing in loose groups instead of continuous frontage. Ravello Archive House carries the weight of it, dark star-glass over white stone, and blue-violet light comes up along the paths as the avenues dim. The paths are cut stone laid flush into turf, edged rather than kerbed, bending around planting instead of through it. The loudest thing on this ground is water moving in the shallow pools. Luminous Forest is left standing on three sides. Part of Solvraxis.
The Archive Quarter.hiddenInfo: Ravello's position is that peace depends on accurate memory, which makes an archive a civic power, and that power is contested quietly. Families ask for lines to be removed, records turn up altered, and Maereth Ravello answers every question with a document and every document with a caution while Eloria Ravello argues permanently that access rather than preservation is what memory is for. Nessa Ravello keeps finding material the catalogue says does not exist, and Maereth keeps declining to notice how often the difficult requests reach her desk. Below the public floors the Sealed Record Vaults hold old house agreements nobody will itemise; what was altered, who sealed it and who may open it go unanswered. A request now on the benches names a line that Nessa found and the catalogue denies, and Maereth will have to notice it or refuse it in writing.

The Ropy Flows.name: The Ropy Flows
The Ropy Flows.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Old flows lie in overlapping sheets across this ground, their surfaces ropy and weathered to grey where the black has been bleached out of them. Ash fills the low seams. Nothing takes root on any of it. Each sheet ends in a low broken lip that has to be climbed or walked around, and those lips carry the sharpest rock on the ground. Sound travels flatly and the wind is the only thing making any.
The Ropy Flows.hiddenInfo: The fissures and tubes of The Ropy Flows give real shade and real drops, and cut across any line of travel. Ignivex patrols and Dravon incursions both cross this ground and neither holds it.

The Route Approach.name: The Route Approach
The Route Approach.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Hard grey rock lies in low broken tables with ash collected between them, close enough to the worked country eastward that traffic has left its mark. Wheel scars and boot-polish show on the stone where crossings repeatedly make for The North Route. Light glares off the pale surfaces. The tables stand a step or two above the ash between them, their edges crumbled where weight has gone over them again and again. Nothing on this ground blocks a line of sight for long. The Outer Yards stands beyond the northern edge, and the approaches that way carry more movement than the open waste behind.
The Route Approach.hiddenInfo: The route at The Route Approach is a line rather than a road, and it is shared by everyone who will not use the gates. Skirmishes between the competing claims keep regular patrol off the line.

The Dust Turn.name: The Dust Turn
The Dust Turn.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Bends in the worked ground take the route around a shoulder of grey rock here, the surface wide enough for freight and rutted where heavy loads have worked it over. Pale stone stands close on the inside of the turn. Dust hangs in the air a long while after anything passes. The ruts run deep and hold fine grey powder that lifts at a touch, while the outer shoulder is loose stone tipped over the edge of the bend. The Outer Yards lies beyond the northern rise, and the open waste west and south is where crews go to be off the line.
The Dust Turn.hiddenInfo: The Dust Turn is where a checkpoint might stand tomorrow and did not yesterday. Approaching Quilrath the danger turns to paperwork; leaving it the danger turns to thirst.

The Academy Sprawl.name: The Academy Sprawl
The Academy Sprawl.basicInfo: [Lv 2-69 · Low] Hillside housing steps down through here in white terraces, reflective pools set at the turns where the ground levels off. Valcoro Academy holds the high side, the Bellovari Market District and Orvessa Welfare District the lower, all of it under the same silver-blue lighting rather than signage or colour. Gardens run between the Solvraxis Residential Wards and greenery pushes close against the southern edge. Stairs between terraces are shallow and broad, worked from the same white stone as the walls, so the fall of the hillside is taken gradually. Movement is unhurried and mostly at ground level, the air still enough that the pools hold a flat reflection. Part of Solvraxis.
The Academy Sprawl.hiddenInfo: Marcon Valcoro assigned Marea Valcoro her first student group a full year early, on purpose; she has not worked out why and he has not said, and the group's first assessment sits on the timetable Tavian Valcoro is perpetually one crisis behind. Down the hill, Darian Bellovari's Cargo-Check Station is where the weapon-free law meets imported goods as routine, so a shipment problem becomes a social embarrassment long before it is a civic matter. House Orvessa is the city's early warning: Jovian, Renzo and Amara Orvessa see arriving families' problems before anyone else, and the reserve count now being taken will show whether the shelters are as full as the running joke pretends. On Silverwell Terrace, families who remember Solvraxis before Castro dominance settled keep circling the question the core does not ask aloud: whether peace this dependable depends too much on one man.

The Stream Channels.name: The Stream Channels
The Stream Channels.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Streams run through this cell in several channels, cutting the forest floor into damp strips between rises of firmer ground. The canopy is close overhead with cleared corridors pushed through it where the tracks run. The Stream Channels stands west and The Pale Root Floor north, and the made routes here serve both. Glowing growth follows the water closely, marking out the channels after dark better than daylight does. Damp strips between the channels are soft and hold a print; the rises between them are firm and carry the made routes.
The Stream Channels.hiddenInfo: The Stream Channels is Luminous Forest country: close cover, small watercourses and quiet that carries sound a long way. The forest hides a camp well and a fire badly.

Hummock Waste.name: Hummock Waste
Hummock Waste.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Dull black rock, hummocked and cracked, fills this ground between the worked corridor eastward and the rising volcanic country on the other sides. Ash lies in the cracks and blows out of them in gusts. The cracks are narrow, deep and irregular, and they take a boot toe often enough to slow a crossing. Heat off the surface is steady from morning on. The hummocks are low, close-set and rounded, so a walker steps up and down continually without gaining anything by it. Little on this ground stands high enough to break a sightline.
Hummock Waste.hiddenInfo: The route at Hummock Waste is a line rather than a road, and it is shared by everyone who will not use the gates. Approaching Quilrath the danger turns to paperwork; leaving it the danger turns to thirst.

Skyhook Clearing.name: Skyhook Clearing
Skyhook Clearing.basicInfo: [Lv 4-28 · Moderate] Green ground takes over from built ground across most of this cell, cropped and cut by service roads rather than left wild, with Luminous Forest standing close on three sides. The Skyhook Docks occupy the cleared middle — tall smart-cable towers, open cargo aprons, loads travelling in slow arcs between them — and the Helvyra Lunar Gate Hub sits behind its own plating and hard-standing beyond. Amber work lighting runs the aprons after dusk. The service roads are laid in rolled grit that darkens where it is watered against dust, and the aprons take a load set down anywhere on them. Part of Helvyra.
Skyhook Clearing.hiddenInfo: Petch Immar refuses to certify a hook he would not stand under, and his last refusal has not been overruled despite the schedule pressure behind it. A recent rigging failure was not what the incident report describes: the discrepancy sits between the Counterweight House's load calculation and what was actually lifted, and cargo has been diverted mid-transfer on the cable runs at least once, which needs cooperation at both ends. At the Helvyra Lunar Gate Hub, Ondrel Vask's manifest archive has a gap: a traveller whose papers passed every Compact check and whom nobody at either end remembers. He has not reported it, because reporting hands the matter to the Contair inspection post, and the last inspection found an irregularity that was Contair's own fault. The next inspection cycle will ask him what he found.

Roadcut Forest.name: Roadcut Forest
Roadcut Forest.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Full canopy covers this cell except where roads have been cut through it, and those run wide toward Windbreak Edgeeast and The Loose Floor with cleared margins either side. Beneath the trees the ground is broken and damp, with streams in the low lines. Traffic keeps to the made routes. The glowing growth is strong in the interior and cut back along the roads, so from above at night the cleared lines show as dark channels through lit forest. The road margins are cleared to a consistent width and kept that way, which makes them legible from above as straight lines in ground that has none.
Roadcut Forest.hiddenInfo: Nothing is built at Roadcut Forest; the forest here is a thing cities lean on rather than a place they own. Foraging is possible for those who know the growth; most do not.

The Redgrit Stretch.name: The Redgrit Stretch
The Redgrit Stretch.basicInfo: [Transit · High] Reddish grit lies over the rock along this arm of the corridor, and the worked line shows in the compaction underfoot rather than in any surfacing. Low scrub starts to appear at the edges. The scrub is woody, knee-high and spaced too widely to screen anything, growing out of the disturbed ground rather than the flat. Heat rises off the ground through the afternoon and holds there. The compacted line runs a few shades darker than the loose grit beside it and reads more clearly from above than from on it. Nothing beside the line stands tall enough to shade any part of it.
The Redgrit Stretch.hiddenInfo: Crews cross The Redgrit Stretch by timing and route variation; nobody holds it and no patrol is dependable. Skirmishes between the competing claims keep regular patrol off the line.

The Forest Gate.name: The Forest Gate
The Forest Gate.basicInfo: [Lv 3-9 · Low] Forest and ridge make up most of this ground, mixed green over rising rock with bare sandy soil where the slope has worn through. Solvraxis shows in one corner only: the westernmost pale stone and dark glass of the city, standing where the trees stop, with the Lunar Gate District laid out there across level plates. Those plates are set flush with the ground and kept clear to their edges, and the silver-blue lighting ends at the treeline as though cut. The approach from the forest side is uphill and unmade, root-crossed and loose underfoot, with birdless quiet under the canopy. A flier has a clear line down onto that open ground with nothing in the way. Part of Solvraxis.
The Forest Gate.hiddenInfo: Solvraxis connects to Relstaris, Korrvane and Helvyra and no more, a standing choice about what the city wants arriving, and the Lunar Gate District's work is largely social: the weapons law is taught as civic trust before anyone has a chance to test it, and newcomers are pointed to the Public Transit Rings rather than sent into unfamiliar aerial lanes. Restricted Transit Control is the quiet end of the operation, where an arrival needing Castro or Valcoro representation is handled and where Dravon pressure at the city edge is absorbed before it becomes visible; what makes a transit restricted and who authorises it are not posted. Calessa Orvessa's reception desk pairs with the Lunar Gate Guesthouse, so the same family meets a visitor at both ends. One restricted transit is pending now, and its handling sets a precedent the Citadel has avoided writing down.

The Corelight Approach.name: The Corelight Approach
The Corelight Approach.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Green closes over most of this ground, dense at head height and denser below, with rock outcrops breaking the slope where it steepens southward. Water collects in the hollows and drains slowly. Academy Quarter lies south and Relstaris — Corelight Crown east, and the tracks crossing the cell are worn deep by traffic between them. The pale growth is strong here, running up trunks and over stone in broad patches. The slope steepens toward the south and the outcrops grow more frequent with it, so the tracks worn deepest are the ones that traverse rather than climb. Undergrowth stands at head height for long stretches and closes the sightlines to a few paces. Part of Relstaris.
The Corelight Approach.hiddenInfo: The Corelight Approach carries Relstaris's ordinary life outward without any place of its own. Corelight reaches it thinly and the city's rules reach it fully.

The Southward Gradient.name: The Southward Gradient
The Southward Gradient.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] Ground here falls southward in a long shallow gradient toward The Barge Terracewest, and the tracks take it directly rather than traversing. Forest covers about half the cell in blocks with worked and cleared ground between them. Streams cross the routes in several places and run high after weather. The glowing growth holds to the blocks of standing timber, and the cleared strips between them stay dark. The Barge Terracewest lies at the foot of the gradient, and the roads that serve it draw everything in the cell toward one end. The worked and cleared ground between the forest blocks is level and open and takes flight traffic without difficulty.
The Southward Gradient.hiddenInfo: The tracks through The Southward Gradient are kept open by use and would close within a season without it. The canopy gives no landing; the clearings decide the route.

The Barge Watch.name: The Barge Watch
The Barge Watch.basicInfo: [Transit · Low] A wide band of water runs through the eastern part of the frame, the forest standing back from it on firmer ground with worked strips laid out between the two. The canopy is moderate and broken by tracks running down toward The Barge Terrace. Barge traffic is visible on the water from the higher ground. Glow off the growth under the trees counts for little here beside the working lights along the bank. The Longreach lies east beyond the water, worked and open on that side. Ground between the forest and the bank is laid out in strips that drain toward the water and stay firm to walk on.
The Barge Watch.hiddenInfo: The Barge Watch is walkable, crossable on foot in a day and easier from the air, where the canopy reads as one surface. Wildlife is the ordinary hazard; Starian bandits the less ordinary one, and both need story evidence.
